name: Stewie
description:
Meet Stewie, a sweet, affectionate 2 year old Chihuahua. He may be small but Stewie has plenty of personality! When meeting new people Stewie can be quite reserved, however once he knows you you’ll have a lap dog for life. He’s such a cuddle bug and loves nothing more than chilling on you and accepting all the gentle fusses you can give, especially a little chest rub. Stewie’s favourite place is anywhere with his favourite people and his dream day would be a short potter in the morning around the local park before enjoying cuddles on your lap all afternoon!

Stewie will need to live in an adult-only home with adopters who can respect his boundaries and provide him with plenty of love. As he is unphased by traffic, Stewie would be able to live in a city or town environment, given his space was respected when out and about. Stewie would prefer to be the only pet in the home and will need calm, respectful introductions to other dogs on walks to ensure he feels as safe and relaxed as possible. In the home, Stewie would benefit from having a quiet area to enjoy his meals undisturbed and will need adopters willing to work on his confidence around handling and be prepared to muzzle train him for vet visits.

name: Winnie
description:
Winnie is rather sensitive so looking for a quiet home where any children are teenaged and above, and she could potentially live with a well-matched dog. She is house trained but doesn't particularly enjoy being left alone for more than an hour or two.

Lovely Winnie is an eight year old crossbreed looking for a quiet home. She's toy mad and seems to love every game her foster family comes up with, and can sometimes get quite vocal and rowdy for an older girl! We don't know anything about Winnie's past but she seems very sensitive and worried in new situations or with new people. She is naturally curious but likes time to figure things out for herself. Winnie does seem to enjoy the company of other dogs and is keen to introduce herself politely and we'd happily rehome her with a suitable friend she can enjoy long walks with. A home away from busy roads and with quiet walking areas would be ideal for this lovely girl.

name: Tallulah
description:
Meet Tallulah, an 8-year-old Chihuahua also known as Tutu. Tutu is looking for adopters who will put in the time to help her build her confidence, as she is the most worried of her siblings. She will need that extra bit of time for her to adjust and feel comfortable in her new environment, so her adopters should be patient with her. She could live with secondary-aged children. Tutu is currently kennel-sharing with some of her sisters and could be rehomed with one of them. However, she would not be suitable to go home with any other pets in the home.

Tutu is a very sweet Chihuahua who loves all the home comforts and spending time with her siblings. She would love patient, kind and caring adopters who can help her settle back into home life and shower her with all the love she deserves. She absolutely loves toys and playing with them. Once she gets to know you, her sweet, affectionate side comes out. Tutu would make a terrific companion!

name: Peggy
description:
Meet Peggy, a 7.5-year-old Chihuahua. She is currently kennel-sharing with two of her sisters. Peggy could be rehomed with one of her siblings; however, she would not be able to be rehomed with any other pets in the home. She could live with secondary-aged children. Peggy's adopters should be patient with her as she adjusts to living in a home again.

Peggy is a lovely lady who has stolen the hearts of our staff. She was quite nervous when she first came in but has come out of her shell massively. She enjoys her walks, as well as having cuddle time with her handlers. She likes to explore and find any lost or forgotten treats on the floor! Her adopters should be happy for her to have her independent moments as well as lots of fuss and cuddles.

name: Rupert
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I am fine with cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning to walk on a lead and harness, but it's still very new for me.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I will be neutered before finding my forever home.

21-09-26 Rupert has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He is the sweetest boy who is understandably a little worried and overwhelmed to find himself here. He has recently moved into foster with a member of staff and is loving learning all about home life for the very first time. He is settling in really well and is already enjoying discovering all the lovely things that come with being in a home.

He is a lovely boy but can be a little worried and overwhelmed at the moment, which is understandable. He can be spooked by loud noises and will need love and TLC as he settles into his new life. Once Rupert gets to know you he absolutely loves fuss and cuddles and we think he is going to adore being someone's special boy. He is very people focused and so can show signs of separation anxiety and become quite clingy. His adopters will need to understand this and be prepared to work with him gently, building up the time he is left alone very gradually so that he can learn that being apart from his family is nothing to worry about.

Because Rupert is so people focused, we would consider homing him as an only dog in the right circumstances, with adopters who have plenty of time to spend with him. He does love the company of other dogs though, and could happily share his home with another kind resident dog. He is also fine with cats, so could potentially live with a dog savvy cat. We would consider homing him with dog savvy teenagers aged 13+.

Rupert has never lived in a home before moving into foster, so there is still lots for him to learn. His adopters will need to be kind and patient as he continues to learn about home life and house training. He is also new to walking on a lead and harness and will need plenty more practice as his confidence grows.

Rupert is such a loving and affectionate boy who is already showing us just how much he enjoys being part of a family. We hope to find him a wonderful home where he can continue to blossom, receive all the love and attention he adores, and become someone's very special boy.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Halo
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and will enjoy going on adventures with my new family!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before finding my forever home.

21-09-26 Halo has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a happy, cheeky girl who already enjoys fuss and attention and is a lovely girl to spend time with. She has a fun personality and we are sure she will bring lots of joy to her new family.

Halo will be looking for a loving home with adopters who have plenty of time to spend with her and understand that she will still need time to settle in and adjust to all the changes in her life. She is confident enough that she could be homed as an only dog, although she does get along well with other dogs and would be happy to share her home with another kind dog. We would consider homing her with dog savvy teenagers 13+.

Halo absolutely loves her toys and can be a little possessive of them around other dogss. If she is homed with another dog, her adopters will need to be understanding of this and able to manage her toy guarding carefully and sensibly to make sure both dogs are happ. This may mean that toys can only be given when they are supervised, or that Halo and her canine companion have separate playtimes with their favourite toys.

Halo has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training. She can already walk well on a lead and we think she will love heading out for walks and adventures with her new family.

Halo is a bright, happy girl with lots of personality, and we hope her new family will give her the time, guidance and love she needs to settle into her new life and flourish.

Halo has been given the Gift of Life by Rebecca Matthewman

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Toast
description:
I would like a quiet, adult-only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me feel safe. I live with a cat in my foster home.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in (6ft+)

I enjoy my walks but hate putting my harness on. I need more practice. Go slow please

I will need to learn about house training and practice lead walking

Toast is a delicate little girl who came to us from a breeder and has been slowly finding her confidence in the world. She has been in foster since April and has come a long way, although she is not your average ex-breeder and still has some very specific challenges that her future family will need to understand.

Toast remains extremely nervous about being touched and will avoid handling wherever possible. She can become overwhelmed if she feels pressured, so fitting her harness is still very much a case of careful timing and patience, as she will try to hide if given the opportunity. Her foster mummy has found that this can be tricky, and her new family will need to be experienced and prepared to work within her limits rather than forcing interaction.

Interestingly, once Toast is out on a walk, she absolutely loves it! She walks happily and enjoys saying hello to other dogs, often approaching them with a lovely waggy tail. She has also become much more confident when visiting friends, happily running around with other dogs and enjoying herself. This is a wonderful contrast to how nervous she can be when it comes to being handled.

Toast has also been to the groomers a couple of times and has tolerated this quite happily. She has even allowed her foster mummy to pick her up and cuddle her afterwards, which shows that she is capable of accepting handling in certain situations when she feels comfortable and secure.

Toast is currently living with a cat in her foster home and can live with a dog-savvy cat who respects her space.

She will need a quiet, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand nervous ex-breeding dogs and can support her without expectation or pressure. A calm, predictable environment will be essential for her ongoing confidence building. Her future family will need to accept that Toast may never become a cuddly or lap dog. She is a little character who likes to do her own thing, and her happiness and confidence will be far more important than expecting her to enjoy affection.

Toast is still learning about house training, and seems to be clean in the home when her foster mummy is around but can have a few accidents when she is left alone. Her new family will need to continue her toilet training patiently as she settles into her new routine.

She will need a kind, confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and provide reassurance as she adjusts to home life. Having other dogs around clearly brings Toast confidence, and she enjoys their company when out and about and when visiting friends.

Toast arrived with a low-grade luxating patella on her left side, which does not currently cause her any problems, although a disclaimer will need to be signed on adoption. She has also been treated for mucky ears, right-sided otitis, hot spots and dermatitis. She requires Apoquel twice daily for allergies that cause her to itch, and her general health will need to continue to be monitored in her new home.

Behind her nervousness is a gorgeous, mischievous and very cheeky little dog with a huge personality. Toast loves her walks, enjoys the company of other dogs and is clearly a very happy girl when she is out enjoying herself. She may never be the dog who wants to curl up on your lap, but for the right person, watching her confidence grow and seeing her enjoy life will be incredibly rewarding. She will need an experienced home that understands ex-breeder dogs, a kind resident dog to help her settle, and someone who will love her exactly as she is.

This is the gorgeous, mischievous, and very cheeky Toast, or Toastie as she's called in foster. She has been in foster since April and she has come a long way, but is not your average ex-breeder. She still doesn't like to be touched and will avoid this at all costs, meaning putting a harness on is very much trial and error and catching her off guard, meaning before she can find a hiding place that's difficult to get her out of. The strange thing is, once she is out on a walk, she loves it. Saying hello to the other dogs with her waggy tail, she'll even go up to some of the owners with her tail held up high. She happily goes to visit friends with me and loves it, running in and out with the other dogs and even playing with some of the toys they have. Toastie has been to the groomers a couple of times and tolerates this quite happily and, when I go to pick her up, she's happy to be cuddled and carried back to the car. I dread to think what has happened to Toastie in her past life that prevents her from accepting that hands can be gentle and well-meaning.

Toastie does require Apoquel twice daily as she has allergies causing her to itch. She's on Arden Grange Sensitive kibble and Pro Plan Mousse, and this all helps to alleviate the scratching. She has a low-grade luxating patella, although this doesn't cause her any problems at all, but she does have a Disclaimer that would need to be signed when being adopted.

Toastie is a real little character and loves to jump around barking at you with a grin on her face, especially when it comes to having her food, and I'm reminded at every mealtime to hurry up and put hers down. She is a lovely dog but likes to do her own thing. I'm not sure she'll ever be a cuddly or lap dog, but she's happy, and it's just so rewarding when you see her out on her walks, but frustrating that you cannot explain that walkies does mean a harness and lead is required.

Anyone wishing to adopt this little girl really needs experience with ex-breeders and all the problems that can come with them. Toastie is only 4 and will need a resident dog to help her adjust and someone who can accept that she may never be a cuddly lap dog but would love her anyway.

Toast has arrived in Foster and continues to be a very frightened little girl and can panic easily if anyone tries to pick her up, so she really doesn’t cope well with handling at this stage. Once she is settled in her bed, she is a little more comfortable and will allow gentle strokes and will accept quiet reassurance and talking.

She is extremely nervous overall and will need a quiet, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand how to support a dog like her at her own pace, without pressure. She is also currently living with a cat in her foster home.

I can't believe toast has been here so long that she was due another haircut with me!She has come on tremendously for handling and as long as you're gentle she is content with being picked up, as well as having a harness put on. She is on the journey of learning to walk on a lead and it shouldn't be long before she achieves it.

I've worked with Toast for a while now and I have been able to see how much she's grown over time, especially when it comes to being groomed. The bath is still not her favourite place to be, but she tolerates it, and I think she quite enjoys the warm air of the dryer. She ends up with such a cute haircut because she is so well behaved when it comes to the styling.

This small dog has such a big and beautiful personality and I believe in the right home with another confidence dog she will flourish tremendously.

Toast was such a nervous girl when she came in and she has come on really far since then. I had the pleasure of giving her a much needed groom and although she was nervous she took to it like a champ. She will need grooming upkeep in her forever home to look after her evergrowing locks and I think with a few more pampers she will feel so much more comfortable with it.

She's currently having harness training so she can be more comfortable with the sensation and has gotten much better at being picked up and handled although she can still be a bit jumpy at times but once she's in your arms she's quite calm. She still has a ways to go but I'm so proud of her progress so far and can't wait for when she flourishes with her forever family.

Toast is a delicate little girl who has come to us from a breeder to start her journey towards a brighter future. Right now, the world feels like a very big and scary place to her, and her first instinct is to run and hide in her bed. However, once in your arms, she is easy to handle and accepts gentle reassurance with quiet trust.

She will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. Pushkin is a special little lady who has so much love to give. With plenty of patience, reassurance and the support of a canine friend, she will continue to blossom into a wonderful companion. She has brought so much joy to those caring for her, and we know that the lucky family who adopts her will absolutely adore her.

name: Cloe
description:
I need an adult only home that understands ex-breeders.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I need an extra secure garden and home that can accommodate my needs.

I am learning to walk on a harness but may need more time as I heal.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 7 teeth extracted and an inguinal hernia repaired. Read below for more!

Cloe is a very worried little lady who has come to us from a breeder and is still learning that people can be kind. It is clear she has had very little positive experience with humans in the past, and as a result she finds trust incredibly difficult. She can be flighty when worried and may choose to protect herself if she feels pressured or uncomfortable.

Cloe is a sweet but complex girl who has already shown us that, once she truly trusts someone, she has a wonderfully affectionate side. Although progress has been slow, it has also been incredibly rewarding. She now greets her favourite carers every morning with an excited waggy tail and is trying her absolute hardest to be brave around the people she trusts.

She has made lovely progress with handling and has recently enjoyed a full groom. Cloe was an absolute angel throughout, allowing herself to be groomed beautifully. She has also recently been bathed and gently dried, taking it all in her stride. These may seem like small achievements, but for a little dog who once found human contact so frightening, they are huge milestones.

We have also discovered that being picked up is only scary for Cloe at first. Once she is safely in someone's arms, she relaxes completely and allows herself to be handled without fuss. We truly believe that, with continued patience and positive experiences, this fear will continue to fade and she will become even more confident.

Cloe has also recently started her harness training. Although she is still a little too timid to venture out on walks just yet, she is making a fantastic start and we are confident that, with a little more time and encouragement, she will soon be ready to begin exploring the world beyond the rescue.

Cloe will need a calm, quiet, adult-only home with no visiting children and adopters who have experience of very worried ex-breeding dogs. Her new family will need to understand that building a relationship with her will take time and that the best way to win her trust is to allow her to approach on her own terms, without rushing or placing expectations on her.

She absolutely loves the company of other dogs and will need a kind, calm and confident resident dog in her new home. Having a canine friend gives her comfort and reassurance and will help guide her as she learns about life beyond the rescue. We have also discovered that Cloe is not comfortable around cats and can become quite fixated by them, so she will need a cat-free home.

As she has never lived in a home before, Cloe's adopters will need to be patient as she learns about house training and everyday routines. Progress with Cloe may never be fast, but she proves time and time again that she is willing to try for the people she trusts.

We are incredibly hopeful for Cloe's future. She has already come so much further than we ever imagined possible in the rescue environment, and we truly believe she will flourish in a patient, understanding home. She simply needs someone willing to take a chance on her, give her all the time she needs, and let her discover that the world isn't such a scary place after all.

Cloe has had seven teeth extracted at the time of her spay, as well as an inguinal hernia repaired. She also had a lump removed from her right upper eyelid, but has recently been advised for further treatment of the eyelid which she will be scheduled for.

Cloe has been given the Gift of Life by Carol Unsworth

Over the past few weeks there have been lots of changes in Cloe, and also a lot of things that have stayed the same! She’s thriving in certain areas, but is still reluctant to drop her guard to have fusses and take treats from me. It’s a weird one because Cloe will eat her breakfast and her dinner in front of me every single day, but the minute I walk into her kennel or the yard holding treats, she runs away and hides in the corner as if she’s frightened of them. She will eat them in her own time, just not really near me, which is such a mystery! I’ve tried lots of different things and also different ways of giving them to her, but it pushes her away. I normally use treats with all of my scared dogs to earn their trust and to get them more comfortable around me, but this definitely doesn’t work for Cloe!!! Maybe just something her future adopters should keep in mind.

Now onto the really good stuff!! Cloe’s biggest achievement is that she’s now started walking on a harness, which is pretty amazing for a dog as scared as Cloe!! I’ve taken my time with it and done lots of practices prior to taking her outside of the rescue, and it was so worth it. I think forming a (sort of) bond with her first was absolutely vital, as she was looking to me for reassurance on our first walk today constantly. If she wasn’t that familiar with me, I don’t think she would have done as well. I talked to her the whole time in my silly baby voice as it always excites her, and it definitely helped as she was wagging her tail through it!

Cloe has also gotten a lot more used to being picked up by me and we now have our own little routine for doing so. She will still run away from me, but I just approach her nice and slowly until she stops and sits down, and then she’ll put her paws up and sort of jump into my arms. Such a good girl!

Cloe may still be a little complex and hard to figure out sometimes, but the progress she’s made from when she first arrived on my section is remarkable. I can only hope someone out there would like to open up their heart to her, and continue to work with her. She’s SO worth it!!!

So Cloe has been with me for about 3 months now and I can happily say I’m finally starting to see the light as the end of the tunnel with her. I think she finally has trust in me and knows that I’m not going to hurt her, and she’s trying her absolute hardest to be brave around me. She still gets really excited to see me every morning and it always instantly brightens my days.

She’s had a busy few weeks since my last update and I really couldn’t be prouder of her. To start with, she had a full groom with our incredible resident groomer who is perfect with our scared dogs, and she was an ANGEL through the whole thing. We were both so proud of her and now she looks absolutely beautiful. I of course had to pick her up to take her into the grooming room and I was a little worried she’d hold a grudge against me, but she didn’t. She was happy when I went to get her and still had a waggy tail at me when I put her back down in her kennel. We decided not to bath her that same day as it would have been too much for her, so I bathed and dried her myself yesterday. Again, she was amazing. She was so good in the bath and let me give her a good shampoo all over. She was more scared of the dryer so I was as gentle as I could have been, and I didn’t dry her completely as I didn’t want to push it. Again, no grudges were held!!!

What I’ve come to learn about Cloe is that she’s only worried and panicky with being picked up initially. As soon as I’ve got her comfortably in my arms, she no longer stresses or fusses and lets me handle her with no issues. I really believe she’ll get over her fear of being picked up in time, and when she does, I think she’ll drop all her guards.

I am truly, truly hopeful for Cloe’s future and I really do think someone just needs to take a chance on her. Even though progress here at the rescue has been slow, it’s still progress, and that is difficult to achieve for dogs like Cloe in such a busy environment. She needs a home, so PLEASE don’t keep her waiting too much longer!!

Progress with Cloe is still very slow, but it is there and it is happening, so that’s all that matters. Since my last update she has opened herself up to me ever so slightly, and now gets very excited to see me everything morning and will run up to me and sniff my fingers with a waggy tail. I know that may not sound like a lot to most, but for a dog like Cloe it’s a big step forward.

I mentioned in my last update that I had to take her into the vets a few times and it made her more frightened of me, so since then I’ve completely left her be as I felt as though we needed to reset. I’ve spent a lot of time with her, just sitting down and being present, but no touching (until today). She wasn’t happy about me picking her up and was trying to bite the blanket I was holding, but she put up way less of a fight than she did a few weeks ago … so I’m taking that as a win!! I took her outside of her kennel just to try and take some nice photos of her and she coped really well. When we were finished and I put her back in her kennel, I got down on the floor and wiggled my fingers at her to see if she was still my friend, and thankfully she did come over with a waggy tail, so that made me happy.

Over the next few weeks I’m going to continue some gentle handling like today, every so often so that she gets more used to it, but it also won’t overwhelm her. I’ll listen to her and what she’s telling me .. stop if it’s too much, and do a little more if she’s ready.I really love Cloe and I’m understanding her more and more each day, and I think she feels the same way about me. I’m starting to feel hopeful!!

Cloe is a sweet but complex little girl who has clearly been through a great deal in her life. She has major trust issues with humans and so far only trusts one person out of all the staff that work here. At the rescue we see 2 sides of her. One side is a happy, excitable girl who enjoys a little fuss and is fine to be picked up (by her favourite person), and the other side is a scared girl who would rather be left alone (by everyone else). Her favourite person here is the first person that worked with her when she first arrived, so I think she sees him as her ‘rescuer’ which is very sweet. She definitely trusts him and it’s quite shocking to see the difference in her when she’s around him - in a good way! With everyone else, she’s still very standoffish and doesn’t tolerate being touched or handled at all. She will nip to protect herself, but this doesn’t mean she’s a nasty dog at all .. she’s simply just that scared.I’ve been working with Cloe for about a month now and even though she’s a lot more comfortable around me now than she used to be, she definitely still doesn’t trust me. I think it’s because I had to take her into the vets a couple of times when she first came over to my section, and it’s definitely stunted our relationship. Normally with dogs like Cloe, I won’t handle them for a good while until I establish some form of bond with them, but I couldn’t do this with Cloe as she had to see the vet. Since then, I’ve been leaving her to her own devises and trying to win her over from afar. Although she still hardly approaches me, she’s more relaxed in my presence now .. so at least we are making progress.I think in Cloe’s case, the best way to work with her is to just leave her come to you first. If she can work out by herself that you’re kind and not a threat, you’re heading in the right direction!! And then when she trusts you, she’ll drop her guard with you and become a little sweetheart like she is with her favourite staff member here. In a home where she has all the time in the world to bond with her new parents, I think she will absolutely blossom!!! But it may take a little while to get there, so her future adopters will need to be very understanding and patient with her. It will be SO worth it though, I promise!

Cloe is a very worried little lady who has come to us from a breeding environment and is not yet comfortable with being handled. It’s clear she has had very little experience of kindness, so she can be quite flighty and may panic if approached too quickly and can choose to make the wrong decision if pushed out of her comfort zone.

Cloe settles quickly once she feels safe and has already begun making lovely progress. With her favourite member of staff she is already showing her funny and affectionate side and is happy to approach him, kiss his fingers and will even do a little excited dance. With patient, understanding adopters who can appreciate why she may feel scared or defensive and support her as she builds trust, we believe she will settle in and start to come out of her shell.

She will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children and with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and who are willing to give her the patience, kindness, and time she needs to truly thrive.

Cloe is already starting to approach you slowly on her own terms and so will need plenty of time, gentle encouragement, and extra TLC to continue building her confidence. She absolutely loves the company of other dogs and will need a kind, calm, and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her as she adjusts to home life.

As she has never lived in a home before, Cloe's adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she settles in and learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and will need to practice around the home and garden once she is more comfortable with being handled.

Cloe has had 7 teeth extracted at the time of her spay as well as an inguinal hernia repaired. She had a lump on her right upper eye lid that has been removed.

name: Margate
description:
I need an experienced adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog, though may be able to live with a calm female.

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I have lots of energy and need an active home that loves adventures.

I can resource guard and will need adopters who can manage this.

I’m fully vaccinated and neutered. I have received treatment for an ear infection.

Margate has now spent over2 and a half years in kennels. That’sover 900 daysof waiting. Waiting while thousands of people have walked past his kennel. Waiting while his friends have come and gone. Waiting for someone to truly see him.

Everyone here adores Margate - he’s smart, affectionate, and bursting with personality. But love from staff isn’t the same as a forever home, and Margate is more than ready for his next chapter.

Since staying with us, Margate has received a dental treatment and had a cyst removed from his back left leg.

Margate came to us from a breeder in November 2023. He'sincredibly intelligent,loves a challenge, and will do absolutely anything for a tasty treat. He picks up tricks like lightning - he knows “sit”, “paw” and “speak” and he’s always ready to learn more. He thrives when his brain is engaged and would be an excellent candidate for scent work or activities like cani-cross (on-lead only!). He’s been described asone of the smartest dogs we’ve ever worked with.

He'svocal, a bit cheeky, and loves to tell us when it’s breakfast time - you can hear his excited barks all the way from the car park. He may come off as bouncy and bold, but beneath the surface, Margate is a sensitive soul who, sadly, has beenlet down by humans before. He can get worried easily, especially in overwhelming environments like the vet, where he becomes a bit of a puddle of anxiety (though he's muzzle-trained and manages with support).

Margate does require avery specific kind of home, and we won’t sugar-coat it - he’s not a “starter dog.” He needs:

Margate ispossessive around food, toys, and bedding, likely stemming from insecurity in his past. These behaviours are manageable - we’ll give guidance - but his adopters will need tounderstand and work with him, never punish or push him beyond his limits. Setting him up for success is the key.

Margate will test you - not because he's difficult, but because he's clever, spirited, and sensitive. But once you have his trust, you’ll havea bond that’s unbreakable.

Because Margate isn’t a dog you can bring home on a whim. He’s forsomeone extraordinary. Someone who sees past the behaviours and looks into his big, soulful eyes and says,“I’ve got you now.”

Margate has come so far during his time with us - he’s learned manners, made friends, gained confidence, and shown us theincredible potentialhe holds. But he deserves so much more than life in a kennel, no matter how much we love him.

Margate isnot for everyone, but if he’s for you - truly for you - then you are in for the mostrewarding journey. He’ll love you with his whole heart, and you’ll wonder how you ever lived without him.

If you think you could behis person, please don’t wait another day.

Margate’s forever is long overdue. Let’s not make him wait another year.

Margate will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

“My boy, Margate… I see all of you, and I’ll love you like you’re my own until your forever person comes along. I’ll be so jealous of whoever gets to share their life with you.”

Mr Margate (AKA Best Boy, the love of my life, Margherita Pizza, Maggie Moo, Margaret, and many other ridiculous nicknames) is approaching his third year here, and we're not letting a single day of his stay be wasted.

His days are full of so much love. So many people are part of Margate's family, and he adores seeing them all when he walks around the rescue or goes up to reception. He gets treats, but he's become quite fussy, so he'll only accept the best of the best.

He loves his long walks, his regular Margate-approved volunteers, his big yard time, sniffing as many sniffs as he can, and occasionally, he loves rolling in poo, which I am not so pleased about, but the boy enjoys it, so I don't judge.

He is the most super special boy who has so many adoring fans, and I am the founder of that fan club. I know his right home is out there; he just needs to wait a bit longer. But every single day here matters, and we're showing him all of the love, understanding, and support that we could possibly offer.

Mr Margate has utterly blown me away in recent times.Around a month ago, Margate had an unfortunate accident in the play yard, which lead to an emergency vet visit and his front paw needing stitches.

As one of the kennel managers, I see and interact with Margate regularly, but unfortunately I don’t get the luxury of working closely with him. But I think the story below highlights how much this beautiful boy wants to do the right thing.

I was the first person to get to Margate after his accident, do you know what he did when I got to the yard? He limped over to me, sat at my feet and cried out. I know some will say it’s anthropomorphism, but I am so sure in that moment, he was asking for help!

We had to carry Margate up to the top of the rescue to clean him off and assess his wounds, Margate is muzzle trained which meant we could safely assess his wounds without any risk - but honestly, he was SO well behaved. Yes he needed reassurance that he was, in-fact, being a good boy, but he blew me away with the trust he gave us.

We cleaned him up and quickly realised he needed to go for assessment with an out-of-hours vet. So, phone calls were made, and off he went, carried into a strange car and taken to a strange place and sedated for stitches… where again, he was such a good boy despite the pain he must have felt.

Upon return, poor Margate was on strict rest, with only short toilet walks, having bandage changes every few days, boots on and off for walks… his whole routine was turned upside down. Living in kennels, his world is already quite small, and these changes, although temporary and for his own good, made his world even smaller.

This is where Margate began to struggle a little; in pain and insecure, some of his guarding behaviours (which we haven’t seen for a long time) did resurface. Luckily, Margates main carer knows him inside & out, like the back of her hand, and created a plan for everyone to follow to help build his confidence back up. Just some small adjustments to keep him & everyone around him safe, which worked beautifully and we got to see the best of our boy again, despite still being on rest.

A few weeks have now passed, Margate has had his stitches out, his wound has healed beautifully - and he fully back to being our incredible, charismatic, clever, fun loving boy! It’s the highlight of my day to see Margate, he is so happy meeting everyone.

All of this is to say, Margate may not always be an “easy” dog, but he SO wants to do the right thing. Occasionally, his worries overwhelm him, but for someone with experience and patience, the love and joy you will receive in return will be so worth it.

Margate is, hand on heart, one of the most phenomenal dogs I’ve ever met, and after nearly nine years at Many Tears, I’ve met a lot of dogs! He is going to be someone’s absolute best friend and the most wonderful adventure companion.

His profile already covers all of his basic needs, so I won’t repeat those here, but I can honestly say that not a single day he’s spent in kennels has been wasted.

He has grown, learned, and loved so much during his time with us. His confidence has blossomed, he absolutely adores people, and he has made some lovely doggy playmates. He knows exactly which treats are his favourites, and he’s settled beautifully into his routine. He heads out to his yard at 9am, then off to reception to spend time with more people (and, of course, collect more treats!).

Throughout the day, different staff members make time to visit him for extra cuddles and attention, and he often spends my entire lunch break relaxing in the yard on sunny days. This is something he enjoys every second of.

Margate is such a genuinely lovely guy, which makes it all the more surprising that he’s had to wait so long. He has the sweetest nature and seems to want nothing more than to be everyone’s best friend. While he’s here, he’s made some great female play friends and absolutely loves spending time with them every day, soaking up the companionship and fun.

In one month's time Margate will have been waiting a full two years for his forever family to find him. He's been in our care for a full 23 months, that's around 700 days, he's never been adopted or gone to foster so he's not been returned to us, he just has been in the rescue for all that time, waiting.

The first picture is his original booking in photo, a very worried boy who arrived knowing nothing about what we would do for him and how much love he'd come to find in this place that should be a pit stop until their forever home is found. But he slowly grew to love people, he started to let his true personality shine through and he started to learn how to be the goodest boy in so many ways. We flash forward to today and I can still see his insecurities at times, these may never truly go away, but we help him through it all and he is one of the best dogs I have ever known.

I love him as I love my own adopted dogs and I try to let him have as much time and love as I can give him to help him not feel like a single day in kennels is wasted. Because this is two years of his life that he won't get back, so I damn well hope that I, and everyone else who has had a part in his journey, makes every single moment count!I know he'll always have his quirks and he does need a specific type of home with people who understand and can positively manage his guarding behaviours so that he doesn't feel the need to show these often. But he's such a good boy, he's so loved by all of us at the rescue, he's so smart and beautiful and funny and loving and such good company. I love every speckle of white he's grown on his face in these two years, I love every snuggle we have and every single moment he looks to me to let me know that everything is going to be okay.He needs the right home but more importantly, he deserves the right home, the right people. If I could move heaven and earth to give him his perfect life, I would.I do want him to leave the rescue, but only to people that can fully commit to keeping him safe and listening to every single guideline and boundary that we give them. One of which is that HE MUST be kept on a lead at all times when out of fully secure areas, his prey drive is very high and he deserves to be given everything he needs to be kept safe from being harmed, which means keeping him on a lead!I shall continue to love him with every day that he's in my care, as well as every day after he finds his perfect home and I wave him off.I'll be so happy that he was chosen but he's going to leave a huge hole in my heart. He's truly one in a billion.If you feel you may be the right fit, please read his profile completely and fill in a very detailed application form. We will be very particular about where he goes, because that is the least he deserves from us.My handsomest boy, Mr Margate

It's strange really, the bond you have with a dog on your section, especially if they're a long stayer.

They aren't your dog and yet you love them as though they are, you cuddle them and tell them how amazing they are, you pour your heart and soul in to them and try your very hardest to make each and every day special in some way because their time in kennels shouldn't be a waste or simply a means to an end.. it should matter and they should be living their life whilst waiting for a family of their own.

This is hard to do when there are so many dogs to care for, but you try to do the best for them and to make sure they know how truly special they are.

This is very much the case for my best friend, Margate (AKA Maggie, Margaret, Marjorie, Marge and he responds to all these names). He is the epitome of special, he does need a specific home with people who don't put him in bad situations, but when the right people come along, they'll be adopting a dog that will give them an absolutely smashing best mate and although I am desperate for his forever home to find him, the thought of saying goodbye to the most special boy with a heart the size of the moon and a brain that's double that still. I will feel as though I'm missing a huge chunk of my heart.

That's the job though, and in a strange way, that sadness is the most rewarding part. To be a part of finding them the perfect match that will not love them in spite of their quirks, but because of them. Someone who will choose them day in, day out with a certainty that just grows with every passing day. The love a dog shares with you, no matter for how brief or long, as many will know, stays in your heart forever.

I shall miss my best mate, Margate. His family will love him the longest, but I loved him first and I am so so grateful for that.

If you are interested in being the exceptionally lucky human that shares their life with this beautiful soul, then please read his profile and apply if you feel that you can give him all he needs.

Another day for Margate in kennels, after another week, another month... I'm just hoping that he doesn't have to wait until the another year mark.

Margate has been waiting for seventeen months for his ideal home to find him, that's 506 days in the same place, with people who adore him, but they're not just his people. He has to share his time with so many other dogs that are waiting for their forever homes, but none have been waiting as long as him.

He does require a special home, with people who can help him thrive and who will not fail him! But as long as they understand his needs and set him up for success, they'll get so much in return.

Margate needs a cat, child (resident and visiting) and small furry free home. He needs mental stimulation and he needs a good deal of exercise too, he is smart, so so soooo smart and this is where his humans will have to try and be smarter.

Margate learns everything very quickly and will need to have clear, set boundaries in his new home from the get-go. He will need to be given his own bed, that he learns is his bed and that he isn't allowed on the sofas or other furniture, especially to begin with. He will need a home that understands how to enrich his life, to use his brain and that LOVES a good walk. He could walk for miles. He could potentially do cani-cross as he loves to run, but Margate needs to be kept safe at all times, so he will need to be kept on a lead in anything he does (unless in a secure rented dog field area). He has a high prey drive and a nose that rivals the very best sniffer dog. If you had treats in your pocket at some point this year, he'll know.

The best set up for Margate would be a home that could adapt a room to be his area that is free of food and where he could go to sleep at night, if visitors came round or if you had to pop out to go shopping etc. He needs this to be his area that helps him feel safe and secure.

Although he can act like a big tough guy, underneath it all he is extremely sensitive and can get very worried by things.

How can we blame him for being this way? He's been let down by humans over and over again, he has had thousands of people walk by his kennel during his stay and no one chooses him.. I know that in a home that FULLY understands him and puts everything in place to set him up to succeed, then he will be the bestest boy you could ever wish to know. His heart is the size of the whole universe and he just needs someone to see him and commit to him, then they'll see what I see too. My boy, Margate, I see all of you and I'll love you like you're my own until your forever person comes along. I'll be so jealous of the person who gets to share their life with you.

Disclaimer - although he picks up agility things quite quickly, this is not something he should do to a competitive level as the environment of the events would not benefit him.

It is now over a year since Margate joined us here in Many Tears.  That’s 365 days of seeing the same kennel, and the same routine and watching his friends leave whilst he gets left behind. This year it’ll be the second Christmas in kennels and whilst others are snuggled up in a warm home and spoilt with presents, it’ll be another day in kennels for him.  Everyone here at the rescue loves Margate!

What can I say that already hasn’t been said about this wonderful boy ??

He’s a real character, smart and witty. Every morning I hear him from the staff car park and you know that he’s announcing breakfast time for the whole rescue!  At times he can be loud and bouncy but deep down he’s just a little baby who loves a good snuggle.

Margate really has improved over the year, learnt new tricks, muzzle trained, met loads of new friends and loves meeting new people! He’ll happily walk past volunteers and once instructed to sit and wait he will receive a fuss.

So far Margate has only needed the muzzle for the vets as a precaution, but he tends to turn into a puddle of mush as he’s actually quite scared of the vets.

Margate does have issues regarding high value treats, toys and beds. This is resolved by removing any food in the area, removing any toys from the yard before play time and using multiple blankets for bedding. This is something that can be discussed and helped with for potential adopters.

All Margate needs is for adopters to understand his requirement’s and who are willing to work with him in a home environment.  He is such a beautiful wonderful boy who really is wasted here in kennels?

Margate is still absolutely thriving and learning every day. He is such a clever boy who enjoys his training and the company of his kennel friend. He has come such a long way, but in a home he could truly excel as long as his new humans know how to keep his training progressing and his mind busy. I really hope he breaks free soon.

Margate is one of those dogs that once you know him, you fall head over heels in love with him. He is one of the smartest dogs I've ever worked with, picks things up incredibly quickly and tries very hard to please you. He would be the perfect only dog for someone who wants to pour lots of time in to training to build a strong bond with him and who will understand that he will train you if given a chance. He's a super special guy with so much love to give, he just needs the right person to choose him and fully commit.

Margate is a super cool bocker. He loves long walks and his time in the yard. He thrives with anything to get his brain working, so stimulation games are an excellent way of working Margate. The best way to work with him is definitely food, he will do anything for a tasty treat. Be careful though as Margate can be food possessive. As you can see by the pictures he is such an affectionate boy who loves a good fuss, to go with that he is just absolutely handsome! Margate has been in kennels for some time now and he does cope well with being in kennels, but he would just absolutely thrive in an active home with someone who is willing to keep him busy and stimulated. While he's been with us he's always had a female kennel friend but he would also be an excellent only dog, so you have the best of both worlds with Margate, but due to his exuberant nature he might grate on any resident dogs a bit . Margate is a stunning young man with bags of personality and he loves all the attention and will need an experienced owner as he is a rambunctious soul. Margate is an absolute star and deserves the best life possible, if you feel you can offer him his best life get in contact. Be sure to read all the previous updates on Margate also to get the best overall idea of this smart little man. This wonderful boy has been in kennels for far too long now and is ready to find his forever home and new loving family. Will you give him the chance to progress to the next chapter in his life?

Margate is a unique boy. Firstly, Margate will need an owner with some experience under their belt, to make sure his rehabilitation is successful. It is probably best that he is homed as an only dog, as Margate struggles to get along with some dogs due to his boisterous personality, which can be overwhelming. This doesn't mean he can't be homed with another dog, as he has had a few kennel friends at the rescue that he gets along great with, he just prefers human attention. Margate will not trust strangers 100% straight off the bat , he's always excited to see people and interact with them, but to build a bond of trust takes some time. However this is an experience that I've found extremely rewarding. I discovered this when I took him to the vets for an intimate checkup, and was surprised to discover that he would only allow me to carry out the checks. It absolutely melted my heart to know that he had complete faith in me. He really is a sweet, colourful personality with so much love and energy to give, he just needs some time, love and repetition with a regular owner to steer all that energy in a positive direction

Since his last update Margate has been enjoying learning tricks and enjoying fun little games. We have learnt to "sit" "paw" and to" speak". Margate enjoys his treats so was very keen to learn and being as smart as he is, picks up training in a flash. He is a very vocal boy and will bark until I give a treat. I do not give in and he will stop and wait patiently. Margate does need to learn manners so will need adopters to remind him of this and to show Margate right and wrong.

Margate has come on so well since being here and I must admit that I do have a soft spot for him. He enjoys his walks but does pull a little when he has found a sniff, but can easily be managed with lead training. I'm currently teaching Margate to sit when I stop walking, to get his pulling under control, and as Margate is food motivated, it’s easy to see that this can be managed with little trouble. He is already  getting the hang of it!

Margate does jump up on you and can jump quite high, so adopters will need to encourage Margate not to jump up, which I am currently showing him, but again he is a very smart boy who is eager to learn. He is a funny, friendly, and vocal boy who will needs adopters to be mindful of his needs and issues and redirect him properly for him to be the best boy he can. He is still kenneled with his friend who both still continue to share their bed and space together with no problems. He is still only young and I can't wait to see him flourish more than what kennel life can offer him. Please read Margate's profile and updates and see what an amazing boy he is. He is perfect for someone that loves to share an active lifestyle with their dog, and we can’t wait to see pictures of him on all his future adventures!

Margate is a gorgeous boy who I have spent a lot of time getting to know recently and has come along way since his last update. He greets you with a waggy tail and excitement when he knows you and does enjoy a gentle fuss. He is also getting used to his name and when you call him he will turn to you. Margate has very high energy and needs an active household who enjoys long walks and adventures and are able to stimulate him mentally as well as physically. He also walks on a lead but can pull, this can easily be managed with lead training and I believe will settle once he gets to go on regular adventures with his new family as he enjoys the sniffs of the world . Margate loves to learn and play and due to his breed, he will need adopters to understand the Bocker breed and the energy they have. Margate currently is kennelled with a female cocker and they spend their time together playing in the yard and rolling around in their beds together. They both get on very well!

Due to Margate's resource guarding, him and his kennel friend have bedding and blankets rather than plastic normal beds and they both share this with no problems. Margate does have food guarding issues  and is fed separately from his kennel friend. This can also be managed in a home with another dog if he is separated at feeding times. Margate does take treats from you when his kennel friend is present and has not shown any issues towards them but this still needs to be remembered. I have been visiting him when I'm not on the same section to issue treats around other dogs in proximity to get him used to being in the same space around other dogs with food and treats. With these small issues, Margate will need an adult home with no children.

Margate has mastered a few tricks with treats, learning to sit and give paw. He gets very excited when you ask him but need to tell him firmly. Margate can be jumpy and will jump on you so he will need a firm voice to encourage him manners. Margate learns quickly so I think teaching him house training, lead training as well as other tricks and manners will come quickly for him, especially with treats!

He is a stunning boy and overlooked here at the rescue. If you have a Bocker sized hole in your heart and are active, love long walks, adventures and fun. Please consider applying for Margate.

Hi! My name is Margate I am 2 years old male Bocker (Cocker X Beagle) and have found myself at this amazing place called Many Tears. When I first arrived, I was extremely worried with my new surroundings, and adapting back to kennel life was very tough. I have spent a little time in a home but because of my high energy levels and need for adventures my family wasn’t able to provide this so unfortunately through no fault of my own I have set out on an adventure to find my new forever home. In my new home I would need a child free home with no visiting children. In my new home I will need someone who understands my breed and have had experience with similar breeds. I am currently in a bedroom (Kennel) with a female Bocker called Nova. We don’t interact too much but we do enjoy one another’s company so I could be happy having another friend in my new home upon having a meet and greet at the rescue. I can also be an only dog as long as I have a loving owner who plays lots of games with me. I have mastered walking on a lead and I absolutely love to explore and go on walks so having a busy home who is as on the go as I am would really benefit my energy levels. I still struggle a little to find the toilet but if I’m shown I will definitely find a way to go in the right place. when I meet new people I can become a little shy and anxious so go slow with me, have a kind voice and I will wag my tail and ask you for some fuss. After spending a day with you i trust very easily and I will become your best friend. If you’d like to meet me I am currently at the many tears rescue.Margate is still waiting for his forever home at Many Tears and despite his struggles around food and resource guarding from humans and dogs when food is involved, all he needs is an experienced home with the ability to adapt and help Margate with this. He will bring so much joy into your home and he can't wait to be a cherished member of the family where he can go on lots of adventures and finally be loved.

Margate is a stunning but very confused boy who is overwhelmed to be here and has been through so much change recently. He has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home. Initially when you first meet him he is mistrustful of strangers and unsure about being handled - he will make his worries known by growling. However once you have spent a few minutes in his company showing that you are safe he quickly warms up to you and jumps all over you for love and attention. We suspect he may have lived in a home before and then returned to the breeder hence his being unsure of people initially which is fair enough, poor boy! Margate already walks on a lead and would probably prefer to be an only dog.  Margate will need a cat free home as he is far too interested in them and a home without children or visiting children as he would find them too much. Margate may need help learning to live in a home and being taught housetraining skills. Margate is such a poor soul who just wants to be loved and to feel safe. Margate would need a home that is experienced in resource guarding and can help Margate work through his struggles. Margate can resource guard when he has food or high value treats/chews/bones around both dogs and people so this would need to be managed with an environment set up to ensure lovely Margate is set up for success.

name: Hachi
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with another kind dog. I am fine with cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning to walk on a lead, but it's still very new for me.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

19-09-26 Hachi is a super sweet old man who has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He has been through so much and is now looking for the perfect retirement home where he can enjoy his golden years surrounded by love, comfort and plenty of cosy naps.

When Hachi first arrived with us, he was sadly very unwell and was passing a lot of blood in his urine and needing to urinate constantly. He required emergency surgery, during which a large 3cm bladder stone was discovered. This must have been causing him a great deal of pain and discomfort, but thankfully the stone was removed and Hachi has made a wonderful recovery. He also had two teeth extracted at the same time.

Hachi has been in foster with a member of staff since arriving with us so that he could recover in a quiet and comfortable environment. He is an incredibly sweet and loving boy who adores fuss and attention and loves to give paw! He spends a lot of his time sleeping, but as his recovery has continued, he has definitely found a little spring in his step. His playful side is starting to emerge too, which is absolutely adorable, and he is even beginning to discover the joys of playing with toys!

Hachi is a fairly confident boy and is very people focused, but he also really enjoys the company of other dogs. He loves snuggling up with his doggy friends, so would be very happy to have another kind and friendly resident dog in his new home to keep him company. In the right circumstances and with adopters who are around most of the time, we would consider homing him as an only dog. He will be looking for an adult only home, as we feel he would prefer a quiet and peaceful retirement home, but he has met young children well and would be fine to have visiting children around. He has also meet a cat fine and so could possibly be homed with a dog savvy cat.

Hachi had never lived in a home before moving into foster, so he has had lots to learn, but he is doing brilliantly and is really enjoying discovering what home life is all about. He is doing well with his house training, although he will need kind and patient adopters who understand that he is still learning. He has been wearing nappies around the house while he has been recovering and these don't seem to bother him at all.

Hachi is beginning to learn all about walking on a lead and harness and is doing really well. We think he will enjoy gentle little adventures with his new family, followed by curling up in a comfy bed and having a well earned nap.

Hachi has been through so much, but he has remained the sweetest boy throughout it all. Now that he is feeling so much better, we would love to find him a special retirement home where he can be cherished, pampered and allowed to enjoy all the simple pleasures of life.

He hasn't been castrated as our vet felt like this would be too much to put him through on top of the other surgeries, so his adopters will need to sign a disclaimer to ensure they understand this and that he cannot be around unspayed female dogs.

Hachi has been given the Gift of Life by Jade Mitchell

name: Orbit
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

20-09-26 Orbit is a very sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is feeling quite nervous and unsure at the moment and is understandably a little overwhelmed by all the changes around her. Despite this, she is an easy girl to handle and we hope that with time, patience and reassurance, she will begin to feel more confident.

Orbit absolutely loves other dogs and especially enjoys snuggling up with them. She takes comfort from having her doggy friends close by and will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help her feel safe as she settles into family life.

She is looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience of dogs and understand that she will need time to adjust. Her new family will need to be patient and allow Orbit to settle in at her own pace, gently encouraging her as she discovers all the new experiences that come with life in a home. We would consider homing her with kind and understanding teenagers aged 16+.

As Orbit has never lived in a home before, there will be lots for her to learn. She will need to learn about house training and all the sights, sounds and routines of home life. She will also need to learn how to wear a harness and walk on a lead, so this will need to be introduced slowly and positively while she builds her confidence.

Orbit is a lovely, gentle girl who is just looking for someone who will give her the time and understanding she needs. With a kind doggy friend by her side and a patient family willing to let her progress at her own pace, we hope she will soon blossom into a happy and confident member of her new family.

name: Orca
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

21-09-26 Orca is a sweet and nervous lady who has come to us from a breeder and is looking for someone willing to take a chance on her. She can still be unsure when meeting new people, but she is showing us little glimpses of the lovely girl she can be. Orca will wag her tail when she is approached or being carried, and we think she will really blossom once she has the chance to settle into a loving home and realise she is safe.

Orca is going to need adopters who are kind, patient and willing to give her the time she needs to build her confidence. We can already picture her becoming a lovely little companion who will enjoy relaxing in her new home and eventually curling up on the sofa for a cosy snooze after a day of exploring. She may take some time to get there, but we think it will be so rewarding to watch her confidence grow.

Orca has never lived in a home before, so there will be lots for her to learn. Her adopters will need to gently teach her all about home life, including house training and walking nicely on a lead, while also giving her time to get used to all the new sights, sounds and routines. She will need someone who understands that these things may be completely new to her and who will celebrate her little steps along the way.

Orca will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can look to and lean on as she settles in. Having a friendly dog by her side will help her feel more secure and give her some reassurance as she learns about her new life. She would also love a quiet home where she can take things at her own pace without being overwhelmed.

Orca is an amazing lady who just needs someone to believe in her and give her the time, patience and plenty of fuss she deserves. We are sure that with the right family behind her, this nervous girl will slowly come out of her shell and show just how wonderful she can be.

Orca has been given the Gift of Life by Trudie Williams

name: Prince
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I can walk on a lead and will enjoy going on adventures with my new family!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have bilateral cataracts and have had 23 teeth extracted.

Prince has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for his forever home. He is a wonderful, friendly boy who really enjoys being around people and absolutely loves his cuddles! He has a lovely nature and is a happy boy who is always pleased to see you.

He has recently moved to a wonderful foster home where he is getting to experience home life for the first time and has settled in extremely well. He is already enjoying all the little things that come with life in a home.. comfy naps, cuddles, walks and plenty of love!

Prince is confident enough that he could be homed as an only dog, but he would also be very happy to share his new home with another kind resident dog. We would consider homing him with dog savvy children 9+.

He had never lived in a home before moving to foster, so his adopters will need to be kind and understanding as he settles in and learns new skills like house training, though he is already doing very well with this and has only had once accident so. far. He can already walk well on a lead and is going to enjoy going for walks with his new family, but will equally enjoy sofa snoozes!

Prince is such a lovely boy who has so much to offer his new family. He loves affection and we are sure that once he has had time to settle in, he will truly thrive. We are looking for a family who will give him the patience, love and guidance he needs as he starts this exciting new chapter of his life.

Our vet has noted that he has bilateral cataracts and the left pupil in non responsive to light, so this is something his adopters and their vet will need to monitor. He has also had 23 teeth extracted so will benefit from a soft food diet moving forwards.

Prince has now been in foster for a week and is the sweetest boy. He’s a lovely, goofy and laid back character who absolutely loves his naps and cuddles - and he is quite the snorer! He sleeps happily through the night and is settling really well into foster life.

Prince could be homed as the only dog or with other dogs. He walks really well on the lead and enjoys a daily trip to the park. He is kind and curious when meeting other dogs, and this morning he met another Spaniel and was very excited to see them!

He is also doing really well with his housetraining. Apart from one little accident, he has been doing everything outside in the garden, which is fantastic progress.

Prince is a wonderful, easy going boy who is enjoying all the little things that come with life in a home.. comfy naps, cuddles, walks and plenty of love!

Prince is confident enough that he could be homed as an only dog, but he would also be very happy to share his new home with another kind resident dog. He can already walk well on a lead and is going to enjoy going for walks and adventures with his new family.

He has never lived in a home before so his adopters will need to be kind and understanding as he settles in and learns new skills like house training.
