name: Pop
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy kids aged 13+ who love cuddles, and are active!

I will need to be the only pet in my new home, so all of the attention is on me!

I would like a secure garden where I can have plenty of play time!

I am very active and will need a home that will take me on plenty of adventures!

I may have previously lived in a home, so I may already know the basics.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

Pop is a fantastic little lady who has come to us from a breeder, although we have been told she has lived in a home previously. She knows her name and responds to "Pop", so her new family will need to keep this name.

Pop is a wonderful little girl who is full of love, character and energy. She can be a little timid when first meeting new people, but it doesn't take her long to warm up. Once she knows you, she absolutely loves cuddles, enjoys giving kisses and thrives on human company. She has a very affectionate, sweet nature and loves being involved in whatever her people are doing.

As an active Jack Russell Terrier x Collie, Pop is looking for a home that can provide plenty of physical exercise as well as mental enrichment to keep her clever little brain busy. She is a very quick learner and has just mastered "sit" and is currently learning "touch". She picks things up quickly, which has also been a great help with her muzzle training.

Pop walks absolutely beautifully on her harness and would happily walk for miles and miles, so she will need an active home who enjoys getting out and about and helping their dog learn new things. Her adopters will need to be committed to continuing the training we have put in place and helping her build confidence.

Pop will need to be the only dog in her new home. She isn't currently sociable with other dogs and can become reactive when she feels overwhelmed. We are working hard to help her become more comfortable by taking her on walks alongside calm dogs at a distance. Once she is happily muzzle trained, we hope to gradually work towards safe mixes with carefully matched dogs. Her new family will need to be experienced, understanding and willing to continue this positive, reward-based training when out and about in public.

As Pop has previously lived in a home, we think she is likely to know many of the basics, although she may need a few reminders as she settles into a new routine.

She could live with sensible, dog-savvy children aged 13 years and over but will need a home without cats.

Pop is a truly wonderful little dog with so much love to give. With patient, experienced adopters who can provide the active lifestyle, training and consistency she needs, she will make a fantastic, loyal and loving companion.

Pops is such a beautiful, smart girl who is super friendly with people. She has just mastered "sit" and is currently learning "touch". She picks things up pretty quickly, which is also helping her with her muzzle training.

Pops isn't sociable with other dogs currently, but this is something we're working on by taking her on walks with calm dogs at a distance. Once she is happily muzzle trained, we will work up to safe mixes with dogs who are a good match.

She does need to be an only dog in the home, and her people will need to keep up the training we've put in place to help her feel more comfortable around other dogs when out and about in public.

She walks absolutely beautifully on her harness and would happily walk for miles and miles, so she will need an active home who enjoys helping their dog feel happier and learn new things.

As an active Jack Russell Terrier x Collie, Pop is looking for a home that can provide plenty of physical exercise as well as mental enrichment to keep her clever little brain busy. She is doing well with her lead walking and enjoys getting out and about, but she will need owners who are committed to continuing her training and helping her build confidence.

Pop will need to be the only dog in her new home. Whilst she can walk past some dogs, she is worried by them and can become reactive on lead, making the wrong choices when she feels overwhelmed. Her adopters will need to be experienced, understanding and willing to continue working on her doggy social skills using positive, reward-based training. We have already started muzzle training with Pop to help build her confidence, with the hope that, in time, she may be able to enjoy controlled walks alongside calm canine companions.

Pop is a truly wonderful little dog with so much love to give. With patient, experienced adopters who can provide the active lifestyle and ongoing training she needs, she will make a fantastic, loyal and loving companion.

name: Whispy
description:
I need a calm & quiet home, with adopters with experienced of scared ex-breeding dogs

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have not met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 2 mammary lumps removed and 2 teeth extracted.

Whispy has come to us from a breeder and is a truly heartbreaking girl. When she first arrived, she was incredibly shut down and would bury her face into the wall in the hope that nobody would notice her. She would tremble when approached and could sometimes grumble or bark, but this has always come from a place of pure fear rather than aggression.

After spending a couple of weeks settling into her kennel routine, it is clear that Whispy has experienced very little kindness in her life. Her fears are deeply ingrained, and she has no understanding of what people's intentions are. When someone enters her kennel, she will often bark and grumble in panic because she is so frightened of what might happen next. Despite this, she allows gentle handling, strokes, and being picked up without any fuss, almost as though she has simply resigned herself to it. It is incredibly sad to see, and all she really needs is someone who will show her that people can be kind.

Whispy takes enormous comfort from other dogs and has formed lovely bonds with her two current kennel companions, who she happily shares everything with.She can be selective about the dogs she befriends and seems to prefer smaller, calm, gentle dogs rather than larger or more boisterous companions.Once she trusts another dog, they become an enormous source of reassurance, soshe will need at least one kind, quiet, confident resident dog in her forever home who can help her navigate the world and show her that life doesn't have to be so frightening.

Whispy is looking for a calm, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with very scared ex-breeding dogs and who understand that trust cannot be rushed.As she has never lived in a home before, she will need help learning everything from house training to settling into a routine. Walks are not something she is ready for at the moment, and her adopters must be prepared to let her progress entirely at her own pace. Gentle garden exploration will be much more appropriate until she feels safe enough to take the next steps.

Because Whispy is an older girl and her fears are so deeply rooted, she may never completely lose all of her worries or become the confident dog people often imagine. Her adopters will need to love and accept her exactly as she is, celebrating every tiny step forward without expecting her to become a different dog. For the right family, watching Whispy slowly learn to feel safe will be incredibly rewarding.

Whispy is a very special little lady who has spent far too much of her life living in fear. She deserves a safe place to call home, where she knows nobody will ever hurt or give up on her again. With endless patience, understanding, and unconditional love, we hope she can finally experience the peaceful and happy life she has always deserved.

She has had two mammary lumps removed at the time of her spay and has also had two teeth extracted.

Whispy has been given the Gift of Life by Alison Smith

I really wish I could say that since my last update, Whispy has made a lot of progress and is finally starting to realise that humans can be kind... but unfortunately, that’s not the reality.

Whispy is finding kennel life very difficult and is struggling massively with letting her guard down, even just a little bit. She still barks at me when I go in her kennel, she still runs away from me, she still won’t take treats from my hand... she basically still just wants to be left alone.

It’s so sad to see every day, but then I think of it from her perspective. Realistically, why would she trust me? When she’s spent 8 whole years not knowing kindness? It’s such a long amount of time to endure, so of course she’s not going to become a normal dog in just a few months.

I think this is something her future adopters will need to think about often. It’s probably not going to be a straightforward, easy road with Whispy, and there won’t be any cheat codes or miracles... as much as we’d want there to be. She simply just needs time, patience, and an abundance of understanding.

She needs somewhere she can finally feel safe, and I really hope it happens soon.

Whispy has been on my section for a couple of weeks now and oh my goodness is she a heartbreaker. I have no idea what she’s been through in her life, but her fears are deeply ingrained. She has no trust in anything or anyone, apart from a select few dogs at the rescue that she has dropped her guard with. She has absolutely no idea about human kindness, nor what our intentions are. She grumbles and barks when we enter her kennel in pure panic, as she’s so scared of what we’re going to do to her. Even though she may sound a little scary, she lets me stroke her and pick her up absolutely fine .. kind of like she’s just given up. It’s quite sad actually.Whispy currently has 2 kennel friends who she gets on well with and shares everything with. One is a Shih Tzu Cross and one is a Poodle Cross. I have tried quite a few dogs with her and it does seem as though she favours smaller dogs to larger ones. And definitely calmer, quieter ones that don’t get in her face.Whispy will need a very patient and understanding home with adopters who have experience with very scared dogs. Because she’s on the older side, she may never truly lose all of her worries and fears, and may never become a ‘normal’ dog, and this is something her adopters will need to be okay with, and love her and accept her anyway. Things such as going out for walks are not currently in the near future for Whipsy, and it’s going to take a lot of time and gentle guidance to ease her into such things.This poor, sweet girl does not deserve to live her life in fear and panic mode. She deserves to have a safe place to call her own, where she knows nobody is going to hurt her. She deserves to be loved unconditionally, and to not be given up on no matter what.

Whispy has come to us from a breeder and is a truly heartbreaking girl. When she first arrived, she was incredibly shut down, and would bury her face into the wall in the hope that nobody would notice her. She would tremble when approached and could sometimes be a little grumbly, but this was simply because she is so frightened and overwhelmed by her surroundings.

Since then, she has started to settle in and is trying so hard to be brave. She can be vocal with people and is still nervous to approach you but with patience and kind handling she has been joining in on yard times and taking treats, but she still has a ways to go. Whispy has never known the kindness of people so will retreat to a corner when she feels stressed.

Whispy will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who are willing to give her all the time, patience and understanding she needs to settle and learn to trust.

She relies on other dogs for reassurance and so she will need at least one other confident, laid back resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and provide reassurance as she begins to build confidence. She can be selective over the dogs she enjoys spending time with however once she takes to a friend, she does so well with them and it boosts her confidence. She will need a very placid dog in the home who won’t worry when she is scared. She has had a few grumbles when meeting new dogs but she is just scared and needs time to develop a bond with them.

As she has never lived in a home before, Whispy will need kind and understanding adopters as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and this will be too overwhelming for her at the moment and once she is more comfortable she can begin learning in a secure garden until she feels brave enough to venture further.

Whispy is a very special lady looking for an equally special home. She has missed out on so much in her life and will need a home who will take things day by day with her and give her the support and love she’s so desperate for.

name: Whimsey
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teens who are sensible and will allow me to settle.

I could live as an only dog, or with a similar sized canine friend. No cats please!

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I walk well on a lead, but will need guidance in the outside world.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Whimsey came to us from a breeder as a very worried little girl who found the world quite overwhelming. When she first arrived, she was unsettled and skittish, needing plenty of time and reassurance to help her feel safe. Since then, she has made wonderful progress and has really started to show what a special girl she is.

Whimsey has formed a lovely bond with her carers and now greets those she knows and trusts with enthusiastic cuddles and kisses. It has been a joy to watch her confidence grow, and she is becoming more comfortable with the people around her every day.

While Whimsey has come on tremendously, she can still be nervous and unsure around new people. She will need a calm, patient and understanding home that is willing to give her the time and space she needs to build trust and settle at her own pace. Once she feels safe, her affectionate and loving personality truly shines through. She could also live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can respect her need for a gentle introduction and allow her to settle in at her own pace.

Whimsey walks nicely on a lead, but as she can still be sensitive to new experiences, her adopters will need to continue introducing her to the world gently and at a pace she is comfortable with, helping her build confidence without becoming overwhelmed.

Whimsey really enjoys spending time with other dogs and loves socialising with her canine friends in the exercise yards. We now feel she could happily live with another resident dog of a similar size, provided they get along well during a successful meet and greet. Like many dogs, Whimsey can be a little selective about her friendships, so finding the right canine companion will be important. She would also be perfectly happy as the only dog in the home, where she could soak up all the love and attention from her family while continuing to enjoy opportunities to socialise with other dogs on walks. She cannot live with cats.

Whimsey has such a sweet heart and has already shown just how much progress she can make when given kindness, patience and understanding. With the right home behind her, we know she will continue to blossom into a wonderfully affectionate companion and a much-loved member of the family.

Whimsey arrived with an abscess on the right side of her jaw, which has been treated by our veterinary team. Our vets have also noted that she has a fractured canine tooth with no root or nerve exposure. At this stage, no treatment is required, but it should be monitored by her adopters and their own vet. She has also received treatment for a urinary tract infection, which has been successfully managed under veterinary guidance.

Whimsey recently had a meet and greet with some potential adopters, but unfortunately, they decided not to go ahead with the adoption as they felt she was too nervous.

I, on the other hand, was absolutely over the moon with how confident Whimsey was around them. She approached them for a sniff, allowed them to stroke her, and even took treats from their hands, all things that are huge achievements for a girl who once wouldn’t have dreamed of going anywhere near strangers.

Yes, she was still timid at times, and sudden movements can still spook her, but that doesn’t take away from how incredibly proud I am of her. Her confidence is growing, and she is showing us more and more of her wonderful personality every day.

Whimsey is proof that patience, kindness, and trust really do make a difference. If you’re willing to put the time into her and allow her to build confidence at her own pace, you’ll discover the biggest, silliest, and most loving goofball you could ever wish to meet.

She just needs someone who can see the potential in her, believe in her, and give her the time she deserves. Once she trusts you, you’ll have a very special girl by your side.

Oh, my heart. Whimsey has completely stolen it.

She is honestly one of the most loving, affectionate, and gentle girls I've ever met. The moment I walk into her kennel or sit with her in the yard, she melts into me. All she wants is kisses, cuddles, and to be as close to you as possible. She has so much love to give!

She's doing so well with her dog socialising too and absolutely adores her best friend, Royal.

Whimsey is going to make the most incredible addition to a very lucky family. She deserves so much more than just being someone's dog. She deserves to be a cherished member of the family, included in all of life's little moments, loved unconditionally, and never made to wonder if she's enough again.

I truly can't wait for the day she finds the home she's been waiting for. Whoever gets to call this beautiful girl theirs is going to be incredibly lucky.

Whimsey has come on so well since she first arrived. She’s bonded with me so much and always welcomes me with a big kiss and cuddle.

She can be nervous and unsure around new people, but with time, patience, and understanding, she’s going to make the most wonderful addition to someone’s home.

Although she needs to be the only dog in the home, she can happily socialise with other dogs and loves going down to the big yard with her friends.

Whimsy has come to us from a breeder and is a very worried girl. When she first arrived, she was very unsettled at the moment and could be quite skittish, finding so many of the sights and sounds of the world quite overwhelming. Since arriving she has started to settle in and come out of her shell, but will still need time and TLC as she settles in to her new life. Once she gets to know you, she will quietly approach you and allow a gentle fuss.

Whimsy needs time to learn and to trust, and needs a calm and quiet home home that understands ex-breeding dogs and will allow her the space she needs to learn about trust at her own pace. She will need a calm, patient, and understanding family who are willing to let her take things slowly and gently as she begins to discover the comforts of home life.

She will need a kind and confident resident dog in her home that she can look to and rely on as she learns about home life and settles in. Having a canine companion to guide her will really help build her confidence and show her that the world can be a safe and happy place.

Whimsy does walk well on a lead, but as she can be a bit skittish, her adopters will need to take the outside world at her own pace, allowing her the time she needs to gain confidence in her surroundings without feeling pressured.

Whimsy seems like she has such a sweet heart, and with time, patience, and kindness, she will begin to show her loving and gentle nature. She just needs someone special to help her learn about trust and companionship and to show her that she is safe and loved.

Whimsy has come to us with an abscess on the right side of her jaw, which is being treated by the vets. Our vets have noted that she has one fractured canine, but no root or nerve exposure and so it is advised to leave it at this time, but will need monitoring by her adopters and their vet. She is currently being treated for a UTI and will be rechecked once the course of medication has finished.

name: Chewwie
description:
I’d like a quiet home filled with love and kindness!

I would like a home with another dog medium size or larger. I am fine with cats.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 2 teeth removed!

Chewwie originally came to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He was lucky enough to be adopted, but sadly, despite being very loved, it became clear that the home wasn't quite the right match for him and he has now returned to our care to begin his search once again. Chewwie was very worried of the adult sons in the home and also wasn't a great match with the smaller resident dog.

Chewwie is a sensitive boy who had experienced very little before coming into rescue and can find unfamiliar situations overwhelming. In his previous home, he formed a very close bond with his female adopter and absolutely adored her, but remained worried around the adult sons in the household. For this reason, he is looking for a calm and quiet home with patient adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and who will allow him all the time he needs to settle and build trust.

Since returning to our care, however, Chewwie has been an absolute pleasure. From the day he came back, he has been nothing but gentle, loving and affectionate with everyone here. Despite being returned because he was said to be nervous, we have seen a completely different side to him in kennels. He happily bounces over to greet us, is always looking for a fuss, and simply loves being around people. His affectionate nature shines through every day, and he has reminded us just what a special boy he is.

Although he had never lived in a home before his adoption, Chewwie adapted beautifully to family life. He was house trained and thoroughly enjoyed all the comforts of home, especially curling up in his cosy beds. He did find being left alone quite worrying, so his new adopters will need to be around for most of the time initially and gradually build up any time spent alone as his confidence grows.

Chewwie will need another kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help reassure him and show him the ropes, but this dog will need to be medium-sized or larger. He previously shared his home with a cat and happily ignored them, so he could potentially live with a dog-savvy cat.

Since being adopted, Chewwie has learnt to walk nicely on a lead and now really enjoys his walks, although he can still be worried in unfamiliar places and will benefit from ongoing encouragement as his confidence continues to grow.

Once Chewwie knows you, he is an incredibly loving and affectionate companion with a wonderfully cheeky personality. He loves playing with other dogs and is especially fond of his kennel friend. He's also a total water baby and absolutely loves splashing around in the paddling pool, making the most of every opportunity for fun. Like many mischievous youngsters, he has also been known to pinch things he shouldn't! His adopters will need to keep a close eye on shoes and other tempting items, as he developed quite a fondness for chewing shoes in his previous home. He especially enjoys hard toys, while softer toys and enrichment items should be supervised as he can quickly chew through them.

Chewwie is a truly special boy who has so much love to give. His return to rescue has shown us just how affectionate, gentle and resilient he is, and we know that in the right home he will continue to flourish. In return, his lucky adopters will gain a devoted, fun-loving and wonderfully cheeky companion who will fill their days with smiles.

When Chewwie first arrived, he had a lick granuloma on his front leg, which healed well. Following his return to the rescue, he began limping on the same leg and holding it up. X-rays at a local veterinary practice showed no abnormalities or injuries, so it is thought to be a soft tissue injury which should continue to improve. His adopters and their own vet should continue to monitor this as a precaution.

name: Crispin
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in.

I could live with other dogs, or be the only dog. I don't mind. I don't mind cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and love being out and about!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but has come back into our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and simply couldn't relax in his company.

Since returning to us, Crispin has moved to a foster home and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be close to his people and enjoy all the love and affection he has missed out on. While he is still worried by some men due to his past experiences, once he trusts you his affectionate nature really shines through. Crispin lives alongside two cats in his foster home and he is not bothered by their presence.

Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He gets on wonderfully with the other dogs in his foster home and sleeps happily alongside them through the night. Although he enjoys their company, his foster carer feels he could also be very happy as an only dog, where he can soak up all the cuddles and attention he so craves. In the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he would thrive.

One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. He now walks beautifully on both a lead and harness, is very sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places, and travels well in the car. Walking has become one of his favourite activities and is a lovely way to watch his confidence shine through.

As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has become familiar with many of the sights and sounds of everyday living. He has settled quickly into his foster home's routine and sleeps soundly through the night. He has had the occasional wee indoors first thing in the morning, but this has already improved over the last few days as he has established a routine. His adopters should still be prepared to continue his house training with patience, consistency, and plenty of encouragement.

Crispin has also shown that he forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite person. He loves to be close by and wants to be involved in everything they are doing. Because of this, he showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours. His ideal home would therefore be one where someone is around for most of the day, and where any time left alone can be built up very gradually, helping him feel safe and secure.

Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing a cataract in his left eye. Despite this, he gets around brilliantly, and you would hardly know he has any issues with his eyesight. He has also had all of his teeth removed, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.

Crispin really is a special little boy who has had a difficult start in life but has so much love to give. He is looking for a very special family who will understand his worries, cherish the affectionate little dog he has become, and give him the love and security he so deserves. In return, they will gain the most devoted and loving companion.

Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could potentially be a little older than this.

Crispin has been given the Gift of Life by Katrina Pirner

Crispin is smashing this home life. He is an absolute gentleman and will make a perfect best friend for an active person who is at home most of the time.

This week he has visited various secure fields, visited coffee shops and even popped into a pub for a cool drink while out on a street walk. He loves to be out and about with his human and then return home for snuggles on the sofa.

Although Crispin has a cataract in his right eye this does not seem to affect him at all. His luxating patellas also don't seem to bother him and his movement is 100%.

He is getting used to being left when I go shopping and I am extending these trips so he gets used to being without humans for a while. name: Toucan
description:
I would like a home with adopted experienced with rescue dogs.

I can be an only dog or live with a calm resident dog.

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden with 6ft+ fences to play in.

I have lots of energy and need an active home that loves adventures.

I am in a foster home and am house trained.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Toucan is a very handsome and active boy who originally came to us from a breeder. He was adopted for a short period of time, but unfortunately found himself back in rescue.

Toucan is a bright and friendly boy. He can be quite worried when meeting new people, but given time to build a bond, forms lovely relationships with his humans. He is affectionate and engaging, and with the right guidance, will make a wonderful addition to a committed home.

He is an active lad who loves his walks and exploring the world around him. At present, he can be strong on the lead as he is eager to get out and sniff everything he sees, so his adopters will need to continue working on his lead training and help him learn to walk more calmly. He is currently being trained to walk on a halti here. His absolute favourite thing in the world is playing with a ball and he just lives to play fetch! He would choose his ball over a treat any day and has proven himself to be the best ball catcher the rescue has seen!

Toucan is a clever boy who is picking things up quickly. He will benefit from a consistent routine and ongoing training to help him feel secure and understand expectations. Providing him with structure, alongside quiet resting spaces where he won’t be disturbed, will be key in helping him manage any anxieties. Although he has lived in a home, he may need some reminders about home life and skills like house training as he settles back into home life.

Toucan was adopted into a family home and though he loved the whole family, there was one isolated incident where he was snoozing in his bed and was accidentally startled by the older child in the home. Waking suddenly and feeling frightened, Toucan reacted in panic and gave a nip before immediately moving away. We believe this response was purely due to being startled while asleep, but for this reason, Toucan will be looking for an adult-only home where there are no visiting children. His adopters will need to provide him with a quiet, safe space where he can rest undisturbed and feel completely relaxed.

Toucan would be very happy to be homed as an only dog and may prefer this, but in the right circumstances we would consider homing him with a calm resident dog,

Our vets have noted that his back legs are slightly deflected outward, but this isn’t causing him any issues.

Toucan is a fun, intelligent, and affectionate boy who, with the right experienced adopters, routine, and understanding, will grow into a fantastic and rewarding companion.

Toucan has been given the Gift of Life by Alison Hale

Why is he still waiting? This handsome man would be perfect for anyone that has an active lifestyle as he has so much energy and just truly loves nothing more than being outside, with a ball.Toucan is walking on a harness and halti as he can be quite strong but with the halti he is much better, although he's not a fan and does try to get it off, he tolerates it as he knows it means outside time.He has met a few new people this week too and has done so well, he goes on long walks with one of our volunteers during the week, and also has playtime with other volunteers in one of our bigger yards and they have nothing but praise for him and really enjoy spending time with him.Toucan just needs that one person/family to take a chance on him. Someone that's going to show him what life should be like, he had a brief experience of that while living in a foster home, but now he needs his forever home with his forever people.

Another month has gone by here at the rescue and still Toucan remains, poor boy isn’t having any luck.

Recently he’s started going out for long walks with one of our experienced volunteers and to say he loves it is an understatement, come rain or shine this boy loves to be outside, either walking or running around the big yard chasing his ball.

The lady that was fostering him also comes up regularly to spend time with him and he gets so excited when he sees her, which shows that once he loves you, he loves you forever and you have a friend for life.

Toucan is a very smart boy and you can’t really fool him by pretending to throw the ball because he catches on quickly that you haven’t, also he is very good at knowing where I’m pointing to. I don’t mean if I’m next to something and pointing right at it, I mean if he can’t find his ball for example, I can point in the direction it went and he’ll look at me and go that way, very very smart boy.

As much as I love Toucan and really enjoy his company, it’s time now for him to find his forever home, I know there’s someone out there for him, the right person could be reading this right now. If you think it could be you but your hesitant, don’t be, honestly Toucan is an amazing dog and everyone that has met him has nothing but lovely things to say about him.

Toucan is a lovely boy who has settled in as though he’s always been part of the family. Once he knows you he’s very confident and affectionate, and has met family and friends - he loves everyone, including my 17-year-old nephew.

He has a big love of food (including everyone else’s!), so he is fed in his crate using a slow feeder bowl to help him pace himself. He needs to gain some weight, so we’ve been adding extra protein to his biscuits and he’s already starting to look healthier.

Toucan is house clean and travels brilliantly in the car, happily jumping in and out. He gets on amazingly well with the four dogs in the home as well as friends’ dogs.

He is comfortable with the crate and, although the door is now left open at night, he still chooses to sleep in there. Toucan can pull on the lead, which we’re currently working on. He isn’t bothered by loud noises and absolutely loves playing ball - he’s fantastic at fetch.

Toucan is a very handsome and active boy who originally came to us from a breeder. He was adopted for a short period of time, but has unfortunately found himself back in rescue. Toucan was adopted into a family home and though he loved the whole family, there was one isolated incident where he was snoozing in his bed and was accidentally startled by the older child in the home. Waking suddenly and feeling frightened, Toucan reacted in panic and gave a nip before immediately moving away. We believe this response was purely due to being startled while asleep, but for this reason, Toucan will be looking for an adult only home, where there are no visiting children. His adopters will need to provide him with a quiet, safe space where he can rest undisturbed and feel completely relaxed. Please don't let this put you off, as he is truly a wonderful boy and his previous adopters have said how wonderful he is and will be in the right home.

Toucan is is always on the go, eager to explore, and looking for his next task. He has a vibrant, happy-go-lucky personality and would thrive in an active home that can provide plenty of attention, as well as physical and mental stimulation. He is super smart and loves to use his brain and already knows "sit", "paw" and "down." He is a lovely boy who is very affectionate and really enjoys having cuddles and fuss once he gets to know you.

Toucan is confident enough that he could be homed as an only dog as long as his adopters had plenty of time to spend with him. He could also be homed with another kind resident dog and has shared his kennel well with dogs at the rescue. He can sometimes be reactive to other dogs when passing their kennels but is fine when out and about on lead. He still needs some training on the lead as he likes to be in charge, pulling us along on his travels.

Toucan has learned to walk on a harness, but he can pull and so will need adopters who can manage this and who are willing to work on this with him. He is obsessed with tennis balls and will play all day if you had the time, so he really hopes his new family will enjoy throwing balls for him!

Toucan can be a little greedy, so at the moment he is fed separately from any other dogs. He is a little and so he is now on a raw food diet to help him gain weight.

He had never lived in a home before his adoption and so home life is very new to him and he will need kindness and patience as he settles in. He was clean in his previous home but may have some accidents as he settles into a new home. With kindness, consistency, and plenty of opportunities to burn off his energy, he will make a wonderful, loyal companion for the right family.

Our vets have noted that his back legs are slightly deflected outward, but this isn't causing him any issues.

name: Oak
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before finding my forever home.

20-09-26 Oak is a sweet, shy little lady who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is feeling quite overwhelmed at the moment however, once she gets to know you, she will give you a lovely little tail wag, and she is an easy girl to handle. These little moments are so precious and show us that there is a gentle girl underneath her worries who is slowly learning to trust.

Oak loves the company of other dogs and takes a lot of comfort and reassurance from having them around. She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help take her under their wing as she learns about her new life. Having a confident doggy companion by her side will help Oak to feel safe and give her the reassurance she needs while she settles.

She is looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need plenty of time and patience. Her new family will need to allow Oak to settle in at her own pace and gently encourage her as she begins to discover the joys of home life. We would consider homing her with kind, understanding teenagers aged 16+.

Oak has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about home life, including house training and all the new sights, sounds and routines that come with living in a family home. She will also need to learn how to walk on a lead and harness, practicing first around the home and garden.

Oak is a gentle little girl who just needs someone to give her the time and reassurance she deserves. With a kind doggy friend, a quiet home and adopters who will let her progress at her own pace, we hope she will soon grow in confidence and discover just how lovely life can be.

Oak has been given the Gift of Life by Sarah Parmenter

name: Mika
description:
I need an adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning to get comfortable on a harness, but this will take time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

13-08-26 Mika has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She is a very shy little lady who prefers to hide away and looks to her canine friends for comfort and reassurance. When left alone, Mika shakes like a leaf, and it is heart-breaking to see just how overwhelmed she can become.

Mika will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in the home that she can lean on as she learns about trust, companionship, and life in a family environment. She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to have ex-breeder experience and be patient and understanding as she learns all about house training and settles into a new routine.

Mika has started to learn comfortability with putting on a harness, and has walked to and from the yard on a lead but she is still too nervous to venture out too far just yet. Her adopters will need to work with her on this and continue to build her confidence and work at her pace. She will need a calm, adult-only home where she can settle at her own pace and slowly begin to build her confidence.

Mika has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

name: Royal
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like to live with a female dog. No cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am learning about house training in my foster home, and am doing so good!

Royal is a very special Chow Chow who has come to us from a breeder in search of his forever home. When he first arrived, he was extremely frightened of the world around him and was very wary of being touched or handled. Thanks to gentle care and patience, Royal has made incredible progress and is continuing to blossom in foster, where he is experiencing home life for the very first time.

Royal has exceeded all expectations with how well he has settled into foster. He has been an absolute superstar, sleeping soundly through the night, travelling well in the car, walking beautifully on lead and has even been completely clean in the house. Every day brings a new milestone, and it has been a joy to watch his confidence grow as he discovers all the comforts and pleasures of family life.

Although Royal is still nervous of people initially, he so desperately wants to trust and tries his hardest to be brave. He has begun asking his foster carers for gentle neck and bum scratches, happily takes treats from their hands, enjoys rummaging through the toy box, has found his little voice and now greets them with his wonderful wagging tail. He is such a sweet, gentle soul who simply needs time to work things out at his own pace.

Royal absolutely relies on the resident female dogs in foster for confidence and reassurance. He watches their every move, learning how to be part of a family, and loves playing alongside them. He will need to share his forever home with at least one kind, confident female dog who enjoys a good play and can continue to show him the way. He cannot live with cats.

As this is Royal's first experience of living in a home, he thrives on routine and will need patient, understanding adopters who will allow him to settle without pressure. He has made remarkable progress already, but he is still very nervous of the unknown and benefits from people who understand that he needs time to process new experiences. A calm, rural or quiet home would suit him best, as he is currently worried by traffic. He is looking for an adult-only home with breed experience and experience with very nervous rescue dogs would be highly beneficial.

Royal has recently had a bath and full groom at the rescue and was an absolute gentleman throughout. As a Chow Chow, his beautiful coat will require regular daily grooming. He is very tolerant of being brushed when it is introduced slowly, little and often, and this has become an important part of his routine.

Royal is an incredibly special boy who has embraced this new chapter in his life with quiet bravery. With patience, kindness and the continued support of confident canine companions, he will become a wonderfully loyal and loving companion. Watching him continue to discover the world and grow in confidence will be an incredibly rewarding journey, and he is sure to make his forever family smile every single day.

Royal is currently being treated for an ear infection.

Wow! This darling boy has just exceeded all expectations with how well he’s settled into his very first home, in his first week. Not a single accident (unheard of for a boy), sleeps soundly over night out of a crate, happy to be left alone with the company of the resident dogs, walks well on a lead, travels well. A literal angel boy.

Royal is the sweetest soul, he doesn’t trust humans easily but he really wants to and tries so hard to be brave.

He relies heavily on our resident girl gang for confidence & reassurance, watching & copying them intently to learn what being a member of a family is all about.

After an initial overwhelming few days for him, every day now brings a new ‘first’ & burst of joy on our part! Asking for a neck / bum scratch, taking a treat from our hand, rummaging in the toy box, playing with the girls, finding his little voice & wagging his amazing tail when we talk to him. He is just loving this next step in life and is so ready to be someone’s special boy.

Royal currently needs an adult only home as has not yet been tested with children. He needs confident kind resident female dogs who like a good play. A rural / quiet location would be preferable as he’s currently quite scared of traffic.

He is still very nervous of the unknown, thrives on routine and needs to be guided and given time to work things out without any pressure so experience with very scared dogs would be helpful.

As a Chow, his beautiful coat will need grooming daily. He is very tolerant of this if done slowly, little & often.

Please get in touch if you feel you might be the right match for this special big guy, he will make you smile every day.

Royal is not a dog I’ve had the chance to work with until recently. I’ve heard a lot about him, as he’s one of our longer stayers. I had heard many great things from other members of staff, including the incredible progress he’s made since joining us!When I did get the chance to work with him, my first impression was “oh my days, you are beautiful!” On first sight, he is one of the most beautiful dogs I’ve ever seen and certainly the most stunning chow I’ve ever seen! How can you look at this handsome boy and not fall in love?!When I actually began working with him, I realised how shy and timid he actually was. Initially, he wouldn’t come to the front of the kennel to see me, he’d hide away in the back. It was evident to me that this boy did not trust me. As I continued to work with him, I was very aware of my actions, to ensure I wasn’t causing any anxiety. I began with treats (who doesn’t love a cheeky bribe?). It slowly worked. Initially, he wanted nothing to do with me. I didn’t want to invade his safe spaces (safe spaces are so important for a more scared or anxious dog. Could you imagine a big scary stranger coming into your home and not leaving? I wouldn’t feel too easy if that occurred to me). So, I’d place the treat and leave the kennel. He’d come out, have a little nosey and take the treat. With time, he began slowly coming out of the back as I entered his kennel. He then began taking treats from my hands and now, whenever I walk onto the section, he comes straight to the gate and waits for me. Honestly, such an incredible feeling making a bond like this with such an incredible boy! There is honestly no feeling like it. They say a dog is a humans best friend but, what no one tells you it works both ways. To build that bond, teach him that I’m not scary, I’m here to help him feel safe, comfortable, happy and to get such a response… it’s honestly the best feeling in the world. Royal needs a home, he needs people to show him this on a day to day basis. We do what we can but, we can’t teach him the safety and comfort of a home, of a family that’s there for him 24/7.Once I got to know this guy a little more, I was taken away. We go out on walks. I feel like this was another bonding experience for us. He loves a walk but, loud noises and interactions with loud people/dogs do freak him out, thus we try to go for quieter walks. He also loves frolicking in the yard. From my experience, he seems to just love being outside!When I worked with him, he didn’t have a friend in his kennel, however, since working with him I have seen him enjoying in the yard with other dogs and is now kennelled with a boxer. He seems very happy. As previously mentioned on his profile, he is to be homed with females around his size or alone. I have not worked with him enough to comment further on his compatibility and amiability with other dogs so, please read the rest of his profile and updates to get a fuller understanding of this incredible boy!At this point, I’ve worked with him enough for him to trust me. He’s happy to see me, he’s fine for me to touch him and fuss him. The Royal I see is a happy dude. He is a scared dog, I’m very aware of that but, the Royal I know now is far different to the Royal I first met. You just have to gain his trust and he’ll let you see him. When you first meet him, he will be shy. He’ll hide and he will not trust you. DO NOT let this deter you. He is one of the sweetest dogs I’ve ever met. From when I first met him to now, I feel like he’s a completely different dog. I was respectful of his boundaries, slow and calm, I did what I could to make him feel comfortable and safe, he then began to trust me and show me his true self (he hides it beneath all that fur). Honestly, I love him. I will take time out of my day to go see him, give him a little treat and some love, just because he is honestly that special. I cannot believe he’s been here over a year. He is one of our most special dogs. I don’t see how anyone can get to know this dog and not love him.Don’t overlook this fluffy dude. Yes, he’s shy and nervous but, the longer you spend with him, care for him and gain his trust, the more you’ll fall in love with him. I can say with confidence; if you put the effort in with Royal, you will fall in love with him.

I absolutely love this boy with my whole heart.

I've been working hard on helping him get used to being brushed because, as a Chow, it's something his future adopters will need to keep up with regularly to keep his coat healthy and prevent mats from developing, especially behind his ears.

Royal is now an absolute angel when it comes to grooming. I brush him every day, and with it being shedding season, no matter how long I brush for, there always seems to be more fur coming out! These days, he simply finds a comfy spot, settles down, and lets me get on with it. If he's had enough, or if I come across a mat that's uncomfortable for him, he communicates so well to let me know he's done for the day.

I also recently decided it was time to give him a bath. I wasn't sure how he'd cope, as it involved picking him up and putting him in the bath, but he was an absolute angel from start to finish. He allowed me to pick him up without any fuss and stood beautifully while I bathed and shampooed him.

I'm so incredibly proud of him. Afterwards, I introduced him to the grooming blower to help remove some of his loose coat. He wasn't a huge fan of it, but he tolerated it for a short while, and I'll continue using it regularly so he can build his confidence with it.

I honestly think all this grooming time has strengthened our bond even more, because lately he seems to be seeking out so much more affection and attention from me. He's such a special boy, and it has been wonderful watching his confidence grow.

Royal has now been with us for over a year, and we’re still waiting for the right person to see just how special he is. He’s had two meet and greets during this time, but sadly neither worked out as he was too nervous meeting new families.

Royal is a sensitive boy who simply needs time, patience, and understanding. He can be unsure at first, but once he begins to trust you, his cheeky, affectionate personality really shines through and it’s such a joy to see.

With a consistent routine, Royal truly thrives. He now enjoys running freely around our large yard without a harness or lead, and when it’s time to go back, he comes straight over. He’s also been out on two longer walks away from the rescue with one of our regular volunteers and has done amazingly well.

All Royal is looking for is someone willing to give him the time and patience he deserves. In return, he’ll become a loyal and loving companion.

I’ve come on leaps and bounds over the past month. I’m still a little shy and can get nervous when I meet new people, but I’m working on it!

I feel most comfortable when I spend quality time with people. It doesn’t take long for me to start feeling at ease (though I still sometimes like my own space). The more time you spend with me, the more comfortable I become—and treats help too! I’ll return your love in equal measure, as long as I’m given the right time, support, and respect.

I love going out for walks, though I can get nervous around loud noises or sudden movements. They might make me jump or feel uneasy, but a bit of love and reassurance always helps!

I feel more comfortable every day. I benefit not only from interaction with my humans, but also from the company of my kennel friends that I live with.

Another month has gone by, and my cheeky boy Royal is still waiting in kennels. I honestly don’t know why this handsome lad isn’t getting much interest. Not only is he completely unique-looking, but he also has the funniest, quirkiest personality. If you want a dog who’ll make you laugh every single day here he is!

Royal is 99% kennel clean and always keeps his bedding tidy… well, until I make his bed perfectly for him. Then he likes to “show me how it’s supposed to be done” by pulling it all across the floor. He walks beautifully on the lead now; he can still get a little spooked from time to time, but he’s made massive progress since the day he arrived.

He loves his toys he just doesn’t love sharing them! He’s also a bit selective with kennel mates, so his ideal home would include a calm, placid large female dog who won’t make too much fuss over him.

Royal truly is an amazing boy, inside and out, and I hope he doesn’t have to wait much longer for the forever home he deserves.

Royal never fails to make us smile with his crazy, funny, and quirky personality. He’s got such a cheeky side to him just waiting for the right people to help it shine.

On the lead, Royal is already walking beautifully, though he can still get a little nervous at times. His new family will need to be patient and willing to help him build confidence. Loud noises or sudden movements can overwhelm him, so he’ll do best with calm, quiet walks to start.

This week Royal had his very first trip down to the big yard! He loved it, though he found his confidence by sticking close to his doggy friend. With more practice, we’re sure he’ll begin to explore on his own.

Royal absolutely adores other dogs. Once he’s settled in, he loves to play, so he’ll need a kind and confident resident dog to show him the ropes, give him reassurance, and of course, enjoy plenty of playtime together.

He’s such a handsome boy with so much love to give we can’t believe he hasn’t found his forever home yet!

This past month has been a huge step forward for our boy Royal! Once a little unsure of the world, Royal is now walking beautifully on lead, it’s such a massive step for him considering how nervous he once was!

Royal currently shares his kennel with both a male and a female dog and he’s proving to be a respectful and easy companion. He enjoys their company, often watching what they do and following their lead. Royal will definitely need another resident dog around his size in his home, so he can continue to have the doggy companionship to help him continue to grow in confidence.

Despite his progress, Royal is still a sensitive soul, and it takes a little time for him to warm up to you. Royals forever family will need to give him time and patience to come out of his shell, so for this reason I believe Royal would be best suited to a home with no children.

Please don’t leave Royal waiting much longer for his forever home, he really deserves a cosy sofa to curl up on!

I’m so proud of Royal, this boy has come on tremendously since arriving at Many Tears. From arriving a terrified dog and very unsure of us humans, he has now slowly but surely begun to trust us and realise we are not so bad, especially when we arrive with cheesy treats.

Royal loves food, toys and being outside in our yards. He has just began harness training, ready to begin lead walking. At the moment he is not so keen on lead walking but he has taken a few tentative steps and with the help of some squeezy cheese and possibly a confident doggie friend to follow I think it won’t be long before he can begin to enjoy exploring the world.

Royals adopters will need to understand he is still very wary and unsure of his environment and he is going to need plenty of time, love and patience to trust his humans, but in the right home and given time I think this boy is going to be a big, playful and lovable boy. Royal will need a home where there is already a resident dog.

Royal is a very scared boy who has come to us from a breeder. He is especially scared when it comes to being touched by us humans but when you get him in the back of the kennel he will allow you to gently stroke him but he is uncomfortable with this. name: Berry
description:
I need a quiet, adult only home that understands ex-breeders.

I need to be the only dog in the home, and cannot live with cats!

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I walk well on a lead but I can be frightened, so I will need to take it slow.

I have lived in a home for a short period and may already know the bascis.

I am being treated for dermatitis around my paws and an ear infection.

Berry originally came to us from a breeder in 2022 and was adopted into a home, but she has unfortunately been returned as she was still struggling to live with the resident dog. While she socialises well with other dogs when out and about, she is looking for a home where she can be the only dog, as she has shown resource guarding behaviours around high-value items such as food and treats within the home.

When Berry arrived back here, she was a very worried little girl who preferred to keep her distance. Since then, Berry has made some lovely progress. Although she can still be a little nervous in new situations and with unfamiliar people, she has grown so much in confidence with the people she knows. She now actively seeks out fuss from her handler and, if they stop, she'll gently paw at them and even have a little cry to ask for more attention.

In her previous home, Berry displayed resource guarding behaviours around both dogs and people. Around people, this can be managed by giving her a little space and swapping the item for something of higher value, rather than trying to take it away. Her guarding comes from insecurity and likely reflects a life where she never truly had anything of her own. Because of this, Berry is looking for an adult-only home with adopters who understand resource guarding, have ex-breeder experience and are committed to using kind, positive management techniques.

We have been told that Berry is clean in the home, although she may need a few reminders while settling into a new routine. She walks nicely on the lead and doesn't pull, although she can be timid and easily startled, so she will benefit from gentle encouragement as she continues to gain confidence in the world around her.

Despite her worries, Berry has so much love to give. She is simply looking for a calm, patient home where she can finally feel safe, build trusting relationships, and enjoy life at her own pace. With understanding, consistency, and plenty of kindness, Berry will blossom into a wonderfully loyal and loving companion.

Berry is currently being treated for some dermatitis around her paw area as we as an ear infection.

What a stunning lady Berry is! She is such an affectionate girl who has been a pleasure to look after since being returned. She mixes with other dogs very well and has one dog in particular that she adores spending time with.

She has shown a few signs of bed guarding but will come away from her bed when spoken to with kindness and offered something yummy, so it has been easily managed here. She does need adopters with experience of guarding, but if managed correctly and kindly, her good will far outweigh her insecurities.

She is such a special girl with so much love to give her people. She loves going out and about and exploring different areas and getting all the sniffs. I can not express how much I love looking after this lady and although I will be pleased to see her going to her forever home, she's going to leave a huge hole in my day here.

name: Winnie
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult-only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home!

Winnie is a very scared girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She has clearly had some very difficult experiences in her past, and at the moment she finds it incredibly hard to trust people or believe that we mean her no harm. She is an extremely frightened little girl who needs a very special and experienced home where she can begin to learn that life can be safe and that human hands can be kind.

Winnie is currently finding human interaction and handling exceptionally overwhelming. If someone approaches her too closely, she can become extremely distressed and will bark continuously as she panics. Being picked up is particularly frightening for her, and when she feels trapped or unable to escape, she will bite wherever she can reach. She may also toilet through fear when someone attempts to pick her up. These behaviours are coming from a place of extreme fear and a desperate attempt to protect herself, but they are very real behaviours that her adopters will need to understand and be prepared to manage safely. Winnie is not currently a dog who can be handled casually, and her future family will need to be very experienced with severely frightened ex-breeding dogs and confident in reading her body language and respecting her boundaries.

Winnie will need a very calm and quiet, adult-only home with no pressure placed upon her to interact before she is ready. Her adopters will need to understand that building a relationship with Winnie is likely to be a long journey, and progress may be very gradual. She will need people who are willing to allow her to take things completely at her own pace, while providing a safe, predictable environment where she can slowly learn that she is not going to be hurt.

Despite how frightened Winnie is of people, she is already showing us some lovely glimpses of the little dog underneath her fears. She absolutely loves toys and food, and although she isn't yet brave enough to take treats directly from our hands, she is more than happy to join in with treat time when treats are gently thrown towards her. She is also beginning to enjoy the simple comfort of being cosy in a big, comfy duvet. These small things are incredibly important for Winnie and give us hope that, as she begins to feel safer, we will see more and more of her personality emerge.

Winnie will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to for reassurance and companionship. Having another dog around may help her feel safer and give her a familiar canine friend to follow as she learns about her new life. Her adopters will need to ensure that any resident dog is calm, confident and able to give Winnie the space she needs.

Winnie has never lived in a home before, so absolutely everything will be new to her. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about home life, including house training and the everyday sights and sounds of a household. Lead walking is not something Winnie is ready for at this stage, and her new home will need a very secure garden where she can begin to explore safely without being overwhelmed.

Winnie is not going to be an easy dog, and she will require a significant level of commitment, experience and patience from her adopters. However, she is not a lost cause. She is a deeply frightened little girl who has not yet had the opportunity to understand that people can be trusted. Seeing a dog like Winnie slowly begin to feel safe and choose to engage with the people around her can be incredibly rewarding, but her adopters must be prepared for this to take time.

Winnie needs someone truly special who understands just how serious her fears are and is willing to give her the space, security and patience she needs. Beneath all that fear is a little girl who loves food, adores toys and is beginning to discover the comfort of a cosy bed. With the right experienced home and plenty of time, we hope Winnie will one day feel safe enough to let her true personality shine.

Jasmine has come to us from a breeder to find the loving forever home she deserves. Jasmine is now in a foster home, where she has settled wonderfully and is showing us just how much progress she has made. She was adopted for a short period of time but was reluctantly returned to us as the resident dogs in her previous home were unable to accept her. She is still a sensitive little lady who can become skittish when worried, but she is beginning to relax and show more of her sweet personality.

Jasmine is looking for a calm, quiet and stress-free home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need time, patience and reassurance to settle into her new life. A quieter area would be preferable, as she can find too much going on overwhelming. There is no quick fix for Jasmine, but she is already showing that with the right environment and plenty of understanding, she can continue to grow in confidence.

She takes great comfort from other dogs and will need friendly resident dog or dogs in her new home. They can be any size or breed, but they will need to be kind and happy to have Jasmine around, allowing her to follow them and curl up alongside them without being fazed if she becomes a little skittish. She sleeps quietly through the night in a dog bed close to her foster family's dogs and clearly finds having other dogs around a great source of comfort and security.

Jasmine would love a secure garden to explore, although she found a very large garden overwhelming in foster, so a smaller area would be preferable. She has been doing wonderfully with her toileting and will take herself outside when the back door is open. In fact, she has been completely clean since arriving in foster, which is fantastic progress. She also enjoys exploring and has even been known to make her way into raised flower beds for a snooze!

Jasmine has also made lovely progress with her confidence and is becoming much more relaxed in her foster home. She loves her food and treats and is now eating her meals more calmly. As she arrived very thin, she is currently having three meals a day to help her gain weight. She can be a little particular about drinking and currently needs a tiny amount of grated cheese added to her water to encourage her, but she is otherwise doing well. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged, 16+, who are sensible and allow her time to settle in.

Jasmine can give you the runaround when she needs to be picked up, but once she is safely in your arms she relaxes and seems to really enjoy being cuddled. She has even started to play with her octopus toy when nobody is looking, which is such a lovely glimpse of the playful little character hiding underneath her worries.

Jasmine's back leg is doing wonderfully and does not cause her any problems. She happily pings up the back steps and even climbs into the raised flower beds for a comfortable snooze. When Jasmine first arrived, she was walking with a noticeable limp and struggling to use her right hind leg. Our vets found that an old injury had healed with significant scar tissue, which was restricting her movement and preventing her from fully extending her leg. Jasmine underwent surgery to remove some of the excess scarred tissue and has continued to recover well. She will need to continue building up the muscle in her leg and may always have a slightly unusual gait due to her old injury, but it certainly doesn't stop her from getting on with life. Jasmine also has an old healed break in her tail.

Jasmine is a truly sweet little girl who has already come such a long way. She will need a special home that is willing to give her the time, patience and understanding she needs to continue building her confidence. With friendly canine companions to lean on, a quiet environment and plenty of love, we are sure Jasmine will continue to blossom. She may take a little more time than some, but we truly believe this sweet little girl will be worth it.
