She gets on very well with the other dogs in foster, but especially loves the humans! She sleeps soundly all night with the other dogs and is happy to be left for a few hours.

Pandora will be looking for a calm and quiet home and would benefit from adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need love and TLC as she settles into her new home. She loves other dogs and would love to have another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend, but in the right circumstances and with adopters who are around most of the time, we would consider homing her as an only dog. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in at her own pace.

She had never lived in a home before moving to foster, so everything is still fairly new to her and she will need kindness and patience as she continues learning about home life and new skills like house training. She can now walk well on a lead and harness and enjoys her walks and adventures so would benefit from an active home. She has even visited a secure field, which she loved! She will need a secure garden with 6ft fences.

Our vets have noted that she has a Grade 1 heart murmur, which doesn't require any medication but will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet going forward. She also came to us with a fluid-filled swelling on the side of her face, which our vets diagnosed as a salivary mucocele. This occurs when a salivary gland becomes damaged, allowing saliva to leak into the surrounding tissue, where it collects and forms a soft, usually painless, pocket of fluid. Our vets have drained this, however it has started to gradually refill again and may need to be drained again in the near future. The only permanent treatment is surgery to remove the affected salivary gland, which would need to be carried out by a specialist. Pandora's adopters would need to be aware that any vet treatment surrounding this would not be coverable by insurance as it's pre-existing.

Pandora has been given the Gift of Life by Lynne Hughes

Pandora has been here for a week and I feel like she has always lived here. She really is an incredibly sweet girl who just lights up a room. She has so much love to give.

She sleeps in kitchen all night and is happy to be left for a few hours in the crate. She LOVES food and being fussed and is just everything you would expect a Labradoodle to be.

She loves being out in my secure field and happily came and found me for a fuss. She also travels well.

She plays nicely with all the dogs, even the small pupster but is not dependent on them. Pandora just simply wants to be loved!

Pandora has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a scared little girl who is worried to find herself here at the moment, but she is trying ever so hard to be brave. If approached slowly and gently, Pandora is happy to enjoy a little fuss and is beginning to show what a sweet girl she is.

Pandora is looking for a calm and quiet home and would benefit from adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need plenty of time, patience and reassurance as she settles into her new life. She gains confidence from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help show her the way. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in at her own pace.

Having never lived in a home before, everything will be new to Pandora and her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life. She will need help with house training. She walks well on a harness but it is advised to initially further practice around the safety of the garden to help build her confidence. She will need an extra secure fence of at least 6ft to ensure her safety.

Although Pandora is not yet walking on a lead, we feel she will be best suited to an active home where, once she has gained confidence and learned all about the world around her, she will be able to enjoy lots of adventures with her family. With time, patience and the support of her doggy friend, we are sure Pandora will blossom into a wonderful companion.

Our vets have noted that she has a Grade 1 heart murmur, which doesn't require any medication but will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet going forward. She also came to us with a fluid-filled swelling on the side of her face, which our vets diagnosed as a salivary mucocele. This occurs when a salivary gland becomes damaged, allowing saliva to leak into the surrounding tissue, where it collects and forms a soft, usually painless, pocket of fluid. Our vets have drained this and it has remained stable so far. However, it is likely to gradually refill over the coming weeks or months and would need to be drained again if this happens. The only permanent treatment is surgery to remove the affected salivary gland, which would need to be carried out by a specialist. Pandora's adopters would need to be aware that any vet treatment surrounding this would not be coverable by insurance as it's pre-existing.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Lollipop
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 +, who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home and would prefer a male dog. I don't mind cats!

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a grade 2 luxating patella and have had 7 teeth extracted. Read below for more

Lollipop is a lovely Bichon Frise who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is an inquisitive and funny little girl who is already showing glimpses of her playful personality. Lollipop will happily come over to lick our fingers before darting away again, as if she's still deciding whether people are quite as interesting as her kennel friends.

Lollipop is still a nervous little girl, but she has been making lovely progress and is gradually becoming more curious about the people around her. The more time you spend with her, the more interested she becomes in you, and it is lovely to see her slowly coming out of her shell.

Lollipop loves the company of other dogs and relies heavily on them for comfort and reassurance. She is happy to follow their lead and takes great confidence from having another dog around. For this reason, she will need to have a resident dog in her new home. She will be looking for a home with a male resident dog as she can sometimes be a little sassy with female dogs.

Lollipop has also been making lovely progress with her harness training. She is easy to put her harness on and recently went out for her very first walk. Considering how nervous she can be, she did incredibly well! She will need plenty more gentle practice to help her become confident and comfortable with walking, and her adopters will need to continue this at her own pace.

As Lollipop has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a whole new world and gains confidence in her surroundings.

Lollipop could share her home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

She has arrived with a Grade 2 luxating patella, but her mobility appears unaffected and this may improve as she builds muscle tone. Lollipop has also arrived with severe periodontal disease and has had seven teeth extracted.

Lollipop is an active and spritely little girl with a bright future ahead of her. With the support of a kind canine friend and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow and her charming personality will shine through even more.

Lollipop has been given the Gift of Life by Jodie Stanley

Lollipop has been making lovely progress with her harness training. Today, she went out for her very first walk and, considering she is still quite a nervous girl, she did incredibly well. She is easy to put her harness on, but she will need plenty more practice to help her become confident and comfortable with walking.

Lollipop relies heavily on her kennel friends for reassurance, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her settle into family life. The more time you spend with her, the more curious she becomes about you, and it is lovely to see her gradually coming out of her shell.

She definitely prefers the company of other dogs at the moment, but she is happy to follow their lead and takes great comfort from having them around. As Lollipop gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends, she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Lollipop has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a whole new world and gains confidence in her surroundings.

Lollipop could share her home with older dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

She has arrived with a Grade 2 luxating patella but her mobility appears unaffected and this may improve as she builds muscle tone. Lollipop has also arrived with severe periodontal disease and has had 7 teeth extracted.

Lollipop is an active and spritely little girl with a bright future ahead of her. With the support of a canine friend and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow and her charming personality will shine through even more.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Buck
description:
I would like an adult-only home that can understand my needs!

I would like to be the only dog in my new home.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I can walk well on a harness and would love an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have no tail, but this doesn't bother me!

Please meet the very handsome Buck, who has travelled all the way from Romania in the hope of finding his forever home. Since arriving here a few months ago, Buck has truly blossomed! Initially a little shy with new people, he now settles quickly and happily shows off his affectionate, gentle nature. He loves attention, enjoys fuss, and is more than happy to make new friends once he feels comfortable.

Buck is such a comical boy, always finding little ways to make you smile, but he is also incredibly affectionate. He has that spark of energy that brightens even the hardest of days.

Buck absolutely loves his food. You’ll hear his excited bark echo around the rescue at mealtimes without fail. He also really enjoys his walks and having a good run around the big yard, where he can let out all that happy energy. Buck also has the most cuddly side to him; he loves nothing more than resting his head on your lap while he slowly dozes off to sleep.

Buck was briefly adopted but was sadly returned as he didn't get along with the resident dog and we believe that we would do best as the only dog in the home. He can get a little jealous of sharing attention with another dog in the home, but he mixes well out and about as long as he is supervised.

Buck will be looking for an adult only home and would be best suited to adopters who have experience of owning dogs from a similar background before and who are around most of the time, so they can spend lots of time with him. He would love to find an active home where he can be kept both physically and mentally stimulated and enjoy plenty of walks and adventures with his new family.

Although Buck had never lived in a home before being adopted, he settled in wonderfully and was clean in the house. He wasn’t phased by the TV or radio and quickly found the sofas and beds! He can still be a little shy when first meeting men, but it doesn’t take him long to warm up. Buck also isn’t keen on sudden loud noises or sticks and brooms, so this is something his adopters will need to work on desensitising him to. He doesn’t like having his front paws touched, but he will politely let you know by gently pulling them away.

Buck is a truly special boy with so much love to give. He is absolutely wasted in kennels and will make a loyal, devoted companion for a very lucky family. He arrived with no tail, but this doesn’t bother him in the slightest and only adds to his charm. Please don’t overlook this wonderful lad, as Buck is more than ready to find his forever home.

Buck has received negative test results for Brucellosis, Leishmania, Giardia, Heartworm, Ehrlichia canis, Borrelia burgdorferi and Anaplasma.

Buck will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

253 days of Buck waking up in a kennel, waiting for the day his person finds him!

Buck isn’t the sort of dog who instantly shows you everything he has to give. He needs time. He needs patience. He needs someone who is willing to sit beside him and let him learn that they’re safe.

But when he trusts you, you get to see the funniest, silliest, most loving boy hiding underneath all those initial nerves. You get to see his personality come alive, and there is honestly no better feeling than knowing he finally feels safe enough to be himself, I just wish everyone else could see the Buck that I see.

Because I know, without a doubt, that someone out there is going to absolutely adore this boy. Someone is going to give him the time he needs, and in return, they’ll get a friend who will love them with his whole heart, but until that person finds him, I’ll keep loving him and reminding him every day that he matters!

Buck is truly the most special dog in the world, I love spending my days caring for him and preparing him for home life, but I would love it even more, to be seeing updates of him in a home.

Buck has now been with us for 7 months and is still patiently waiting for his forever home.

Buck absolutely loves the people he knows and trusts. If Buck is unsure of someone, it will take him awhile to come out of his shell and get to know them, but once they've built a bond with him, he is the most loving gentle boy, who loves attention!

Buck has plenty of doggy friends and enjoys socialising outside of his kennel environment, although he definitely has a preference for the ladies and gets on best with female dogs.

Buck can potentially live with another calm female dog who will respect his space when he needs it.

Buck is looking for an adopters who will give him the time he needs to settle and understand that he can be a very worried boy at first.

I do genuinely love Buck with my entire heart. I would love nothing more than seeing him finally settling into home life, with people who will cherish him just as much as I do!

For the past few weeks, Buck has been front and centre in our big yard play group! This is a great chance for our people-shy new dogs to meet and play with more confident long-stayers like Buck, and he's met a lot of new dogs this way, which suggests that once he's settled into his new home, he might benefit from a dog park or opportunities to meet up with friends.

Buck's best friend is another Romanian dog called Olive. You rarely see one without the other, in their yard, the big yard, or on walks! Sometimes in big yard play group, Bucky and Olive will separate from the other dogs and chase and wrestle each other for a while, and it's lovely to see. Unfortunately, Buck and Olive don't like to be kenneled together as they prefer their own space to unwind after all that time spent playing.

However, Buck has really come out of his shell with people around the rescue. He has a few people he's very close to, and is always up for cwtches with them. How can you say no that handsome face? He's also happier now to meet new people than he used to be, and now goes on walks with volunteers (accompanied, of course, by Olive) most days.

Buck can still get possessive over his favourite people, which is something we have to be aware of in big yard play group and that his adopters will need to bear in mind. He may grumble at other dogs in warning if they get too close when he's having his cuddles, though this does not usually escalate beyond a warning snap. It's likely that our sweet Bucky may not have had stable affection in his past, so he feels the need to guard that love from other dogs.

Luckily for Buck, we have plenty of love to go around at Many Tears! Hopefully, as he settles, he'll realise he is safe and loved and doesn't have to guard anyone anymore.

I’ve had the absolute pleasure of working with Buck, or “Buckaroo” as I like to call him, since the very day he arrived with us. I know you’re not supposed to have favourites, but if I’m honest, Buck has completely stolen a place in my heart.

Buck is such a comical boy, always finding little ways to make you smile, but he is also incredibly affectionate. He has that spark of energy that can turn even the hardest days into better ones.

Buck’s kennel friend, who he came over from Romania with, has recently been adopted. He adored her so much, and since she left, there’s been a little piece of him missing. Now he is the one still waiting, and it is heartbreaking knowing he doesn’t understand why it is not his turn yet.

Although Buck has shared his kennel and enjoys playdates with other dogs, always greeting them nicely out on walks, he would also thrive as the only dog in a home. He loves human attention so deeply and would really benefit from having people around most of the time to give him the love, comfort, and reassurance he deserves.

I recently took Buck out for a day to a local beach. From the moment we arrived, he was in his absolute element and enjoyed every second of it. Buck spent the majority of the time on a long line; although he ran around and explored, he also came back to me when called and always turned to make sure I was still close. This just shows how much of a loyal companion he can be.

I honestly love Buck with my whole heart, and it breaks me a little every single day knowing he is still waiting for his people to come for him. He has so much love, loyalty, and joy to give; he just needs someone to give him that chance.

It’s been a few weeks since Bucks arrival, and oh my has he made his presence known. Every single staff member who has had the pleasure of meeting this boy is utterly obsessed, and it’s very clear as to why!

Buck’s energy is infectious, he is the happiest, bounciest, most adoring little man and whoever adopts him will be truly lucky!!! When you meet him you’d never assume he is 6 years old - he exudes puppy energy.

Buck loves to play with his fellow Romanian buddy Jenny and they get along great. He also goes for play dates with the lovely Orietta, and he thoroughly enjoys it. He would like adopters who have experience with owning dogs before and who are around most of the time.

This sweet sweet boy is absolutely wasted in kennels, he is bursting with love to give and he’ll make a very lucky someone the happiest person in the world. Our foreign dogs are often overlooked and tend to hang around in kennels much longer than needed - please don’t let this be the case for our lovely Buck.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Toby
description:
I need an experienced, adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog and no cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk well on a lead but can be reactive to bikes.

I was born with deformed toes which have been amputated and I have a luxating patella

Toby is a handsome Cocker Spaniel who has been through a lot in his young life and is now looking for a special someone to help him write his next chapter. Originally coming to us from a breeder at just three months old, Toby was a very scared little puppy who found the world overwhelming. Although he found a loving home, he was sadly returned to our care after his adopters felt unable to manage some of his behaviours.

Toby is still a sensitive soul and will need a calm, adult-only home with no visiting children. His new family should have experience with worried or complex dogs and be confident in helping him feel safe. He will need a home without cats as he has met them at the rescue and was too interested. While Toby had previously shown some resource guarding tendencies in his home, we have not seen any guarding behaviour from him while he has been with us. He has spent time in the office with staff members and has been completely comfortable with people coming in and out, which has been lovely to see.

Toby does enjoy playing with tennis balls and can be reluctant to drop them, but this is not a guarding issue. If we offer him a tasty treat in exchange, he is more than happy to swap his ball!

Since returning to us, Toby has come out of his shell beautifully. He greets staff with a wagging tail and absolutely loves attention, affection and food – especially food! Those who work with him absolutely adore him and think he is the most special and wonderful boy.

Toby will be looking for a home where he can be the only dog. He did live with another dog previously and while they got along, he could sometimes guard his adopter's attention, so for this reason he is best suited to being homed as an only dog.

Out and about, Toby enjoys his walks and is lovely on and off the lead. He has good recall and mixes well with other dogs, although he can be reactive to bicycles, so should only be let off lead in safe, secure areas away from the public.

Toby was born with some deformed toes that were later amputated. He has always had a slightly unusual gait due to this, but our vets have noted that he also has a luxating patella, although it may improve with gentle exercise. He also has a naturally short tail, which just adds to his unique charm.

Toby is a sweet, loving boy who truly wants to connect. He has already won the hearts of everyone here, and we're all rooting for him to find a calm, understanding home where he can feel safe, build trust and thrive. If you have the time, patience and experience to offer Toby the gentle guidance he needs, he will reward you with loyalty, love and plenty of cuddles.

Toby has a Grade 1 patella luxation of the left stifle, the vets believe this may be due to age-related osteoarthritis and he has been advised to be placed on joint supplements. However, his adopters will need to be aware of this for any future treatment or medication that may be required as it will not be covered by insurance.

Tobywill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Over the last 3 days and nights, I picked up some night shifts and thought it would be the perfect opportunity to bring Toby into the cabin with me and see what he was really like in a home environment.

When I first brought Toby into the cabin, he settled almost instantly. He had a little explore, took everything in, and then happily climbed onto the sofa, curled up, and went to sleep.

I also wanted to use this time to assess Toby around any guarding behaviours that were mentioned in his previous home, particularly as he was going to be in an environment with sofas, beds, and all those lovely home comforts.

During his second day, Toby found himself a very comfy dog bed. He still had his lead attached, and when I went to remove it, he gave a little grumble and snapped towards my hand. Toby immediately removed himself from the bed and came over to me for reassurance.

This wasthe only guarding behaviour Toby displayed during the entire 3 days, and it was incredibly easy to manage.

Toby is a boy who just needs a home that will understand that he can be a worried boy. If he is happily relaxing on his dog bed, he simply needs to be left alone and given his own space. With this in place, he was a dream throughout his stay.

Whenever I wanted to sit or lie down on the sofa or bed and Toby was already there, I would simply call him off, give him a treat, and then invite him back up once I was settled. Toby also coped brilliantly with being left alone while I went off to do the night rounds. In fact, I’m pretty sure he just slept the whole time!

Toby slept all night in bed with me, and he absolutely loved it. He was so calm, content, and relaxed and, yes, he even snored!

Watching Toby in the cabin has made me realise even more how much love he has to give. This is the side of Toby that I wish everyone could see. I honestly cannot put into words how heartbreaking it was to then put him back into his kennel while he continues to wait for his person to find him.

Toby doesn’t need someone to be perfect. He doesn’t need someone to constantly fuss over him. He simply needs someone who will understand him, give him a little structure, and allow him the time and space to settle.

In return, you get the most gorgeous, loving boy who just wants to be part of your life.

These last 3 days have given me a little glimpse into what Toby’s life should look like! Toby deserves the absolute world. He is an incredibly special boy who just needs someone to understand him!

This week, Toby’s kennel mum celebrated his 1 year anniversary by breaking him out of the rescue for a couple of hours of fun!!Toby travelled good as gold in the car, and happily climbed into the back of the car and had his seatbelt harness fitted with no issues at all.He travelled to Pupstars Paddock with his kennel mum and another staff member who was new to him. He was absolutely brilliant with that staff member who could only sing his praises!!Toby absolutely LOVED the secure field, his tail did not stop wagging, he followed his kennel mum around everywhere and was (very gently) taking treats of both staff members.Once Toby bonds with you, he is the most loyal boy in the world. His circle of trust is only getting bigger, with more and more staff members falling in love with him as time goes on. He may have a stricter criteria than most, but it just means he is just an incredibly special boy in need of a special home. He is such a darling and we wish more people would be able to see it!

Toby’s one year anniversary with us is slowly approaching, and it honestly breaks my heart every day knowing he’s still not curled up on a sofa in a home of his own.

Toby is literally such an amazing dog when he knows you, all he wants to do is spend time with you, whether that be sitting with you, or going out for a gentle stroll!

Recently, I’ve been working on Toby’s lead reactivity, and he’s been doing incredibly well. He’s making such good progress, and I’m so proud of how far he’s come!

I really hope this is the last update I have to write about toby, hopefully his next updates will be coming from his new pawrents, showing us him blossoming in a home and how truly special he really is!

I’ve had the absolute joy of working with Toby for a couple of months now, and he truly is one of my more sensitive, special boys!

Once Toby gets to know you, he turns into the happiest, most affectionate little soul you could ever meet! He absolutely loves zooming around our big play yard, or heading out for a calm, gentle stroll along the lanes taking everything in at his own pace, Toby can be reactive towards passing cars or other dogs, it is something we are currently working on with him!

With the weather getting nicer, I decided it was the perfect day for a little adventure down to the river! To get there, we walk through a huge open field, so I popped Toby on a long line to give him some extra freedom to explore.I don’t think I’ve ever seen a dog so happy he spent most of his time rolling around on his back in the grass with the biggest grin on his face!

When we reached the river, Toby was a little unsure at first. He sat at the edge, watching the water. But after a few minutes of building up his courage, he dipped his paws in and that was it, he was happily paddling back and forth, enjoying every second. It was such a special moment to watch.

I truly adore Toby with my whole heart, he’s one of those dogs who just stays with you, always on your mind.

He can still feel a bit unsure when meeting new people and might bark or back away at first, but give him a little time and patience, and he’ll become your most loyal, loving best friend.

I honestly can’t believe Toby is still waiting for his forever home. He is such a gentle, beautiful soul who deserves the absolute best life has to offer!

Toby is a sweet older gentleman who truly enjoys the quieter side of life. He loves nothing more than snuggling up for a nap and being close to his people.

Toby still has a playful spark and enjoys his daily walks as well as pottering around the yard. He would thrive in a calm, peaceful home and is best suited to a household with no children or cats, where he can relax and enjoy his golden years in comfort.

I love Toby. He is so loved by many of us here at the rescue. He's a confident boy once he knows you, but until he feels comfortable around you he can bark and sometimes be a bit standoffish.

Toby is a big cuddle bunny, he absolutely loves a fuss, and will happily accept butt scratches any time of the day.

He enjoys going out for walks but absolutely loves being off lead and running around the big play yard, when his butt wiggles with happiness and excitement it really doesn't stop, it's super adorable. He likes chasing a tennis ball but he won't bring it back, instead he rolls around with it usually in his mouth and will then lay with it and play with it, he's a comical boy.

Again, once he's comfortable with you he's very easy to handle, I can get a coat or a jumper on him with no problems, I can pick him up and I can brush him with no problems, he had a groom recently and he was no issue at all.

It's a shame he keeps getting overlooked, yes he might have some typical cocker issues such as guarding, but it hasn't been a huge issue since he's been here, I can go in and out of his kennel, pick things up etc and he's been fine. I've also been yarding him with other dogs to try and socialise him more, and although he can be selective of who he likes, once he's found a friend then he just wants to play. He is a beautiful boy inside and out, and in my opinion anyone would be lucky to have him as part of their family.

Also he is kennel clean so house training shouldn't take any time at all.

Please, don't let Toby spend another year in kennels, he truly deserves to find his forever home, as they all do. It's getting colder, it's been snowing, a nice warm, cosy house with a loving family is what he wants, I know his forever home is out there somewhere so please come and find him.

Toby is still doing incredibly well with us here and hasn’t shown any signs of guarding, while this has stopped with us here we still are unsure how he will react in a home environment.

It is an absolute pleasure working with Toby and he always brings a smile to your face throughout the day. Toby is a gentle, loving and happy boy and is desperate to have somebody he can give all his love to.

Toby has definitely come out of his shell since he's been here, he still barks when you first see him but it's a happy bark and his tail doesn't stop, before he would stay for scratches for a little bit, but now he doesn't want to leave you and wants all the attention. He is a very loving dog.

Toby originally came to us from a breeder when he was around 3 months old. He was a terrified puppy who was worried about everything and would even squeak in fear when being handled. He was quickly adopted and found a loving home, but he has sadly been returned to our care as he was displaying some behaviours that his adopters felt unable to cope with.

Toby was homed with another dog and while they got along well, he did show some signs of guarding his adopter from the other dog, for this reason we now think he would be most suited to being homed as an only dog.

Toby can also sometimes grumble if people walk past the sofa or his bed and he is on them, so he will be looking for an adult only home with no visiting children, with adopters who have experience with dogs with similar issues and will be able to work on this with him. He did nip his adopter once around 18 months ago, but that was the only time that resulted in more than a grumble.

Toby is still quite a scared boy in some aspects and certain things will make him extremely nervous, such as the hoover or sometimes even minor things like the sounds of a drawer closing, but with confident owners with experience of scared dogs we do believe he will progress further. He would be best suited to a calm and quiet home, where he can settle in at his own pace and follow a routine.

He enjoys going for walks and is very good both on and off lead. He has good recall and gets along well with other dogs outside of the home. He can be reactive to bikes, so his adopters would need to be mindful of this and keep him on lead in any areas where he may encounter bikes and only let him off lead in secure areas.

As he has lived in a home before, we believe he is house trained, but he may need some reminders.

Toby is a sweet boy at heart and in the right home and with the right adopters we think he will thrive. Since his arrival with us he has been on his best behaviour and already adores all of the staff that work with him and they adore him too. He absolutely loves his food and has a true zest for life which makes us smile each day, so we are so hopeful that his perfect home is out there and will find him soon.

Toby was born with some deformed toes, which have since been amputated but don't seem to bother him, though he does walk with a slightly abnormal gait. He also has a short tail.

name: Orchid
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and will enjoy going on adventures with my new family!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have an undershot jaw and I will be spayed before finding my forever home.

20-09-26 Orchid is a lovely, friendly girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a very affectionate girl who is always happy to come over for some fuss and attention. She is also an inquisitive little lady who enjoys taking an interest in everything going on around her and discovering new things.

Orchid is a fairly confident girl and could potentially be homed as an only dog, provided her adopters are around for most of the day and can give her plenty of company. She also loves the company of other dogs and would be very happy to share her new home with kind doggy friends.

She is looking for a loving home with adopters who have plenty of time to spend with her and who understand that, although she is a confident and friendly girl, she will need time and TLC as she settles in. We would consider homing Orchid with dog savvy children aged 9+.

Orchid has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her and she will need to learn all about house training and her adopters will need to be kind and understanding with this. She can already walk well on a lead and will enjoy going for walks with her new family.

Orchid is such a sweet and affectionate girl with a lovely personality and whoever adopts her is going to adore her.

Our vets have noted that she has an undershot jaw, though this doesn't cause her any issues.

Orchid has been given the Gift of Life by Victoria Griffin

name: Maggie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I can be an only dog or live with one dog my size or larger.

I'd like a secure garden to play in that has 6ft fencing.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been spayed and I’m ready for my new home! Read below for more!

Maggie is a very sweet girl who originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted for around 16 months, but has sadly returned to us from a home following an incident with one of the smaller resident dogs in the home. During the evening, while out in the garden, Maggie was frightened by the other dog barking. Although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight and they struggled to make up or co-exist after this.

Maggie will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and where she can settle in at her own pace. Unfortunately on one occasion in her previous home, Maggie became tangled in her harness and in a panic, bit the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. This was purely through fear and was an isolated, one off incident, but due to this, Maggie will be looking for an adult only home.

When Maggie first returned to our care, she was a very shy girl who was unsure about new people, but since then she has settled in wonderfully and is an absolute dream. She is a very gentle girl who is so loving and confident, especially with her main carer, who has built such an incredible bond with her in a short period of time.

Maggie is now confident enough that we would consider homing her as an only dog in the right circumstances, with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who have plenty of time to spend with her and to help her settle in. She could also live with another calm and confident resident dog, but they would need to be her size or larger. She has shared her kennel with quite a few different dogs since being back with us and she has been amazing with all of them and is happy to share food and toys. She even visits the big play yard with a larger group of dogs for a play date, which she really enjoys!

She is a playful girl and likes to keep herself entertained by playing with a tennis ball by herself, which is very sweet to watch! She does also like to run around and play with some of her dog friends too. She is also very food motivated and loves her treats.

As Maggie has previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with home life, but may need some reminders of house training. She can already walk on a lead and harness and will often check back to you for reassurance. She walks well without pulling and is lovely to take out on walks.

Maggie can be worried by men and did initially bark at the male resident in her previous home, but with time, patience, and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. We are ensuring she socialises with males here and she does have a male staff member as part of her care team and has bonded well with him, which is lovely. She is very people oriented and once she knows you and is comfortable with you, she will become your best friend. She absolutely adores her main carer and will follow her around like a shadow and loves a fuss and cuddle!

Since Maggie has been with us, she has shown that when she feels stressed or overwhelmed, she may try to find a way to escape by climbing. Because of this, she will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft to help keep her safe and prevent any potential escape attempts.

Once Maggie knows and trusts someone, she is a very sweet and happy girl. In the right calm and understanding home, with patient and dog-savvy owners who are willing to let her settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to make wonderful progress and become the most lovely companion.

Maggie aka Magaluf, Magarita, Mags or Miss Maggie is a special girl. She's the kind of dog that once she's comfortable with you, you instantly feel the love she has for you from her and it's such a lovely feeling, she is very affectionate and loves her people more than anything, well, maybe not more than her food or treats but we're her second favourite.

Maggie's confidence has grown so much these past months that she's even helped some of our more shyer residents come out of their shells, and by them seeing how she is with us makes them realise that they too can be like that with us and have fusses and cuddles etc.

She is an incredible girl and it truly baffles me as to why she keeps getting overlooked. She is beautiful both inside and out and has such a fun personality. She is good with other dogs but won't necessarily need to be rehomed with another dog as we believe that she is confident enough to be an only.

Maggie will become a best friend and a true companion, and I know I'm probably a lot biased being one of her kennel mums but she truly is so so special and anyone would be lucky to have her in their life.

Maggie has settled into rescue life beautifully, but having spent over a year in a home, we are really desperate to get her back into one ASAP!

Since her arrival, Maggie has been kenneled with our lovely Bocker Eddie whom she gets along with wonderfully. She does enjoy her time with him, and would happily live alongside one resident dog - male or female, her size or larger!!

During Maggie’s time here she has formed a wonderful bond with her kennel mums who she absolutely dotes on. She’s even bonded with a kennel dad who has said she’s an absolute sweetheart, and he’s had no trouble with her too, which is so good to hear.

Maggie's kennel mummies describe her as loyal, affectionate, and loving. She really looks to them for reassurance, and when they’re around nothing else matters. Seeing as she’s grown so much in confidence, we’re happy to say she can now also be homed as an only dog too in the circumstance her adopters have lots of time to spend with her!!

Maggie isn’t really too fussed on playing with toys, but what she does love is her food & treats so gaining her trust will be a breeze!

A dog like Maggie is absolutely wasted in kennels, she’s already lived a life at home & we are so desperate to get her back into one!!

Maggie is a sweet Cockapoo who originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted for around 16 months, but has sadly returned to us from a home following an incident with one of the smaller resident dogs in the home. During the evening, while out in the garden, Maggie was frightened by the other dog barking. Although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight and they struggled to make up or co-exist after this.

Maggie is a very shy and sensitive girl who is wary of strangers, although she does allow handling. She is trying very hard to be brave and is beginning to show small signs of progress, even getting close to taking treats from our hands, though she is not quite confident enough just yet.

Maggie is not yet confident enough to be an only dog, so we feel she would settle best in a home with one calm and confident resident dog of a similar size or larger, who can help her feel safe and reassured as she adjusts.

As Maggie has previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with the sights and sounds of a home environment. However, she may still need some support with house training as she settles into a new routine. Maggie can already walk on a lead, so she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with the resident dog when she is settled in.

Maggie is particularly worried by men and did initially bark at the male resident in her previous home. With time, patience, and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. Unfortunately, there was also an incident where Maggie became tangled in her harness and, in a panic, bit the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. Because of this, Maggie will need a calm adult-only home with patient and understanding adopters who have experience or understanding of the challenges that can come with rehoming ex-breeding dogs.

Once Maggie knows and trusts someone, she is a very sweet and happy girl. In the right calm and understanding home, with patient and dog-savvy owners who are willing to let her settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to make wonderful progress and slowly come out of her shell.

Maggie is currently being treated for an ear infection in the left ear.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Rizzle
description:
I can live with older dog-savvy children who understand I need time to settle in.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am learning to walk on a harness but may need more time as I heal.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

28-08-26 Rizzle is a quiet and timid girl who has come to us from a breeder. She is beginning to show us just how inquisitive she can be and is trying her hardest to be brave. Rizzle isn’t quite ready to approach us just yet, but she does follow the lead of her doggy friends and takes lots of comfort from having them around. With plenty of TLC, patience and reassurance, we’re sure it shouldn’t take her too long to come around and start showing her lovely personality.

Rizzle will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she begins to gain confidence and learns that the world isn’t such a scary place. She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life, including house training. She will need time to take everything at her own pace and shouldn’t be rushed before she is ready.

Rizzle can live with older, dog-savvy children who are sensible and will understand that she needs time and space to settle in. She is a sweet little lady with so much potential and just needs someone willing to take a chance on her. With a loving home, a confident canine companion and plenty of patience, we’re sure Rizzle will slowly find her confidence and become a wonderful companion.

Rizzle has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Hayley
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and will enjoy going on adventures with my new family!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had an entropion repaired in my right eye.

20-09-26 Hayley is the sweetest, gentlest little girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a little timid, but once she feels safe, she will gently approach you to ask for a little fuss. She has such a lovely, gentle nature and we know that with time, patience and plenty of kindness, she will blossom.

Hayley absolutely loves the company of other dogs and takes a lot of comfort and reassurance from her doggy friends. Because of this, she will need a home with another kind and confident resident dog who can help her to feel safe as she learns about the world around her.

Hayley is looking for adopters with plenty of time to spend with her and previous experience of dogs, who understand that she will need time to settle in to her new home. We feel she would benefit from a quiet, loving home where she can build her confidence and discover how wonderful life can be. We would consider Hayley living with gentle, dog-savvy children aged 9+.

As she has never lived in a home before, her new family will need to give her plenty of time and understanding as she learns all about home life and new skill like house training. She can already walk well on a lead, and will enjoy going for walks with her new family.

Hayley is such a precious, gentle girl who has so much potential. She just needs someone who will give her the time, patience and love she deserves while she learns what it means to be part of a family.

She arrived with an entropion in her right eye, which has been repaired by our vets.

Hayley has been given the Gift of Life by Diane Westwick

name: Gabriel
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I would need to be the only animal in the home.

I may be shy now, but once I have settled I would love a nice garden I can play in!

I love going for walks, and would love an active home!

I know some tricks & walk well on the lead but will need help with housetraining.

I have been neutered and am ready to find my forever home.

Gabriel originally came to us from a breeder, and for him the world felt like a very frightening place. He was worried of people, and new environments and unfamiliar experiences left him feeling overwhelmed. Even something as simple as having a lead put on was a huge challenge. He needed time, patience and gentle encouragement to begin to feel safe.

Gabriel was adopted for a short period, but unfortunately it was not the right fit for him. He was returned after displaying unwanted behaviours in the home and making the wrong choices when he felt uncomfortable in a situation, which did result in Gabriel biting. He will need a quiet, adult-only home without resident or visiting children. Gabriel can struggle with visitors coming to the house, so he will need a home without too many visitors and where he can be placed in a separate room when people do come over. His adopters will also need to be willing to meet him multiple times before adoption so that he has the opportunity to develop a bond and build trust with them.

Gabriel is a very sensitive boy who feels anxious about a lot of things. During his time here we are trying to help him feel more comfortable by giving him the tools to know how to be more relaxed in these scary situations. To Gabriel, new people are very scary and he feels that he needs to tell them to go away by barking and lunging, when put in poor situations this has led to him having a bite history. He is a very sweet dog but he has very little he trusts in this world and unfortunately humans are top of that list at the moment. With people who have earned his trust he is exceptionally sweet and loving, he loves to give you cuddles and he really thinks he should be a lap dog. When introductions are done slowly and in a manner that he can cope with he will allow that person into his circle reasonably quickly and then he gets very excited to see them.

As he has had very little in this world he does become exceptionally attached to his trusted humans and doesn't like to share them with other dogs or other people, so he is looking for a home with a maximum of two people and will need to be the only dog in the home. Adopters with experience of guarding behaviours are essential to help him succeed in his next home and make sure it really will be his forever home.

Gabriel walks nicely on his harness and gets very excited to see dogs when out and about but is wary of strangers walking past, for this reason he is muzzled when out as it keeps him safe in the event of someone getting too close or trying to touch him.

He has shown signs of resource guarding his food here and any high value long lasting treats. He has Kongs as he is happy for the empty Kong to be removed from his kennel once he feels he's finished with it, but these are things that will have to be managed in his new home. It would be a good idea to limit his access to the kitchen in the home to avoid the possibility of him getting things that he may be inclined to guard, especially until he settles and the bond has been built with him to ensure that he trusts that you won't take things away from him without him getting something higher value in its place.

Gabriel socialises well with other dogs here and does enjoy chasing dogs around our big play yard here, so having the opportunity to continue making friends with playful dogs in his new home is necessary to keep him happy and help him to continue to grow in confidence. Someone will be incredibly lucky to have Gabriel as their companion, they will just have to understand that he does require the time and effort to make sure he progresses and starts to see the world is less scary than he thinks it is.

Gabriel will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Today I got to spend more time with Gabriel than I usually would so I took advantage of that and we went for a much longer walk.... As usual he was brilliant, he listens, if we need to move out of the way for a car he'll listen to me and move off the road to the side, if he's walking slightly ahead and I call him he stops and turns back.

We also sat around the other side of the rescue where it's usually busier as I want to get him used to being in busier areas and being around people he doesn't know, as he can be a bit reactive.... He did so well, it was fairly busy so he was a little unsure at first but the longer we stayed the better he was, he was good with others around him too, he has come such a long way, but this is something I'm going to keep on working on with him for the foreseeable as we don't know what life he'll have outside of here and he may need to used to busier areas.

We also played with a puzzle feeder today, which he decided would be fun to pick up with his mouth and drop it on the floor to get the treats out faster, he really is a funny boy, but he's super smart too and is quick to pick up tricks especially when there's treats involved.

He really is every Bocker lovers dream and he always gets so overlooked.

He is muzzle trained, and would need to wear his muzzle when meeting new people, dogs or at the vets, but he's also just a big softy who gives the loveliest cwtches and kisses, to be a part of his gang is such an amazing feeling and he shows his affection for you so clearly when he loves you.

This week we’ve had a heatwave which has meant alot of our rescue dogs have needed their ears checked incase they’ve had any mucky build up - Gabriel was one of the unlucky few that have needed some TLC in this area!!We’ve recently had a new meds person who has been visiting Gabriel to do his ear cleans & he has been an absolute angel. He’s even been given the nickname Angel GabrielIt’s just a testament to Gabriel that yes he can be unsure of new people, but once he knows you he truly is such a wonderful boy. He just needs someone to take that chance on him, show him the love he’s desperate to have & he’ll return it tenfold.Gabriel has been waiting such a long time now, and seeing a boy so full of love & hope is heartbreaking when we can’t reassure him that his time will come soon!!!

Today, I worked with Gabriel again for the first time in months. I was a little worried he’d have forgotten, however, it’s safe to say the bond previously made still remains.Gabriel is such an excited little boy. He lives for treats. He’s such a clever and obedient boy when the treats come out. Usually, he’s full of energy and excitement. Once the treats are out, he’s still and sits like the perfect little boy we know he can be.As he can be very busy, I’ve always thought it essential to take him out on walks, the longer the better. As mentioned in a previous update, he loves walks! Once you pull the lead out, you get a similar reaction to the treats.The longer the walk the better. Walks are so good for this gorgeous boy. They keep him stimulated and help shave off the pounds he gains from everyone giving him treats!On the whole, I was so happy to see my boy again. So happy, so loyal, keen to go on walks and he listened so well. I’m so proud of the progress he’s made since I last saw him!Gabriel still can be a challenge and, he does not like everyone. Once you’ve made that bond with him though, it stays. Don’t overlook this boy. He’s such a beautiful, intelligent and fun dog!

This boy has my heart, once you form that special bond with him I do believe it's for life. He is very loving and enjoys a cuddle and a fuss from people he feels comfortable around, as his adopter you'll hopefully get that bond through spending time with him and letting him go at his own pace.Gabriel, as most bockers do, lives for his food and treats, whenever I run him in from being in the yard I always leave a small treat in his bed or somewhere in the back for him to find, and he absolutely loves this he gets so excited knowing he'll get a treat and runs straight to the back of his kennel to find it.He loves his walks and his time in the big yard. He's the curious, adventurous type who just wants to investigate everything, a 10 minute stroll up the road can take us an extra 20-25 minutes to stroll back because he likes to explore, but I don't mind, seeing him happy makes me happy I'd never want to stop him from exploring the world.Gabriel would need an experienced, adult only home (view profile for explanation), he would need someone who is active and can provide him with mental and physical stimulation daily. He is a very smart boy and can pick things up quite quickly which is why, with the help from some treats I think he would pick up toilet training rather quickly.Please don't overlook this handsome guy just because he's not your small and fluffy type dog, Gabriel is a special boy with a lot of love to give, and for that right person/people he would become a true companion and best friend.

Gabriel, a stunning Bocker with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. This handsome boy is full of life and enthusiasm, always ready to embrace whatever the day brings. Gabriel thrives on affection and absolutely loves a good fuss and cuddle — he’s a real people-dog who enjoys being close to those he trusts.

Gabriel is a clever lad with so much potential. He’s already showing us just how intelligent he is as he responds to basic commands! With the right guidance and training , we know he’ll flourish and continue to grow in confidence, not that he lacks any confidence! He also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out on adventures.

Sadly, Gabriel has been returned to us, and we are now searching for the right forever home where he can truly settle and feel secure. Gabriel would be best suited as an only dog, in a calm and quiet home environment. We are looking for a home with minimal visitors and no children, as busy households can feel overwhelming for him.

Gabriel can display guarding behaviours, so he will need experienced owners who understand this and can manage the home environment appropriately to support him. With the right knowledge, structure, and patience, Gabriel will thrive and continue to build trust.

Gabriel has so much love to give to the right person. With understanding, consistency, and kindness, he will make an incredibly loyal and devoted time

Gabriel is a stunning Bocker who is full of life, love, and character! This gorgeous boy is bursting with energy and adores nothing more than a good fuss and a cwtch.He’s incredibly smart, and we just know it wouldn’t take long for him to be trained to a very high standard – he’s already showing us how bright he is every day. Gabriel also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out and about.Now all he needs is a forever family who can give him the love, attention, and adventures he deserves. With his brains, energy, and big heart, Gabriel is sure to make someone the most wonderful companion.

Gabriel has come to us from a breeder and has made incredible progress since arriving with us! When he first came, he was nervous around new people and worried about having a lead put on, which made walks and new kennel staff introductions a real challenge. Now, he gets excited for walk time and happily allows us to put on both his lead and harness with no issues.This handsome boy is a true foodie and loves learning new tricks. He already knows “sit” and “paw,” so with trust and patience, teaching him more tricks should be a fun and rewarding experience. Gabriel needs a confident, experienced, owner who will provide clear boundaries and structure, as he can be cheeky if he thinks he’s in charge as well as an adult-only home where he can continue to learn. Gabriel has the confidence to be an only dog in a home with can allow him the dedication and time he needs and will need a home with no cats or small furries.Once Gabriel knows and trusts you, he is affectionate, loyal, and loves nothing more than sharing his goofy charm. Underneath his shy moments, he is a beautiful boy with a heart full of love. He is looking for someone who will continue his training, set clear rules, and enjoy all the affection, loyalty, and joy he has to give.

name: Sophie
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 16+ who respect my space.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

i have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

27-08-26 Sophie is a very sweet-natured and placid girl who has come to us from a breeder. She is a gentle soul who doesn’t quite have the confidence to approach you just yet and instead follows her kennel friends around for comfort and reassurance. Sophie looks to them to help her feel safe, and she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can lean on as she continues to grow in confidence and learn to trust the people around her.

Sophie has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life. She is working with her kennel mummy on harness training and would like to continue this in her new home. Some gentle garden sniffs and exploring in a secure garden will be a great place to start while she builds her confidence and learns that the world can be a lovely place.

Sophie can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are kind and sensible and can offer her the calm and quiet environment she needs to settle in. Her new family will need to give her plenty of time, patience and reassurance and allow her to progress at her own pace. With the support of her resident dog and lots of love, we’re sure Sophie will slowly begin to find her confidence and show everyone what a lovely girl she really is.

Sophie has been given the Gift of Life by Candice Sullivan

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Ollie
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I've started my vaccinations and will be neutered before adoption.

17-09-26 Ollie is a very nervous boy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. Despite retreating to the corner of his kennel and showing us just how scared he is, Ollie is okay being handled and will accept a gentle fuss, although he shakes like a leaf. He very much wants to be brave and has allowed us to clean around his eyes and give him some gentle fuss, but we can see just how hard he is trying to cope with these new experiences.

Ollie will need another kind and confident dog in his new home, and this dog will be a much-needed support system for him as he settles in and begins to understand that he is safe. As Ollie has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. His adopters will need to be patient and give him plenty of time to adjust at his own pace.

Ollie could share his home with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home, as well as his own space where he can retreat and settle in. His adopters will need to have experience with ex-breeders to better understand his needs.

Ollie is a sweet boy who is trying so hard despite how frightened he feels. We hope that with the support of a confident canine companion, patient adopters and plenty of kindness, he will slowly begin to find his confidence and realise that the world is a much kinder place than he has known.

Ollie has been given the Gift of Life by Diane Bentley

name: Odette
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a Grade 2 heart murmur & I will be spayed.

17-09-26 Odette is a heartbreaking little girl who has come into our care from a breeder and is not coping well with her new surroundings right now.

She is absolutely terrified and very shut down, so she needs slow, careful handling and plenty of patience. At the moment, she mostly tries to bury her head in her bed when you interact with her and has been too frightened to eat unless she is left alone somewhere quiet. Despite this, we are already starting to see a little improvement, which is encouraging.

Odette will need another kind and confident dog in her new home, and this dog will be a much-needed support system for her as she learns to trust and gains confidence.

As Odette has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to understand that this will take time and that she will need to progress at her own pace.

Odette has a Grade 2 heart murmur which does not appear to be bothering her.

name: Luca
description:
I'd like an active home and enjoy human company!

I’d like to be the only dog in the home. I can't live with cats or small furries!

I will need a large secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I walk well on a lead, although I can pull. I am learning to walk with a muzzle.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home! I have had 1 tooth extracted.

Luca is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a fresh start. He already knows his name very well, so it would be nice if his adopters kept his name.

Luca was previously spent most of his life living outdoors, but beneath his impressive appearance is a real softie. He is easy to handle and genuinely enjoys human company, although he understandably found kennel life quite stressful when he first arrived and would often pace his kennel and the exercise yard, struggling to settle.

As Luca has become familiar with the routine, his surroundings and the staff at Many Tears, his confidence has grown enormously. One of the biggest changes we have seen is his newfound love of toys. For the first couple of weeks, he showed no interest in them at all, but now he absolutely adores them! His favourite game is a good game of fetch in the big yard, where he happily charges after his ball with great enthusiasm.

Like many large, playful dogs, Luca can occasionally become overexcited during play. He may jump up to catch the ball or become a little mouthy in his excitement. He is a gentle boy who simply gets carried away when he is having fun. Because of his size and strength, we are helping him learn commands such assit,waitanddrop, as well as encouraging calmer play so he can enjoy himself without becoming overstimulated. This training will be important for his future adopters to continue, as an overexcited Luca could unintentionally knock over someone who is less steady on their feet.

Although he loves chasing a ball, Luca's absolute favourite toys are cuddly toys! He delights in carrying them around and showing off his softer side, which perfectly sums up his character. He really is a big, lovable boy with a wonderfully playful personality.

For now, Luca will need to be the only dog in his home. He has not been kennelled with any other dogs while with us and currently does not mix with them. Luca has had very little basic socialisation with other dogs throughout his life, so we are putting a muzzle-training plan in place with the aim of eventually being able to carefully trial him around other dogs. Until we know more, however, he must remain an only dog and his adopters will need to understand and respect this.

When out walking, Luca can pass other dogs well when they are at a suitable distance, but if another dog barks at him or comes too close, he can become reactive and may get worked up enough to grab at the lead. His future adopters will therefore need to be confident and experienced handlers who are willing to continue his muzzle training and carefully manage his environment. We would consider homing him with dog-savvy older teenagers aged 16+.

Luca is actually very settled when he is in his kennel on his own. He happily lies down in his bed surrounded by his favourite toys and is content to relax, which is a lovely contrast to how unsettled he was when he first arrived.

Luca already walks on a lead, although he can pull initially, so this is something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an active, intelligent boy who would love a home where he can enjoy plenty of adventures, enrichment and quality time with his people. He is also a very strong dog who can jump and even open gates, so he will need a very secure garden and confident handlers who can safely manage his strength.

As Luca has spent most of his life outdoors, he will need to learn about house training and the other basics of home life, and his adopters will need to be patient and understanding while he learns. With consistency, kindness and plenty of encouragement, we are sure he will adapt well and enjoy discovering all the comforts that a family home has to offer. He is laid-back and loves to relax, so we think he will really enjoy home life.

Luca is an affectionate, loyal and wonderfully characterful boy. Now that he has settled and his playful personality has begun to shine, it has been a joy to watch him embrace life. In the right home, with structure, ongoing training and plenty of love, Luca will make an incredibly rewarding companion.

Luca has had one tooth extracted at the time of his neuter.

Luca has been given the Gift of Life by Lynne Hughes

Before they arrive at Many Tears, many of our dogs have never had toys, and, as strange as it sounds, may not know what to do with them. Fetching, licking, and chewing are important forms of enrichment for dogs and can help to regulate their nervous system and reduce stress, but it can take a while for these dogs to figure out how to use toys in these ways. It's one of the reasons many of our dogs are recommended to have a resident dog at home, as they can learn from each other.

When Luca arrived, he did not engage with toys for the first two weeks or so. He was also very anxious, pacing his kennel and the yard and struggling to settle. However, as he has become used to the routine, surroundings, and staff at Many Tears, Luca has settled very well and discovered a love of all sorts of toys!

We try to give our dogs a mix of toys and enrichment until we know what they like. Luca is not very interested in food-based enrichment like LickiMats or Kongs. He will tug-of-war hesitantly with a rope toy but doesn't really engage with it. However, Luca LOVES a game of fetch down the big yard. He may occasionally jump up to try and get the ball and become over-excited and mouthy, so we are working on balancing his stimulation so he can get his energy out without getting worked up, and on commands like "sit", "wait", and "drop". Luca is incredibly gentle and does not want to hurt anyone, but he is a big boy and could knock a vulnerable person down if he gets too over-excited, so this kind of training is important.

Luca's FAVOURITE type of toy, though, is cuddly toys! It just proves what a big softie he is, as he really loves nothing more than carrying around his stuffed pig toy or cwtching up with his favourite, a string of stuffed Brussels sprouts. It's really lovely to see him relax and enjoy himself this way. Even better when he's doing it on your lap!

Luca is loved by all the staff and volunteers who meet him, but he's definitely ready to be someone's best friend.

Luca is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a fresh start. He already knows his name very well, so his new adopters should keep this the same to avoid confusing him as he settles into his new life.

Luca was previously used as a fake security dog and has spent most of his life living outside, but beneath his big appearance he is a real softie. He is easy to handle and enjoys human company, though he has understandably found kennel life quite stressful and will often plead with us to come back when we have to leave him.

Luca would be happiest and thrive best as the only dog in the home, where he can enjoy all the attention, settle more easily into a routine, and build a strong bond with his new family. He will need adopters who have plenty of time to spend with him and who have experience of the breed or similar breeds. Luca cannot live with cats or small furries and he cannot be around small dogs.

As Luca has spent most of his life outdoors, he will need to learn about house training and the other basics of home life. He will need patient adopters who can help guide him through these new experiences as he adjusts to living in a home environment.

Luca can already walk on a lead, though he does pull at first and so this is something his adopters will need to work on with him. He is a very active boy, so he would love an active household where he can enjoy plenty of adventures and become a loyal companion once he is settled in. He is a strong dog and can both jump and open gates, so he will need a very secure garden and confident handlers who are able to manage his strength safely.

Luca is an intelligent, affectionate, and loyal boy who simply wants to be close to his people. In the right home, with structure, companionship, and plenty of love, he will make an incredibly rewarding companion.

Luca has had 1 tooth extracted at the time of his neuter.
