name: River
description:
I need an experienced, adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog, but I have lived with another dog. See more below.

I would like a secure garden in a quiet area.

I can walk well on a lead and would like an active home.

I need experienced adopters to work on my reactivity with me.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

River originally came into our care in 2020 from a breeder and was adopted into a loving home. Sadly, her family later found they were unable to continue meeting her needs, and River has now returned to us.

River is a highly intelligent, affectionate girl who forms very strong bonds with her people. According to her previous home, once she feels safe she is extremely loving, enjoys close contact and seeks reassurance from those she trusts. She loves cuddles, gentle scratches, and being near her humans, and is very in tune with their emotions, often offering comfort when someone is feeling down.

River is a clever and enthusiastic learner who already knows a wide range of cues and enjoys training, enrichment and mental stimulation. She loves her toys, especially balls and tug toys, enjoys scent games such as “find it”, and is very food-motivated, peanut butter is her absolute favourite! She settles well at home, enjoys routine and structure, and is clean and non-destructive.

River enjoys her walks and would suit an active home with access to quieter walking routes. She walks nicely on a halti and enjoys being out and about, but can find busy environments overwhelming and may be reactive to dogs, vans or motorbikes when anxious. She will need confident handling and continued training, and should remain on lead unless in a secure area.

Although affectionate and loving, River is a sensitive dog and can struggle with unfamiliar people, visitors and loud or sudden noises such as fireworks. When frightened she may bark or retreat. For this reason, River is looking for acalm, quiet, adult-only homewithvery few visitors, ideally in arural or semi-rural setting. Her adopters must beexperienced with reactive dogs, patient, and willing to work at her pace while respecting her boundaries.

We are advised that River can occasionally display guarding behaviours towards her trusted humans, such as growling if another person enters the room while she is settled. This will need calm, confident and experienced management.

River is currently looking for a home as anonly dog, although she has previously lived with another small dog and may be able to live with a calm companion following careful introductions.

River may not be suited to everyone, but for the right home she will be an incredibly loyal, affectionate and rewarding companion who has so much love to give.

A bit about River from her previous home:

Riverwill need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

River is honestly the sweetest girl once she knows and trusts you.

Recently, I’ve been taking River around our reception area and spending some quiet time with her, helping her learn that people she doesn’t know don’t have to be scary.

River is now happily taking treats from numerous members of staff she doesn’t know, something that might seem so small to some, but for River and everyone who knows her it’s a massive achievement!!

Once River lets you into her world and that special bond is built, she will be your best friend for life. She has so much love to give; she just needs someone willing to take the time to earn it!

I really, really hope River’s people find her soon. It’s heart breaking to see such a loving girl waiting in kennels when I know just how much happiness she could bring to someone’s life.

River may need a little time to trust you, but i can promise you, she will be worth every second.

Just wanted to share quick update for our wonderful River! Her kennel mum has been working on showing River that visiting the vets isn’t always a scary ordeal. Today, I popped in with her to see how it was going. I was SO impressed!

Although she was hesitant to come in, once in the vets she settled enough to have the biggest cuddles (River gives the BEST cuddles). We spent 5 minutes or so telling her how beautiful and amazing she is and made sure to head out before she got too worried.

River is honestly one of those special, once in a lifetime dogs. Once she bonds with you, she has this incredible ability to make you feel like the most important person in the world. She gives you her whole heart. Whoever adopts her will be so lucky to have her in their life!

Our gorgeous girl River is still on the search for a new home and family and hopefully her forever one. River is continuing to do very well here at the rescue and has progressed so much since being back with us.

Having lived in a home River knows a lot of commands and has been very well taught. She's clean in her kennel and isn't destructive at all. Although, she has lived in a home before she does still struggle at times with busy environments and people she doesn't know. When shes greeted by someone she doesn't know she will bark out of uncertainty but if you offer her a treat she tends to make friends with you pretty quickly. There were only a couple of people who could work with River initially when she came back to us due to her being so overwhelmed and worried but now half the rescue can work with her so shes made massive progress and I couldn't be any prouder of her.

She walks lovely on the lead and absolute loves going out for walks or down the big yard where she also loves to play fetch. We have been training River to understand that going to the vets isn't all that scary. We have been desensitising her by walking her up the vet steps and just sitting there for a moment praising her. Before, she wouldn't even go up the steps so for her to do this and sit there for a moment is massive for her. Our next step will be to open the vets door and go from there. River is such a special girl and when she trusts you she loves you with her whole heart and she genuinely does make you feel so loved. Being Rivers Kennel Mum is honestly the best and having all that love and affection from her is just utterly amazing.

River is continuing to do incredibly well here and is trusting more and more people she meets each day. It’s been lovely to see her confidence grow as she builds good relationships with other people. As part of her ongoing desensitisation, we’ve been walking River around the front of the rescue and gradually up towards the vets. This helps her learn that these environments are safe and nothing to worry about. Throughout this training we give her plenty of praise and tasty treats, and she is responding really well.

Considering everything she’s working through, she’s doing brilliantly. River is muzzle and Halti trained, as she can be reactive to certain dogs and can be strong when she first heads out on walks. We are working on her reactivity daily, and she is improving.

Her future adopters will need to continue with this training to help her keep progressing and feeling secure. River is an absolute darling. She has such a loving nature and truly makes you feel so loved when you spend time with her. With the right support and understanding, she would make a wonderful companion and a very special addition to the right home

River is a gentle girl who has previously lived in a home and is already kennel clean, giving her a great foundation for her next chapter. She can be a little cautious with new people at first, but with time and patience, she soon shows her sweet, affectionate side. Once she trusts you, River forms a lovely bond and just wants to be close to her people. She’s looking for a kind, understanding home that will give her the reassurance and love she deserves.

I love my walks so one or two a day would be great!

While she can still be sensitive and appreciates having her space respected, it’s clear that Crumble simply needed time to feel safe. With gentle reassurance and plenty of TLC, her true personality is beginning to shine through. She is a gentle soul who responds best to calm, kind interactions and slow introductions.

She would be happiest and thrive best as the only dog in the home, where she can enjoy all the attention, settle more easily into a routine, and build a strong bond with her new family.

As she has never lived in a home environment before, she will need patient support with house training and learning everyday routines. She will need a home without cats as she is overly interested.

We are looking for an experienced, adult-only home where Crumble can continue to build her confidence at her own pace. A quiet household with understanding adopters who are happy to let her take things slowly will allow her to truly flourish. With the right people, time, and lots of love, Crumble will make a wonderfully rewarding companion.

On arrival, our vets noted that Crumble had a Grade 2 luxating patella. During her time with us she has shown very intermittent lameness, mostly only seen when she’s getting up from laying down for a long time. She was sent for x-rays which showed potential damage to her left cruciate ligament, as well as hip dysplasia in her right hip. She is currently managing very well with rest and pain relief, and we will work on building correct muscle tone to support her as well as slow introductions to controlled exercise and physio.

Crumble is the most incredible girl who loves her humans once she has bonded with you. She has such a huge personality and makes all of her kennel mums and dads laugh every single day.

She absolutely loves playing with her best friend Criss Cross and she loves splashing in water when it's warm weather.

She's one of those exceptional girls who will make someone incredibly lucky and give them so much love and fun once they've put in the time to earn her trust and build that bond with her.

There’s not a bad word you could say about this girly pop. She is goofy, affectionate, playful, friendly and gaining confidence by the day! She has been trying her best to be kennel clean, no encouragement needed.

She is a staff favourite and that girls little teefys are part of her personality! Nibbling at you to show you just how much she loves to play with you, entertains her pal Criss cross and her kennel mums in the yard.

She belongs in a home where her people can show her the best doggy life imaginable while also understanding that Crumble has also not known much of the world and requires a bit of patience and care when handling her.

Taking every opportunity to play and zoom around with her best friend, Criss Cross.Her confidence is growing and enjoying her walks and greeting new people at her own free will as long as she is guaranteed some fuss or treats.

She enjoys sprawling out on the floor with her chew toy just enjoying the vibes.When she finds her home she will be very eager in sharing her affectionate nature with her family

Crumble is becoming a very happy chow now and has recently discovered that there's no limit on zoomies. She does get along with her chow friend, Criss Cross, but isn't keen on other dogs, so is looking for a home as an only. She is wary of people initially, but once you've gained her trust she becomes your absolute best mate. She loves her walks and gets very excited when she sees you bringing her harness towards her. She's a big foodie too and loves treats.

Crumble is coming on so beautifully and it truly makes my heart melt. Today we had some cuddle and play time in her kennel, and it was such a special moment. For a girl who once wasn’t very happy with touch, she’s now rolling over for belly rubs, snuggling in her bed, and even playing “paw paw” with me.

She’s also learning about wearing a harness and is improving every day. If you have a Crumble shaped hole in your life, she really is something special.

Crumble is a worried lady who came into our care from a breeder, searching for a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was very worried and unsure of the world around her, but with time and patience she has begun to settle beautifully. Crumble is now much less fearful of us humans and has really started to come out of her shell, choosing to engage more with staff members and showing curiosity about her surroundings.

Crumble will need a confident and friendly resident dog who can help guide her and show her the ropes. As she has never lived in a home environment before, she will need patient support with house training, lead walking, and learning everyday routines. But will need to take things slow to start with some garden sniffs adventures on the lead may be too scary to start.

Crumble has a previous bite wound inside her ear, which is currently being treated.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Monet
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have had 12 teeth extracted at the time of my spay.

Monet is a very worried little lady who came to us from a breeder and was understandably very worried when she arrived. She relied heavily on the other dogs around her for comfort and reassurance and could be very skittish when approached and was in need of lots of TLC.

Monet has now been in a wonderful foster home for a few weeks and, although the first couple of days were very stressful for her, she is slowly starting to settle and discover the comforts of home life for the first time ever. Initially, she spent much of her time pacing around the house and garden, but she is now making progress in little baby steps.

She takes much of her confidence from the resident dogs in her foster home and loves following them into the garden and cuddling up with them on their beds or the sofa. She sleeps quietly downstairs on the sofa with her canine friends and is happiest when her whole pack is together. She is curious and likes to keep an eye on everything that is happening.

Monet had never lived in a home before moving to foster and is doing well with her house training, mostly taking herself outside during the day, but her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she continues to learn in her new home.

While Monet is becoming more comfortable in her surroundings, she remains very flighty and fearful and is not yet comfortable with handling or being stroked. As she is still quite worried about being handled, she can panic if she feels overwhelmed or pushed out of her comfort zone and may become distressed and choose to make the wrong decision in her fear. For this reason, harness training has not yet begun. She also has a remarkable ability to spring into action when frightened, so her future home will need a very secure garden with tall fences.

Monet will need an adult-only home and will need at least one other kind, confident resident dogs that she can rely on. Her adopters will need experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and, most importantly, the time, patience and understanding to allow Monet to build her confidence and trust at her own pace.

She is still very much at the beginning of her journey, but seeing her starting to settle, follow her canine friends and enjoy some of the comforts of home life is lovely progress. With the right family and plenty of patience, we hope that Monet will continue to blossom and that, in time, her sweet personality will shine through.

Monet has had 12 teeth extracted and would benefit from a soft food diet.

Monet has been given the Gift of Life by June Torgersen

Monet is a gentle little lady who has been in a foster home for a few weeks. She found the first couple of days very stressful and spent her time pacing in the house and garden ‘howling to the moon’. Thankfully she has started to settle and learn about home life and comforts.

Monet is making progress in baby steps but can easily become flighty and fearful, she will need a very secure garden as she has springs on her paws. Don’t underestimate how high a skittish Bichon can jump!

Monet will take herself out to the garden for toileting, follows the resident dogs out to chase pigeons and cuddles up to them in their beds or on the sofa. For a couple of days she sat on the same sofa as the fosterer and resident dogs but she has not repeated that this week. She is clean in the house during the day (door is open) she has had some accidents overnight but it’s still early days.

She is curious, watches everything and needs to know where her human is and is unhappy if her pack is not all together. She sleeps quietly at night downstairs on the sofa with the resident dogs, she does not use a crate.

Monet enjoys her food and s being fed by hand to help build trust but will not accept handling or stroking at present and for this reason harness training has not started.

Monet needs an adult only, calm but active multi dog home with adopters who have experience of scared ex breeding dogs with the time and patience to gain Monet’s trust at her pace.

Monet is a very timid little lady who has come to us from a breeder and relies heavily on her canine friends for comfort and reassurance. She is easy enough to handle but can be quite skittish when approached, so she will need plenty of time, patience, and TLC to help her build her confidence.

Monet will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can rely on as she begins to trust, learn about companionship, and discover that the world isn't such a scary place. As Monet has never lived in a home before, she will need a calm and quiet, adult-only home will be patient as she learns about house training, walking on a lead, and all the other basics of home life.

Monet is a very sweet little lady who simply needs a kind and understanding family willing to give her the time she deserves. As her confidence continues to grow, we're sure her lovely personality will shine through.

name: Lucy
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

27-08-26 Lucy is a very worried lady who has come to us from a breeder and is understandably nervous around people. She can be quite vocal when approached and doesn’t yet enjoy being handled, she prefers to keep her distance while she works out that people can be trusted. Lucy is a sweet girl underneath her worries and will need plenty of TLC, patience and understanding from her new family as she begins to build her confidence.

Lucy is very active and playful with her kennel friends, and this is where we get to see a little more of her personality. She would love a home that can offer her an active lifestyle once she has had time to settle and feel comfortable. She will also need at least one kind and confident resident dog who she can look to and lean on for reassurance as she learns about home life and gains confidence.

Lucy has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. These things may take some time, and she will need a family who is willing to go at her pace without putting pressure on her. Lucy will need an adult-only home with ex-breeding experience, where her needs will be understood and she can have the time and space she needs to blossom. With patience, love and the support of a confident canine friend, we hope Lucy will slowly learn to trust and show us the wonderful girl hiding underneath her worries.

Lucy has been given the gift of life by Linda Towers

name: Rachel
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I have had a pea size cyst removed from my right shoulder at the time of spay.

Rachel is a very scared girl who has come to us from a breeder. When she first arrived she was extremely overwhelmed by her new surroundings and clearly hadn’t had much socialisation or handling before. Since being with us, she has slowly started to show small signs of progress as she begins to realise she is safe. Although she still finds being handled very frightening, her kennel mum can now stroke her gently when she's in her bed at the back of the kennel.

She will need a calm and quiet adult-only homewith adopters experienced with traumatised ex-breeding dogs who can provide the reassurance and stability she needs to continue building her confidence and learning about trust and kindness. Her adopters will need to allow her to settle in at her own pace and let her set the speed of her progress as she can still become easily overwhelmed.

Rachel relies on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and help her settle into her new home. They will need to be happy to snuggle up with her and to let her rely on them for support. For some reason she is especially fond of Dachshunds, but she does love all dogs. When she forms a bond with another dog, she absolutely dotes on them and becomes the most loyal best friend to them. It’s so sweet to see.

Day to day, she is a super happy and laid back girl. She LOVES toys and spends a lot of her time chewing on a bone or playing with a plush teddy in one of her beds. She also really loves her food and this has been a great help in gaining her trust and forming a bond with her.

Rachel has never lived in a home before, so she will need very patient and understanding adopters while she settles in and learns all about home life and new skills like house training.She follows a daily routine beautifully, happily running out to the exercise yards and returning to her kennel when it is time to come back in. She is not currently 100% kennel clean, but she is likely to take to toilet training well in a home, as she toilets almost immediately when she goes out into the yard. Her adopters will need to give her plenty of opportunities to go outside while she learns the new routine. Rachel doesn't walk on a lead or harness just yet, but hopefully in the future this is something that we can introduce to her.

The big wide world still feels quite scary for Rachel, but she is beginning to show curiosity in safe environments, and gentle time in the garden will be a great way to help her slowly explore and build confidence. She is not yet cat tested, but we feel cats are unlikely to be an issue for her, although this would need to be assessed appropriately.

Although Rachel has been making progress and will now allow her kennel mum to gently stroke her when she's in a bed in the back of her kennel, she still doesn't enjoy this. She finds being picked up extremely frightening and will panic and does have the potential to bite purely out of fear, so it is imperative that her adopters fully understand her behaviour and are confident managing her needs. We really don’t think she’ll be this way forever, and she’ll get better and better as time goes on, but it would be a lot easier if she was in a home with someone who knew how to help her.

Recently, Rachel needed to have her thick coat clipped during the warm weather, which unfortunately had to be done under sedation as she is not yet ready to be groomed. Despite how frightening this experience must have been for her, she coped far better than we ever expected, allowing herself to be carried to the vets and held for her injection once she was safely in our arms. We couldn't have been prouder of how brave she was. As her coat grows back, we will continue gently introducing her to grooming so she can slowly learn that being brushed doesn't have to be scary.

Rachel has so much potential and, with time, patience and kindness, we truly believe she will continue to make progress and learn that she is safe and loved. She really is an easy dog to care for in every other aspect – she is wonderful with other dogs, thrives on routine and never puts a paw wrong. She just needs a truly understanding home where she can continue building on the trust she has started to develop and finally blossom into the dog she is meant to be.

Rachel came to us with a pea-sized cyst on her shoulder, which was removed at the time of her spay.

Rachel has been given the Gift of Life by Tracy Davidson

Rachel (or Rachy as I call her) has had quite a few updates on her page now, so I thought I’d do something a little different with this one and basically summarise her and the type of home she needs!

Rachy is a super happy and laid back girl day to day. She LOVES toys and spends a lot of her time chewing on a bone or playing with a plush teddy in one of her beds. She also loves other dogs - especially Dachshunds!! We have no idea why, but she lights up when she’s around them. When she forms a bond with another dog, she absolutely dotes on them and becomes the most loyal best friend to them. It’s so sweet to see. She also loves her food (probably more than anything), and this has been a massive help in gaining her trust and forming a bond with her. She runs to the play yard from her kennel, and back in with no problems, and she also toilets as soon as she gets to the yard every time, so I have a feeling it won’t take long to house train her at all.

Rachy is very easy to look after at the rescue and follows routine beautifully. If you didn’t know anything about her, she looks like quite a normal and happy dog most of the time. But, and this is a big but, she still absolutely hates being touched, and hates being picked up or handled even more. I’ve taken things very slow with her as she isn’t the type of dog you can rush, so I’ve managed to get to the point with her where I can give her gentle strokes when she’s in one of her beds in the back of the kennel. She doesn’t enjoy it, but she does tolerate it now. Picking her up, on the other hand, is a different story. She’s still not used to it and she will still bite to protect herself, so I do have to use a thick blanket to avoid that. I really don’t think she’ll be this way forever, and I do think she’ll get better and better as time goes on, but it would be a lot easier if she was in a home with someone who knew how to help her.

Things such as walking on a lead, grooming, vet visits etc. won’t come easy, but I do believe she will get there and allow these things in the future. She really just needs someone who will love her for who she is, accept her worries and fears, and work with her on them. Most importantly, she needs someone who will never give up on her no matter what.

Rachel’s progress continues slowly and steadily and even though she still doesn’t like to be touched, she is so much more content and calm in general. She’s now more than happy to hang out with me and lay down near me, and just this week she actually went to sleep next to me with her tummy exposed!!! I know that may not sound like a lot, but it’s HUGE for a dog like Rachel with such severe trust issues.

The past couple of weeks at the rescue have been extremely warm and Rachel started to struggle a little bit with having such thick fur, so I decided to get it shaved off. Rachel is still not ready to be groomed, so I did have to take her into the vets to be sedated. This is the first time I’ve had to actually pick her up since I started going the crate and touch work with her, but it had to be done. She does still try her very best to get away and she does still try to bite, but it is less severe than what it was when she first came in. Getting her into my arms was the most difficult part, but after I had hold of her I was able to walk over to the vets carrying her, and hold her while she had her injection without a fuss. I was so, so proud of her. She’s now a bit bald, but so much more comfortable and cooler. When her fur starts to grow back I am going to start introducing her to a brush so she can get used to it, as her coat does grow quite fast and it’s very dense which means it gets matted easily. It’s not ideal for a dog like Rachel needing to be groomed regularly, but I’ll try my very best to ease her into it.

Looking after Rachel on a daily basis is very easy. She follows routine beautifully - running to the play yards and back into her kennel when it’s time to come in. She tries her best to be clean with her toileting and I think if she had access to a garden regularly, she would pick it up really quickly. She also shares everything with her kennel friends perfectly and she never puts a paw wrong with other dogs. Aside from hating being touched, she really isn’t a problem at all. I really am hoping that she’ll start to get used to it soon, and I think she will … but being in a home would help massively. So I hope she doesn’t have to wait too much longer for that to happen.

For the past month, Rachel has officially been my “project dog”. This means I’ve been spending a lot more time working directly with her, and I set a goal for both of us when I started. Because Rachel’s biggest fear is human hands, that became my main focus — helping her feel more comfortable with being touched and gently stroked.

In the first week, I wanted to get her used to my touch without her panicking. When Rachel thinks she’s about to be handled, she’ll run around the kennel, jumping from bed to bed to avoid me, and will bite to protect herself if I get too close. I felt that all the running and panic was only reinforcing her fear, making things harder for both of us. So, I introduced a crate to safely contain her in a smaller space, allowing me to begin gentle handling in a more controlled way.

My hope was that she would start to realise that a soft fuss on her head or body isn’t actually that scary — that the anticipation was worse than the reality. Each day for that first week, I set up a crate at the back of her kennel and spent a short session gently touching her, just once a day to ease her into it.

On the first day, it took a little while for her to go into the crate, but she eventually went in with her friend. She was actually very good and allowed me to gently stroke her face for a few minutes, before becoming a little unsettled and starting to nibble my hand. By the second day, she went into the crate much more quickly and again allowed strokes around her head and under her ears. As I carefully moved further down her body, she became uncomfortable and nibbled a bit harder to let me know she’d had enough.

By the third day, she went straight into the crate, and I focused more on her body. She allowed longer strokes before becoming unsettled. The fourth day was very similar, but on the fifth day there was a real breakthrough — she let me stroke her tummy and chest without any nibbles at all.

After every session, I made sure to sit at the front of her kennel for a few minutes and give her treats so we always ended on a positive note (and to make sure she was still my friend!). Rachel is known to hold a grudge, so maintaining that trust was really important, and thankfully this work hasn’t damaged our relationship at all.

In week two, my goal was to remove the crate and see if she would choose to stay settled in a bed while I handled her. I wasn’t sure how it would go, but she absolutely amazed me. On the first day, she settled into a bed at the back of the kennel while I sat on the floor and gently shuffled towards her — and she stayed still, allowing me to stroke her. I kept things consistent over the next few days without pushing her too far.

By the fifth day, I introduced something new: scissors around her head. She needs a fringe trim, so I wanted to begin desensitising her to the sensation and presence of them. She did incredibly well — so well, in fact, that I managed to snip a tiny bit, which I hadn’t even planned to do. Because she was coping so calmly, I took the opportunity, and it paid off.

In week three, I continued trimming her fringe gradually, little by little. After a few days, I was able to clear the hair from around her eyes.

That’s where we are now. There’s still a long way to go, and Rachel will need plenty more time, patience and love, but I’m so pleased with how far she’s come. We’ve definitely made real progress, and I’m excited to keep building on it with her.

Rachel has been at the rescue for just over a month now and in that time she’s gained a lot of inner confidence, and has blossomed into a very cheeky and happy girl who always seems to be up to mischief!! She absolutely loves toys and gets very excited when I put them in her kennel every morning, and she also loves playing with them in the yards. She’s also very partial to starting ‘parties’ AKA getting all the dogs to have a massive game of chase with her, which she finds very amusing. Her favourite thing in the world though … food!!! She is one of the foodiest dogs I’ve ever met and is always at the front of the queue for breakfast, dinner, and treats.Even though Rachel has made progress in many areas, one thing she still simply can’t handle is being touched by us humans in any way. Her fear of our hands is so strong and she will try to bite to protect herself. This doesn’t mean she’s a nasty dog in any way, it’s just complete panic and fear. It’s something I’m trying to de-sensitise her to and I’m working with her as much as I can, but I do think it’s going to take a long time and a lot of consistency. We don’t know what she’s been through in her life that’s made her the way she is, so all we can do now is prove to her that humans can be kind, and hope that one day she’s able to put her past behind her.Rachel will need a very experienced home with people who will be extremely patient with her, understand her, and work with her through her worries and fears. She’ll need at least 1 resident dog to learn from, and absolutely no children. Things that are normal to most dogs such as going for a walk, being brushed/groomed, or even just having a little fuss, are alien to Rachel, so it’s important her adopters take all of this into consideration and be okay with it.

It may be a long and slow road to get Rachel to where she needs to be, but I promise it will be so worth it. There is no better feeling than a dog like her showing you love and trust for the first time!

Rachel is a very scared girl who has come to us from a breeder. She is a very scared girl at the moment who is quite overwhelmed to find herself here and clearly hasn't had much socialisation before. She is looking for a home with adopters with experience of scared ex-breeding dogs who can provide the reassurance and stability she needs to help build her confidence as she learns about safety, trust, and our intentions.

She will need an adult-only home that can offer a calm and predictable environment where she can take things at her own pace. Rachel will also need at least one kind and confident resident dog to help her settle in and take her under their wing, as she can be easily overwhelmed at the moment.

Rachel has never lived in a home before, so she will need patient and understanding adopters while she learns about house training and how to walk on a lead. Right now, the big wide world may feel too overwhelming for her, so gentle sniffs in the garden would be a good place to start.

Rachel is only acting out of fear, and we have not yet been able to see the girl she will become once she feels safe. She deserves so much love, she just isn’t sure how to accept it yet and will need a truly understanding home to help her blossom.

Rachel has come to us with a pea sized cyst on her shoulder that has been removed at the time of her spay.

name: Archie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 21 teeth removed.

Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him. Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive and patient way.

He is a cuddly and affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

As Archie has lived in a home before, he will already be familiar with the sights and sounds of home life. However, he may need a little reminding of his house training in a new environment. He walks well on a lead and enjoys his walks with volunteers.

Archie is looking for a quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of the breed and of rescue dogs. He will need people who are happy to give him the time and space he needs to settle and understand that he is safe.

Archie is doing really well since returning to us and his confidence is growing all the time. He is such a loving little dog, and in the right home, we hope he will continue to thrive and become a devoted companion.

Archie is an absolute pleasure to work with! It’s been some time now, and our bond continues to grow stronger every day.He absolutely loves smothering you with kisses and will do anything to get himself onto your lap! Archie has been kennelled with a few dogs and socialised with plenty more, but he has become particularly taken with a Cocker called Trixie. They share some similar traits, including not wanting to share their humans, although neither has displayed any jealousy towardsthe other so far. They absolutely love running laps around the yard together before heading straight into your lap for some fuss. Archie will even stand on Trixie’s back just to make sure he gets in on the action and doesn’t miss out on any attention!As mentioned, Archie is yet to display any jealous traits towards either dogs or humans, but that doesn’t mean he won’t potentially show this once settled into a home. It’s something any potential adopter should be mindful of and prepared to manage appropriately.

What I can promise, though, is that Archie will become your best friend. He has so much love to give and, once he trusts you, he will love you unconditionally.This gorgeous boy deserves someone who will give him the love, patience and understanding he needs — and in return, you’ll have a loyal companion who will want nothing more than to be by your side.

Archie is the funniest and cheekiest of little Dachshunds. Archie needs a little time to warm to you (but not all that long), and once he does, he is the most lovely of boys. I have been caring for him for a few weeks now, and I am totally smitten.

Archie walks beautifully on lead and loves nothing more than when we venture out for a stroll along the lanes around the rescue. Archie is very fond of his toys and will happily run around the yard with a ball in his mouth. He will also spend much time organising his cuddly toys, making sure they are in just the right place.

Archie has been kennelled with other small female dogs. He seems to do best with robust smaller females, as he can be a little frisky with the more timid dogs. Archie could go as an only dog in the right home, one where there are humans who will have lots of time for him.

Archie is very enthusiastic with his kisses once he knows you and will desperately clamber over you for fusses. Archie is an all-round lovely little dog, best suited to a quiet adult home where there is plenty of love, time, and patience for him to truly settle in.

Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him. Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive, patient way.

He is a cuddly, affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

Archie is a gorgeous little boy who came to us from a breeder and was understandably unsure of the world around him. It was truly heartbreaking to see how frightened he was as he would shy away from human contact and retreat when approached. Archie needs gentle handling, patience, and calm, slow movements to help him feel safe. Already, we are seeing progress. He enjoys a gentle fuss and has grown some confidence wagging his tail enthusiastically.

He gains reassurance from other dogs and will need a kind, confident resident dog in his new home to help guide him, boost his confidence, and show him that people and home life can be safe and rewarding.

Archie has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be patient and understanding as he learns the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. He could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and his own space to settle in.

Since arriving with us, Archie has undergone extensive and much-needed dental treatment and has had 21 teeth removed. He is now recovering well and feeling much more comfortable.

name: Gala
description:
I need a quiet adult-only home with no visiting kids to keep me stress-free.

I need at least one resident dog to help me feel safe, preferably a female my size.

I’m frightened and will need a secure garden to learn about being outside.

I enjoy secure enclosed areas where I can run around, but the lead still worries me.

I’m learning to walk on the lead, it's scary for me but I am toilet trained!

I’m fully vaccinated and spayed, ready for my forever home!

Gala is an extremely sweet but incredibly sensitive girl who originally came to us from a breeder. Sadly, she has already been adopted twice and returned both times, as the homes simply weren’t the right fit for her. Because of this, Gala is now searching for a very special forever home with people who truly understand her needs and are committed to giving her the time, patience, and stability she has never had.

When she first arrived, she was an extremely scared, flighty, and shut-down girl who wanted nothing to do with us humans. Since then, Gala has made some lovely, if small, steps forward. She will now allow a gentle stroke while she is on the sofa, usually for around a minute before she chooses to move away. This is huge progress for her and shows just how brave she is becoming.

On one occasion, she even chose to jump up onto the sofa and sit beside someone. Although she ran off as soon as there was a slight movement, it was still a big milestone and a really positive sign of her growing confidence.

That said, Gala is still a very worried girl who carries a lot of fear, and she has a long way to go. She is still frightened of interaction and will run away when approached. However, once she has settled into one of her beds, she will stay still to be gently picked up or have her lead put on.

She remains very nervous of the harness and lead. While she settles a little once it is on, the process of putting it on is still very scary for her. This will need to be built up slowly and gently to avoid overwhelming her or setting her back. She does know how to walk on a lead, but finds it quite daunting, and the outside world is still very overwhelming. She will need time and patience, starting in a secure garden to help build her confidence before any bigger adventures.

Gala takes great comfort from other dogs and truly thrives in their company. She loves to snuggle up with them and will be happiest in a home with other female dogs — the more, the better if possible. She has already shown that she forms particularly strong bonds, often choosing a favourite companion and looking to them for guidance. A kind, confident, and playful female dog of a similar size would be ideal for her, as she finds reassurance and happiness with other dogs while humans are still a source of uncertainty.

She also has a lovely playful side beginning to emerge, and she enjoys carrying around and playing with cuddly toys, which seem to bring her comfort and contentment.

Gala cannot live with cats and will need a calm, child-free home, including no visiting children, where she can feel safe and secure.

Gala has never truly known security, so what she needs most now is patience, kindness, and someone who will never give up on her. There won’t be any overnight miracles, and she may never become a confident, outgoing dog, but with the right person by her side, we know she can continue to grow in confidence, heal from her past, and finally understand what it means to feel safe and loved.

Gala has visited the vets regarding a small mass of inguinal fat. This is not causing her any harm and is currently being left alone, but it may need monitoring in the future.

Gala has made a few small improvements over the past month. She will now allow us to give her a short stroke while she’s on the sofa, usually for about a minute before she moves away. This is massive progress for her and shows how brave she’s becoming.

On one occasion, she even jumped up onto the sofa and sat beside me. As soon as I moved slightly, she ran off, but it was still a big step forward and she did so well.

She is still very scared of the harness. Once it’s on, she settles a little, but the process of putting the lead on frightens her. It’s going to be a very slow process, as we don’t want to push her too far and risk setting her back.

She also loves carrying around and playing with a cuddly toy, which seems to make her feel more content and happy.

Gala is still happiest when surrounded by other female dogs — the more, the better if possible. She has chosen a favourite and looks to her for guidance. A confident, playful female companion would be ideal for her, as she finds comfort in other dogs while humans are still a source of fear.

Gala has been back in foster for a few weeks and she seems to be happy and loves being with her dog friends. She settles very quickly and will happily sleep on a comfy chair. But she is still a very worried girl, as although looking settled, If one of us gets up, she'll be up and running to hide out of our  way. We have found routine is the best thing for her, she is more confident with this.

She very quickly learns what to do and does get animated when certain times arrive, such as breakfast and dinner - as long as she doesn't need to be too near a human. She will definitely need a very stable home without changes and without expectation. At the moment she will interact with us from a distance ok but doesn't get close. If you approach slowly she will stay put and you can stroke her or pick her up but she's not comfortable with it and would much rather escape from you...

On the positive side, she has started to show signs of enjoying a tummy rub, she will lift her leg for more to show she's liking it - almost like her doggy instincts are getting the better of her, this is the only time she happily excepts touching that she seems to enjoy.

Putting her harness on she shakes with fear when she sees her harness and it needs putting on very very slowly. She then is happy to walk in her own surroundings on a lead, but is so scared of being outside in the big world on it and will try to escape.

However she does love being taken to a secure field where she can run around playing with her furry friends. She loves all our other dogs and interacts very well with them all. Plus she is house trained.

Her new home must be one who gives her patience and time and expects nothing in return, this could be for a long time. She needs a very stable quiet home without too many changes happening and a good routine She wouldn't react well to things like doggy day care or holidays. She needs some very gentle persuasion to gain trust on humans but without expectations so she is not pushed too far and regressed.

Gala has been back at the rescue with me for just about two months now. I also looked after her when she was at the rescue originally, around a year and a half ago. Seeing her arrive back was hard for me, but it was nice to see how much progress she’s made during her time away. When I knew her all that time ago, she was an extremely scared, flighty, and shut-down girl who wanted nothing to do with us humans. It’s very clear she has gained confidence since then and has (sort of) learnt that she can trust us humans, so it is lovely to see the difference in her. Having said that, she does still carry a lot of worry and fear, and she still has a long way to go. Steps have been made in the right direction, so hopefully she can continue learning and growing, and eventually try to put her past behind her.Gala’s biggest love is food, so this is the main thing I’ve been using to get her comfortable around me. She has learnt how to ‘sit’ and also how to give the best puppy dog eyes that I can never say no to! She waits patiently for her turn for a treat, and takes them nice and gently too.Gala does still have quite a big fear of human hands and won’t approach me for a fuss, but she is good when it comes to things such as being groomed. When I need to pick her up, she’ll usually jump into one of her beds and then stay still for me to scoop her. She knows how to walk on a harness, but the outside world is another one of her fears, so this is something that needs to be taken slowly with her. I doubt very much she’ll be up for big adventures any time soon and will need a lot of practice in the garden and very quiet areas for a good while, so this is something her future adopters will need to take into consideration.After a life full of uncertainty and confusion, her next home HAS to be the right one for her. She really needs adopters who will love her regardless of her worries and work with her through them. Most importantly of all, she can’t be given up on again. She deserves to know where she’s going to wake up in the morning and not have to worry about being passed from pillar to post. She deserves love, trust, and commitment … and not a smidge less.

Sadly, Gala has returned to the kennels after her recent adoption. Although her new family cared deeply for her, it turned out not to be the right match. This decision was made with everyone's best interests at heart, and she’s now back with us while we look for her perfect forever home. Gala is a wonderful dog who just needs the right environment to truly thrive, and we’re hopeful that her special someone is out there waiting for her.

Gala is still in foster and gradually making progress. She is still extremely hand-shy but has started to come up and let her nose touch your hand before running off! She will then come back wanting to do it again and wagging her tail (huge progress!).Gala is looking for a forever home to offer her patience and lots of time to help her get over her fears. She is fully house trained and very happy to follow our other dogs around copying what they do. She is an escape artist on a harness as she is still nervous walking on a lead, but we have found taking her to a secure dog run field is amazing for her and she absolutely loves her freedom running around. Gala is ideally looking for some playmates in her new home as she does love to run and play with other dogs.

Gala is doing brilliantly in her foster home. She loves the company of other dogs and loves to play with them but is still very hand-shy with us humans and very wary.Gala would love a home with one or more furry friends who love playing, but what she also needs is a home which would help her understand to not be frightened anymore and people who will understand it's going to take time and patience until you get any affection or love back from her.Gala has big trust issues and needs a selfless home to get her over this hurdle she is facing.

Gala has sadly returned to the kennels through no fault of her own after a six month adoption. Her adopter made the difficult decision to bring her back due to a change in their personal circumstances, and she was much loved during her time with them. She’s now back with us and receiving lots of care and attention while we help her find another loving home. Gala is a lovely dog who truly deserves her second chance.

Gala came to us from a breeder a few months ago. We are told she is a Poodle cross Cavalier cross Bichon and she is the cutest little girl but is very overwhelmed and nervous so does need an experienced home who have had scared ex-breeding dogs before.Sadly Gala was returned after a short adoption due to a change in her adopters circumstances but was lucky enough to go to a foster home. She will need a calm and quiet home and is very scared of children so will need an adult only home with no visiting children. She will need a secure garden as she is so worried she can be a flight risk.Gala will need a home with at least one other kind and confident resident dog to be her friend and help her to settle in. She is house trained, but may need some reminders in her new home and walking on a lead is a little scary for her, so she will need more practice with this. She LOVES food and that's the way to her heart, she will take a treat from our hand, but other than that she is very hand shy and will run away if we go to stroke or approach her.This little lady just needs to find her perfect home for she can learn that people can offer her kindness and love. She is a sweet girl who with time, love and kindness will soon start to blossom.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Juice
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have learned how to walk on a lead and am enjoying going for walks.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have had 7 teeth extracted at the time of my spay.

Juice came to us from a breeder and when she first arrived, she was understandably very shy and overwhelmed by everything around her. She wanted to trust people but was nervous about approaching, often hovering nearby and watching with interest before her worries got the better of her. She has since moved into foster and has made some lovely progress and is settling in well. Juice is still cautious, but she now follows her fosterers around the house and will approach for fuss when they offer their hand to her. She particularly loves belly rubs and will completely relax and close her eyes!

Juice will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and help her settle into her new home. Although she does rely on other dogs for comfort, she can guard her bed from other dogs, particularly when she has just woken up, so she will need a calm, relaxed resident dog who will not disturb her while she is sleeping. She can also be startled by people when she is in her bed and on one occasion she did nip her fosterer when they stroked her in her bed. Her new family will therefore need to be confident managing this behaviour, recognising her body language and ensuring she is always left undisturbed when she is resting.

Juice had never lived in a home before moving to foster, but she is already settling in wonderfully. Her toilet training is going really well and she has only had 2 accidents in the home so far. She has also learned all about walking on a lead and harness and is now becoming more confident wearing her harness and she is starting to enjoy her walks. She is also beginning to understand that the home is a safe place, happily relaxing and sleeping near her fosterers and enjoying the company of their resident dog.

Juice will be looking for an adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand that she is still learning to trust and who will allow her to continue building her confidence at her own pace. She has already come such a long way in a short time, and we hope that with the right family, she will continue to blossom into a happy and loving companion.

She has had 7 teeth extracted at the time of her spay.

Juice has been given the Gift of Life by Holly Kantolinna

Juice has settled in really well. She is still cautious but follows us around the house although backs off if we approach her as she prefers it if you put your hand out to her. She will then approach us, sniff our hand and accept fuss and scratches. She loves having scratches but her favourite are belly rubs and she will close her eyes and completely relax!

She sleeps well over night in her bed on the floor in our bedroom and will wake us up by walking around the room when she needs to go to toilet. Her toilet training is going really well and apart from 2 accidents early on she goes in the garden either asking to go out or when the back door is open taking herself out to go.

She is getting more confident having her harness on for walk and as long as you put it on slowly, she is happy to have it on. She is starting to walk really well on her lead and enjoys her walks and plenty of sniffs! She has met a few dogs on her walks and as long as they are not too energetic and boisterous she seems happy to meet them and have a sniff! She is ok walking along roads but does startle if there are any loud or sudden noises.

She loves being with us in the house and although she doesn't sit right next to us she enjoys being close by and really relaxes and sleeps. She enjoys being with our resident dog but is also happy to follow us outside or sit with us when our dog isn't there. She's also happy travelling in the car with our dog.

She hasn't mastered going up and down stairs yet so at present we are carrying her up and down. She is starting to go up a few small steps on her walks.

She enjoys her food and will sometimes take treats or food from our hands.  She is a lovely girl who has really progressed in the short time that we have had her and is continuing to develop her confidence.

Juice will need an experienced, adult only home with adopters who can understand and manage her nervousness and recognise when she needs space. She can guard her bed from other dogs, particularly when she has just woken up, so any resident dog will need to be calm and relaxed and not likely to bother her while she is sleeping. She can also be startled by people when she is in her bed and, on one occasion, she did nip when she was stroked resting. Her adopters will therefore need to be confident in managing this behaviour, ensuring she is left undisturbed in her bed and giving her the space she needs to feel safe and comfortable.

Juice has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a loving forever home where she can begin the next chapter of her life.

She is a wonderful little lady who is feeling a little shy and overwhelmed at the moment, but she is trying so hard to be brave. Juice is already showing lovely signs that she wants to trust people. She will quietly hover nearby, watching you with interest and looking as though she would really like to come over for a gentle fuss, but at the last moment her worries get the better of her. We think that with time, patience, love and plenty of reassurance, her confidence will continue to grow and her true personality will begin to shine through.

Juice will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She will need patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time and who will let her make progress without putting any pressure on her. She will also need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can be her friend and help show her that life is full of good things.

As Juice has never lived in a home before, everything will be a brand new experience for her. She will need help with housetraining, learning about household routines and gradually becoming accustomed to all the sights and sounds of family life. She is also yet to learn how to walk on a lead and harness, so her adopters will need to introduce this gently and positively as her confidence grows.

Juice is a lovely girl with so much potential. With a patient family by her side and a canine friend to guide her, we are sure she will blossom into a happy and much-loved companion.

name: Gigi
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

27-08-26 Gigi is a very worried lady who has come to us from a breeder and is understandably very nervous and uncomfortable around people. She can be considered a flight risk as she will do her best to get away when she feels worried, so she will need very slow and gentle introductions to the world around her.

Gigi is going to need lots of TLC, patience and understanding from her new family as she learns that she is safe and begins to build her confidence. She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on for reassurance as she settles in.

Gigi has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. These things may take some time, and she will need a family who is happy to let her progress at her own pace. She will need a very secure garden with fences 6ft+.

Gigi will need an adult-only home with ex-breeding experience, where her needs can be understood and she can receive the patience and reassurance she deserves. With time, love and the support of a confident canine companion, we hope Gigi will slowly learn to trust and become the happy, active girl we know she can be.

Gigi has been given the Gift of Life by Rachel Morris

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Sianon
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before finding my forever home.

27-08-26 Sianon has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a worried girl who is unsure around humans and isn't used to being handled yet. She is going to need plenty of love, patience and TLC as she settles in and slowly begins to grow in confidence.

Sianon will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who understand that she will need time to adjust. Her new family will need to be kind and patient, allowing her to settle in at her own pace without putting pressure on her. She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her, and she will need gentle guidance as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training and how to walk on a lead and harness.

Sianon relies on other dogs for confidence, so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help her feel safe. We hope having a canine companion by her side will help her learn that the world isn't such a scary place. Any children in the home will need to be teenagers aged 16+.

Sianon is a gentle girl who has lots to learn, but with the right home, a patient family and a lovely canine friend to show her the ropes, we hope she will gradually discover her confidence and enjoy all the wonderful things life has to offer.

Sianon has been given the Gift of Life by Dee Wickson-Dix

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Crush
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I walk well on a harness and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I have bilateral nuclear sclerosis, and will be neutered before adoption!

13-08-26 Crush is a fairly nervous boy who has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. He can be very shy and tends to rely heavily on his kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so he will need time and patience as he settles into his new surroundings.

Crush will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in the home that he can look to and lean on as he learns about home life and begins to build his confidence. He has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be understanding as he learns all about house training and adjusts to a new routine.

Crush is walking well on a harness, so he would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with the resident dog when he is settled in.

He could live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand that he will need plenty of time and space to settle in and begin to trust. Crush is a lovely boy who simply needs plenty of TLC, patience, and kindness as he finds his paws in the world.

He has come to us with bilateral nuclear sclerosis that will need to be monitored in his new home, and does not seem to bother him at this time. The vet has noted that he has a potential for chronic skin issues and dental disease that will need to be monitored in his new home.

Crush has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

name: Nicole
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. When she first arrived, she was understandably feeling very scared and overwhelmed. It was clear she hadn’t had much handling or socialisation before, so human hands were quite worrying for her.

Nicole did move into a wonderful foster home for a short period, where she began learning all about home life. Unfortunately, she has now returned to our care following one moment where, while learning about wearing a lead and harness, she became tangled in the lead and panicked. In her fear, she nipped her fosterer. This was a single incident during a very frightening experience for her, but it is important that her future adopters understand that she may panic when she feels overwhelmed or trapped.

Since coming back into our care, Nicole has settled back in well and is trying so hard to be brave. She has a wonderfully inquisitive nature and is beginning to show us more of her sweet personality. She is still very worried about being handled and can bark when she is unsure, but she is making progress and absolutely loves her food.

Nicole will be looking for a calm and quiet adult-only home where she can settle in completely at her own pace. She will need adopters who have experience with nervous ex-breeding dogs and who understand the patience, time and reassurance she will need as she learns to trust. She loves other dogs and takes great comfort from their presence, so Nicole will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe and secure.

As Nicole had never lived in a home before moving to foster, she will need patient adopters who are ready to help her continue learning everything about home life. She will need to learn new skills such as house training and will also need to learn about walking on a lead and wearing a harness. Her adopters will need to take things very slowly and be mindful that she can panic if she feels frightened or restricted.

With time, kindness and plenty of TLC, we hope Nicole will continue to grow in confidence and learn that she is safe. She is trying so hard to be brave, and we know that with the right home, she has the potential to blossom.

Our vets have noted that Nicole has a slightly unusual heart rhythm, so she underwent a heart scan at our vets which showed some mild valve changes. At this stage she does not require any treatment and is expected to live a normal, happy life, although we would recommend routine heart checks and monitoring for any future symptoms.

Nicole has been given the Gift of Life by Shirley Bourne

Nicole has been in foster for a week and is a sweetie. She has a wonderfully inquisitive nature and loves investigating everything around her, which makes us chuckle! She is still very nervous about being handled and will bark when she's feeling unsure, but she is already making progress. She now takes treats from us and absolutely loves her food. She is also mostly clean overnight.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She is a lovely little girl who is understandably feeling very scared and overwhelmed to find herself here. It’s clear she hasn’t had much handling or socialisation before, so human hands are quite worrying for her at the moment, but we will continue gently helping her learn that hands can be kind.

Nicole will be looking for a calm and quiet adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She would really benefit from adopters who have experience with nervous ex-breeding dogs and who understand the patience, time and reassurance she will need as she learns to trust.

She loves other dogs and takes great comfort from their presence, so Nicole will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe and secure.

As Nicole has never lived in a home before, she will need patient adopters who are ready to help her learn everything about home life from the very beginning. She will need to learn new skills like house training and will also need to learn all about walking on a lead and harness.

With time, kindness and plenty of TLC, Nicole will begin to grow in confidence and let her personality shine.

name: Molly
description:
I'd like a quiet, patient home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I am new to lead walking, and would like to continue this once I have settled in.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I am being treated for a ear infection and am slightly overweight.

12-08-26 Molly is an anxious lady who has come into our care from a breeder in the hope of a fresh start.

She is very worried about handling at the moment and won't even eat if we are watching her. Molly prefers to stay at the back of her kennel and is still unsure of our intentions. She doesn't yet understand that we are here to help her, so we will be giving her plenty of time and space to settle and learn that she is safe.

Molly relies heavily on the other dogs for company and comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Molly has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and allow her to take things at her own pace. She is new to lead walking and her kennel mummy is working with her on this to help her comfortability, but she will need to continue this in her new home.

Molly has arrived overweight, so she will need a good diet and gentle exercise to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight. This will need to be continued in her new home.

Molly is a very worried girl right now, but we hope that with time, patience and the support of a kind canine friend, she will begin to feel safe and show us the sweet girl hiding underneath all those nerves.

She is currently being treated for a severe ear infection

Molly has been given the Gift of Life by Victoria Charlton
