I’m going to keep taking him into the cabin once a week or so just to ease him into it slowly, and then hopefully that will help his transition to home life when he does get adopted.

Cuba has been with me for over 3 months now and I literally love him more and more every day. I’m lucky to have a very close relationship with him and he loves me and trusts me completely, so I see a side to him that not many other people get to see.

He absolutely oozes charisma and character, and he makes me laugh and smile every time we’re together. He’s fiercely loyal, super affectionate, and SO comical. He gives the best of everything. He loves running around the yard with me and playing with toys, but loves a big sit down snuggle equally as much. So much so, he now likes to sprawl across my whole lap and fall into a deep sleep on me (snores and all)! His kennel is filled with plush toys that he loves to carry around in his mouth and sleep with, and he’s SO gentle with them. Isn’t he just the sweetest boy!?

He does still find a lot of things quite challenging, but I do feel as though we’re still making steady progress, and you can’t rush certain things. He’s still very easily spooked by loud noises, cars passing, people trying to approach him etc, so on walks especially I do have to make sure I’m paying complete attention to him. Most of the time he does recover quickly with a bit of reassurance from me, but then sometimes it will ruin his whole walk and he’ll immediately want to turn around and go back to the safety of his kennel. That’s okay though - I always allow it and take him back to make sure he knows he always has a safe place as and when he needs it.

We’ve briefly mentioned in a previous update that Cuba doesn’t like other dogs that much, but I hope this won’t put you off him as he’s not reactive to other dogs out on walks or anything like that - he simply just doesn’t like to share his space with them. I don’t think he was socialised with others apart from his old kennel friend before he came to us, so I think it’s understandable.

If you have the time and the patience to put the work in with Cuba, I can promise you 10 times over that adopting him will be the best decision of your life. Once he settles, he will truly be your best friend and the love of your life. That’s how I feel about him and I’m just his kennel mum!! He is utterly special and he deserves someone equally as special, who will love him as much as he will love them. He has such a big heart and he really does deserve the world and more.

Cuba has come on leaps and bounds over the past few weeks, and I feel so lucky to have been appointed as his “Kennel Auntie,” spending two days a week with this incredibly handsome boy.

Although Cuba can still be wary of strangers, the bond he forms once he trusts you is truly something special. Knowing him from when he first arrived, you honestly wouldn’t recognise him now. He used to hide away at the back of his kennel, wishing we would go away, now he demands to be the centre of attention and absolutely smothers you in kisses. While he may take a little time to warm up to new people, once he feels safe, his affectionate nature shines through.

Cuba has taken some big steps (quite literally!) and is absolutely smashing his harness training. His progress has been incredible, and his confidence grows more each day. He happily trots along on walks, tail wagging, taking in all the exciting new smells he’s never experienced before. Watching him discover so many “firsts” is truly magical.

We’ve found that Cuba isn’t too fussed about other dogs (aside from his kennel friend Chippy), so he would be best suited to a home where he can be the only dog. This will allow him to soak up all the love and attention he thrives on.

I cherish every moment I get to spend with Cuba. He is the sweetest, soppiest boy. He is so full of love, yet not enough people get to see this side of him. He adores playing with toys, cuddling, bouncing around like a lunatic, giving kisses, and sniffing everything in sight on his walks. But most of all, he loves his people.

There isn’t a moment with Cuba where you won’t feel loved. He makes every second count and whoever is lucky enough to adopt him should do the same. He truly is a special boy, and you wouldn’t want to miss out on him.

Cuba has been on my section for a few weeks now and I am just head over heels in love with him. I knew he was a nervous and sensitive boy so I have taken things slow with him and left him be to suss me out and get used to my routine, but it really didn’t take long for him to become quite attached to me. Within a few days he started to trust me, and now I would say he actually trusts me completely. So much so, I’ve been able to start harness training with him, put medication in his eyes after his surgery, and he’s given me his belly a couple of times for fusses!!!

I still haven’t taken him outside of the secure yard on his harness yet, but I do think he’s ready so I’m going to try it really soon. His biggest fear was having any tension on the lead - he would get really spooked by it and panic - but I think we’re just about over that now and he’s gotten used to it.With Cuba, once he gets to know you and forms a bond with you he is an extremely affectionate, happy, and playful boy, but he is still standoffish with people he doesn’t know and he doesn’t trust them to touch him or handle him. This is something his future adopters will need to take into consideration and prepare for. He’ll just need to be given some time, patience and gentleness to begin with. I am certain he’ll come around, but it will need to be in his own time as he can’t be pushed.

Cuba is hilarious and so goofy, and he will make such a great addition to someone’s home in time, but it does need to be the right home to ensure he’s set up for only success. I adore him very much and I just know his future parents will too, so please keep him in mind if you think you could be a good match for him!

Cuba is making lovely progress and is becoming increasingly sociable as his confidence grows. He is still finding walking on a harness quite scary and will need a patient home willing to help him continue this training at his own pace.

Cuba may need a couple of meetings to feel comfortable, but once he knows you, he will happily approach with his tail wagging and enjoy a gentle fuss. He particularly loves relaxing in his bed with trusted company nearby, quietly enjoying being stroked as he drifts off to sleep.

At heart, he is a very sweet and gentle boy who is learning to trust and has already formed strong bonds with familiar staff. He is simply a scared boy who needs a fresh start in a calm, understanding and respectful home where he can continue to blossom.

Cuba is a very nervous and shy boy who is finding the world quite overwhelming at the moment. He needs a slow, gentle approach and plenty of time to build trust, but once he feels safe with someone, he will allow calm, gentle fuss while settled in his bed, which he finds very reassuring. Underneath his worried exterior, Cuba is simply a big, scared baby who needs kindness, patience, and understanding to help him feel secure.

Cuba will need an adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand nervous dogs and are happy to let him settle at his own pace. He has never lived in a home before, so everything will be completely new to him. His adopters will need to be patient and supportive as he learns about home life, including house training and how to walk on a harness and lead. Gentle practice in the garden will be an important starting point before he is ready to venture further afield.

Cuba will also need at least one kind, confident resident dog in the home. He gains comfort and confidence from other dogs and will benefit greatly from having a calm canine role model to help guide him and show him that the world is a safe place. He is not suitable to be an only dog.

Cuba is currently learning to walk on a harness, but this is something he finds very challenging and will require a great deal of time, patience, and dedication. He is also quite fond of using his voice and enjoys a good grumble rather than barking, which is very much part of his character.

Cuba will need a calm, quiet home where he can have his own safe space and plenty of downtime alongside gentle interaction. With love, reassurance, and understanding adopters, he will slowly begin to realise that not all people are bad and that he is finally safe. In the right home, with the right support, Cuba has the potential to blossom into a deeply rewarding companion.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Louise
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home with experienced adopters.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am not ready to learn about lead walking yet. A garden is fine for now.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and can still find people and handling very frightening. However, she has made lovely progress since arriving and is showing us more of her cheeky personality every day.

Over the past month, Louise has grown in confidence. While she is still very worried about being touched and picked up, she is no longer as shut down as she was when she first arrived. She is now more than happy to come over for treats and will sit close by while waiting for more. She likes to use her voice to let everyone know how she is feeling, is very partial to chasing flies, and has quite a big personality packed into such a tiny dog. It is wonderful to see her becoming more comfortable in her surroundings.

Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her as she settles into family life.

Louise can be vocal around food and may give a warning growl, but she does not actually do anything and this appears to simply be her way of communicating that she would like some space. She can happily be fed alongside her canine friends as long as each dog has their own bowl and they stick to their own food. She is also absolutely fine taking treats, so this is something her adopters should continue to manage calmly and sensibly.

Louise is slowly becoming more comfortable with being handled, and gentle work has begun to help her get used to being picked up. This is still very worrying for her and she can become wriggly and panic when lifted, but she has never tried to bite during these sessions. With time and patience, we hope she will continue to learn that she is safe and that nobody is going to hurt her.

Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns the basics, including house training. She is not yet ready for harness training, so her future family will need to carefully plan how and when to introduce this once she feels more secure. Everything must happen at Louise's pace so that she can continue building confidence without becoming overwhelmed.

Louise is a sensitive little soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her flourish. Every small step she takes is a huge achievement, and she continues to surprise us with just how much she is growing in confidence. With experienced adopters, kind canine companions and lots of love, we truly believe Louise will continue to blossom into the wonderful little dog we know she can become.

Louise has been given the Gift of Life by Ann Winter

Louise has been with us for about 3 months now and even though she has progressed since she first arrived, things are happening very slowly and steadily. I would have liked for her to have gained more confidence by this point, but some dogs struggle with being in such a busy kennel environment to let their guard down … and Louise is one of them! That’s okay though. Making sure she’s happy and content within herself is the most important thing, and I’d say she is!

I haven’t really pushed Louise too far out of her comfort zone up until now, just because I didn’t want to send her backwards with her progress, but there does come a point where you have to, to prove to them that it’s okay. So today I took Louise into my grooming room for a very gentle and calm brushing session. She didn’t want to stand on the grooming table and kept clambering back onto me - which is the first time she’s ever done that - so I opted to keep her on my lap while I brushed her. She was settled for the most part, but she did have a little panic when we got to her ears as she had a couple of tangles which must have hurt her. I managed to cut them out with a scissors and then she was okay with me brushing around that area. I kept the session very short and sweet as I didn’t want to push too far, and I think it was the right decision. When I took her back to the kennel she didn’t sprint away from me or anything like that, so I’d say our relationship is still there!

Louise is such a special little character, and I really hope someone will see her in the same way I do soon. She deserves a life outside of kennels, one where she can finally start to thrive.

Louise has been on my section with me for about a month now, and I’ve definitely seen some positive changes in her. She’s still terrified of being touched and picked up, but her overall confidence is improving daily. She’s now more than happy to come and take treats from me and sit close to me while she’s waiting for more. She’s also nowhere near as shut down as she was when she first arrived and is now turning into quite a cheeky monkey. She does like to use her voice to express her feelings, and she’s also very partial to chasing flies! She’s actually got quite a big personality for such a little girl, and it’s a pleasure to see it emerging as the days go by.I’ve been working slowly on getting Louise used to being picked up, and while she’s definitely still very worried about it, she has calmed down slightly. She’s never tried to bite me, but she does sometimes have little panics and becomes very wriggly when she’s in my arms. I do think this is something that will improve over time. She just needs some more practice and to realise that we’re not hurting her. She obviously hasn’t been handled a lot in her life, so now it’s up to us to prove to her that it’s okay.I love working with Louise, and I can really see the potential in her. She just needs someone to give her a chance and work with her through all her worries and fears. She’s not ready for harness training or conquering the outside world yet, so that’s something her future adopters will need to take into consideration and make a plan for. I do believe she’ll progress faster in a kind home with adopters who have lots of time and patience to give her, so I really hope she won’t have to wait here for much longer.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and currently finds people and handling very frightening. At the moment, Louise feels safest keeping her distance and, if pushed beyond her comfort zone, may make the wrong decision and nip purely out of fear. She is a very scared girl who needs understanding, patience and time.Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience of helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing.Although Louise takes great comfort from other dogs, she can show signs of resource guarding around food. For this reason, she will need to be fed separately from other dogs, and care will need to be taken when giving treats or other high-value food items. Her adopters will need experience of managing this behaviour and the confidence to do so appropriately.Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns new skills such as house training. She is not yet ready to begin learning about lead walking or wearing a harness, as handling is still very worrying for her. These things will need to be introduced gradually and at her pace once she feels more comfortable and secure.Louise is a sensitive soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her build confidence. We will continue to work with her every day, helping her take small steps forward at a pace she is comfortable with. In the right home, with the support of canine friends and experienced adopters, we hope Louise will slowly learn that people can be kind and that life has so much to offer.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Max
description:
I need an active, breed experienced home that loves playtime!

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I walk on the lead but I can pull when excited.

I am house trained but I need to learn some manners.

I will need to be neutered when I am of age! It's important!

Max is a superstar Lurcher who has been returned to us from his adoptive family. They made the heartbreaking decision to bring him back as he was becoming dominant over the other dog in the home.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people. He is very food oriented, which makes training enjoyable and rewarding, and he already shows lovely food manners, waiting patiently when asked.

Max absolutely loves other dogs and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend. However, he is still young, full of energy, and not always aware of his size and strength. This can sometimes lead to him becoming overexcited, a little mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs. He has been working hard on his social skills and has been socialising while wearing a muzzle for safe and positive interactions. This is purely as a precaution, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to other dogs.

As he was too much for a more timid dog in his previous home, we feel that Max would be best suited to being homed as an only dog, provided he has plenty of appropriate socialisation with dogs of a similar size and play style. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training, structure, and consistency will be important, along with plenty of mental stimulation to keep his busy mind engaged. He would thrive in a home that can offer activities such as training games or even dog sports.

Max could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who understand that he can be a bit of a bull in a china shop. Any young people in the home will need to be confident and not worried by an enthusiastic dog who may jump up while he continues to work on his manners.

Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods, so he will need a home where someone is around most of the time and who is committed to helping him gradually build confidence with being left.

Max's new home will need a large, secure garden with 6ft boundaries, where he can let off some steam.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy, bouncy, affectionate, and full of life, with so much potential. He is a big-hearted lad who gives his whole heart, and with the right guidance, he will grow into an incredible companion.

Where do I start with the wonderful ball of energy that is Max.

First and foremost, the question I ask myself and almost everyone that meets Max asks too, how on earth is he still waiting?! A young, handsome, intelligent dog who is BARRELS of fun. There’s something about Max that is just so loveable and he truly does capture people’s hearts. Many of the volunteers who walk him are always so happy to see him and enjoy their time together.

Recently we’ve been working on nailing a ‘touch’ command. When Max is focused he is such a rewarding dog to train. Sometimes his desire to please takes over and he waves his paw at me until I have to accept it (and of course reward because he's the goodest boy no matter what). He is also learning to be calmer when greeting people and has even had some gentle fuss from some children too. It remains true that Max cannot be homed with children under the age of 16, but it is so important for Max to have positive interactions with respectful children to prevent any reactivity / fear from developing. It also helps teach him to be calm when meeting new people, especially when they’re smaller than him!

Max brings such a unique type of energy to the rescue, he is such a joyful boy and truly comes alive when he is with his people. I threw Max a 1st birthday party and all of his favourite people came throughout the day to play with him and bring him yummy treats, fuss and cuddles. He had the best day and it was so touching to see how loved he is despite not being in a home.

We are doing our very best to raise Max into a well rounded, well socialised and well adjusted adult dog. However, he is at such a crucial stage in his development and has already spent 5 months in kennels. It’s no place for a young dog to grow up. Nearly half of his life spent in kennels patiently waiting for his second chance to come and take him home.

Despite his size Max really is just a baby and definitely a lap dog too. So if you have a spot on the sofa you can share, Max will happily join you and be the bestest friend anyone could wish for.

Myself and Max have formed a very close bond over the last few months we’ve been working together. We take daily walks, go to the big play yard and have plenty of cuddles and fusses.I’m not sure what it is about Max that keeps getting him overlooked, it could be his size or that he is like a big playful puppy or something else, whatever it is, anyone would be lucky to have this handsome chap in their lives, he will always put a smile on your face and he has such a good sense of humour, watching him having zoomies in his kennel yard while he’s jumping off the obstacles in there then stoping then going back round again is nothing short of entertaining, or when he’s fishing treats out of the paddling pool while simultaneously blowing bubbles with his nose.Max truly deserves the world, he is such a sweet and caring boy with a big personality and so much love to give, as well as his big size there is also a big heart and all he wants is to be able to fully give it to someone and finally find his forever home.

Max is a big, happy baby with bags of energy and so much love to give. He is an excitable, affectionate boy who adores attention and loves having people around him. He is always happy to greet you and be part of whatever is going on.

As Max is still young and growing, he is slowly learning his manners and how to greet people politely without jumping. . He will need adopters who can match his energy, continue his training, and give him the stimulation, guidance, and love he needs to thrive.

Max is a gentle, overlooked soul who is learning new things every day at the rescue, but he is missing the comforts of home. He cannot wait to find a family who understands him and can help him blossom into the wonderful companion he is meant to be.With the right home, patience, and plenty of love, Max will make a loyal and joyful best friend.

Since coming back into our care, Max has been working hard on learning how to socialise with other dogs. He absolutely adores them and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend! Because he’s still young, full of beans, and a bit unaware of his own size, he can sometimes be a little too enthusiastic. This can lead to him becoming overexcited, a bit mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs.

To help him learn safe and positive interactions, Max has been socialising while wearing a muzzle. This is purely for his safety and that of other dogs, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to new canine companions. Aside from that, Max is everything you’d want in a young pup he's bouncy, happy, affectionate, and full of life.

He’s very food oriented, which makes training a dream! He already knows commands like “sit” and has learned great food manners where be waits patiently until he’s told he can eat. Max thrives on mental stimulation and ongoing training, and with the right guidance, he has all the potential to grow into an incredible dog. Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods. He really craves human company so he’ll need a home where someone is around most of the time and is committed to helping him build confidence being alone gradually. He’s such a loving, handsome boy who gives his whole heart, and it would be wonderful to see him back in a home environment where he can truly thrive. As a young pup, he’s missed out on some important early experiences, so a patient, committed family will make all the difference in helping him become the best version of himself.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people.

Max loves other dogs but is often unaware of his size and strength, having grown into such a big lad very quickly. As he is still just a puppy, he is still learning about manners and can be mouthy and plays in a very typical Lurcher way. In his previous home, there was an incident when he was around 3 months old, where he was a little too rough and resulted in a small dog needing veterinary treatment. He has started muzzle training for off-lead play as a precaution, and he will need a home that understands Lurcher play styles and is confident managing this appropriately. We have been socialising him with dogs of all sizes on walks and he is doing very well.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training and consistency will be important.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy. He is a big-hearted, affectionate lad who is still convinced he can curl up and fit on your lap.

name: Dutch
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need to be the only dog in my new home. No cats please!

I walk well on a lead and muzzle trained. I would enjoy an active lifestyle!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am already vaccinated and neutered and ready for my new home!

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet, with a heart as big as his personality. Dutch simply wants to be close to his people, whether that's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up beside you for cuddles. Being with the people he loves is all he really wants.

Dutch would love to find a home with adopters who are around for most of the day and can include him in everyday life. He thrives on human companionship and will make a wonderfully devoted shadow to his new family. He will need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and understand typical breed traits, including prey drive and the need for appropriate mental and physical enrichment.

Dutch would be best suited to life as an only dog. Although he can socialise well with other dogs of a similar size, he can become overexcited and mouthy, which may lead to frustration. Because of this, he is muzzle trained and wears a muzzle during social interactions to help him continue building positive experiences. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need support with house training and learning the general routines of family life. He is such a clever boy and always tries his very best to do the right thing, so we are confident he will enjoy learning with patient, positive guidance.

Dutch already walks well on a lead, although he can occasionally be reactive when passing other kennels. This is understandable in a busy rescue environment and may be something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an energetic, happy-go-lucky boy who is more than ready to start exploring the world with his new family. An active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, training and quality time with his people would suit him perfectly.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate that he will need a gentle introduction to his new surroundings and his own space to settle in.

Dutch is bright, affectionate and full of love. He has so much to offer and is simply looking for someone to love as much as he loves them. For the right family, he will be an incredibly loyal, fun-loving and devoted companion.

Dutch has a passport and travel document.

Dutch has been given the Gift of Life by Louise Southward

I still can’t quite understand how this incredibly smart and loving boy hasn’t found his forever home yet.If you’re looking for a dog to train, learn new tricks and go on lots of adventures with, then Dutch really is your boy.He’s the best of both worlds a crazy, energetic boy who also absolutely loves his people and loves nothing more than a good snuggle.

Dutch, or as I like to call him, Dutchy, is honestly one of the most loving and affectionate boys you could ever hope to meet.

He's the kind of dog who just wants to be close to you. Whether it's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up for cuddles, being with his people is all he really wants. Watching him have to go back into his kennel after spending time together is heartbreaking because kennel life is just no place for a boy like him.

What makes it even sadder is that he hasn't received a single application. If I'm honest, my biggest worry is that he'll become one of our long-stay dogs, and my heart breaks at the thought of that because he simply doesn't deserve it.

He's such a clever boy and always tries so hard to do the right thing. He recently went on his first long walk with one of our wonderful regular volunteers and was an absolute angel. He took everything in his stride and made everyone so proud.

He's also been having play dates with our lovely girl, Swanny, to help him burn off some of that doggy energy while learning good doggy manners.

At the end of the day, Dutchy is just a baby. He's got the biggest heart, so much love to give, and he deserves a home where he'll be someone's whole world instead of waiting behind kennel doors. I know his family is out there somewhere; I just hope they find him before he spends another day wondering why no one has chosen him.

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet.

He would love to find a loving home with adopters who are around most of the time and would have plenty of time to spend with him. He would need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and experience with his typical breed traits like prey drive etc.

Dutch would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as although he does socialise well with other dogs of his size, he can become over excited and mouthy which can lead to frustration. For this reason he is being trained to wear a muzzle when socialising. He cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. With patience and guidance, we think he will adapt well and enjoy all the comforts a home has to offer.

Dutch can already walk well on a lead, though he can be a little reactive when passing other kennels, this is understandable in a busy rescue environment, but may be something his adopters will need to work with him on. He is an energetic and incredibly lovely bo who ie is happy-go-lucky in nature and is more than ready to start adventuring with his new adopters. He would love an active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, and quality time with his people.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle and quiet introduction to the home, along with his own space to settle in.

He is a bright, affectionate, and fun-loving boy who is sure to make a wonderful and loyal companion for a lucky family.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

name: Audrey
description:
Audrey is a one-year-old female Labrador x Pointer Mix.

There was a moment in her life when the world showed her its harshest side. Left by the road with her siblings, Audrey was only a tiny puppy, surviving on scraps and learning far too early what it feels like to be unwanted.

She grew into a beautiful, gentle girl with a quiet kind of presence. The kind of beauty that does not ask to be noticed. The kind that reveals itself slowly, like a flower opening when it finally feels the warmth of the sun.

Audrey carries a softness that cannot be taught. A gentleness that survived everything life placed in front of her.

When she first meets you, she may watch from a small distance.

Her eyes will follow you carefully, trying to understand who you are and whether she can let herself feel safe.

And then, little by little, she begins to come closer.

A small step. A gentle wag of her tail. A softness in her eyes that was not there before. And suddenly, you realise she is beginning to trust you. With Audrey, trust is never something ordinary.

AUDREY AT A GLANCE:1 year oldMedium-sized Lab mix × English PointerGets along beautifully with other dogsGentle, calm and lovingA little shy at first, but incredibly soft once she feels safe

HEALTH:Fully vaccinatedSpayed4D testedBrucellosis testedMicrochippedFull RBU

Audrey is not the loudest girl in the room. She will not push herself forward or demand to be chosen.But the love she carries is deep, loyal and incredibly pure.

She needs someone who understands that the most beautiful bonds are sometimes the ones that are given time. Someone patient.

Someone kind. Someone who will let her discover, at her own pace, that she is finally home.

And when Audrey truly feels safe, we know she will give everything she has been quietly holding inside.

Her trust. Her loyalty. Her whole heart. She is a quiet soul. A gentle girl. A beautiful life waiting for the person who will help her bloom.

If something in Audrey touches your heart, please send us a message.

She is waiting for someone who will see past that first shy moment and recognise the love already waiting underneath. We would love to hear from you.

name: Orchid
description:
ORCHID – THE KIND OF LOVE THAT CHANGES A HOME!

Orchid is a one-year-old female cross breed.

She saw us… and she chose us. Inside a kill shelter, surrounded by fear, noise, and dogs slowly giving up, Orchid stepped forward with everything she had — hope, trust, and a quiet plea to be taken out of that life.

We took her. And she never looked back. From that day on, she has lived every moment as if it matters — with joy, with softness, and a kind of gratitude you can feel just by being near her.

Orchid is a gorgeous, middle-to-small sized girl, around a year old, and she carries something incredibly rare — a heart that stays open, no matter what she has been through. She is also absolutely beautiful.

Orchid is happiness you can touch. With dogs, she blends in effortlessly — playful, social, kind. With people, she becomes soft and affectionate, always close, always connected.

With children, she is pure gentleness — patient, careful, and full of love. She brings light into a space without trying. She settles into your life as if she has always been part of it.

There is no heaviness in her. Only warmth, softness, and that quiet joy that stays. Orchid is the kind of companion who doesn’t just live beside you — she becomes part of your everyday rhythm, your calm, your happiness.

A small dog with a huge heart. A soul that chose life… and never stopped being grateful for it.

ORCHID AT A GLANCE:Around 1 year oldMiddle-small sized mixed breedGets along beautifully with all dogs & cat-friendlyGentle, cuddly, joyful, full of warmthEasy-going, people-oriented, naturally well-behaved

HEALTH:Fully VaccinatedNeutering to be arranged4D TestedBrucellosis TestedMicrochippedFull RBU

If you are ready for a dog who will fill your home with warmth, closeness, and gentle joy — Orchid is waiting for you.

name: Remi
description:
REMI — THE KIND OF DOG WHO MAKES A HOUSE FEEL LIKE HOME

Remi is the kind of dog whose gentleness reaches you before anything else.

Before you notice how breathtakingly beautiful he is.

Before you notice his elegant Pointer features or his gorgeous silky coat.

The quiet warmth he carries wherever he goes.

Remi is three years old, and he is truly everything a family could hope for in a dog.

He is affectionate, beautifully mannered and wonderfully easy-going. He gets along perfectly with other dogs and has such a peaceful, balanced nature.

A softness that makes being around him feel easy.

He does not need to be loud to fill a space.

Remi is the kind of companion who would bring calm into a home, tenderness into ordinary days and the steady love only a truly good dog can give.

He is beautiful to look at, but it is his nature that stays with you.

Ready to become the dog someone will look at every day and wonder how they were ever lucky enough to find him.

Because Remi is not simply a perfect dog on paper.

He is the kind of dog who could make a home feel warmer just by being part of it.

3 years oldMedium-large, full-breed English PointerGets along beautifully with dogsCalm, gentle, affectionate and quietly joyfulWell-mannered, easy-going and a peaceful companion

Fully vaccinatedNeutered4D testedBrucellosis tested

name: Maddie
description:
MADDIE — EVERYTHING A FAMILY COULD HOPE FOR!

The hardest thing about Maddie is knowing that a dog this beautiful inside is still waiting for someone to see her.

And she already carries the kind of nature that people spend years hoping to find in a dog.

Maddie is gentle in a way that reaches straight into your heart.

She is quiet, affectionate and soft in everything she does. She is simply a kind girl who makes being beside her feel peaceful.

And she is incredibly gentle and friendly with children.

Maddie has so much to offer a family, yet she asks for nothing more than the chance to belong to one.

A whole lifetime of loyalty, affection and companionship waiting to be given.

And somewhere, there must be a person or family whose life is missing exactly what Maddie carries.

1-year-old femaleSmall-to-medium-sized Lab mixWonderful with other dogsCat friendlyVery child-friendlyGentle, calm, affectionate and incredibly kindLead trained

Fully vaccinatedSpayed4D testedBrucellosis tested

Please do not let this beautiful girl grow up without ever knowing what it feels like to be someone’s whole world.

name: Sailor
description:
SAILOR — READY TO BECOME SOMEONE’S WHOLE WORLD

Sailor is a three-year-old Lagotto mix male.

Sailor has the kind of face that stays with you.

That handsome Lagotto look that makes you stop for a moment longer every time you see him.

But Sailor is more than just a beautiful dog.

He is a wonderful three-year-old boy, full of life, love and possibility, ready to become part of someone’s world.

Beautiful, proud and incredibly handsome, with a softness about him that makes you want to reach and touch those soft curls.

Sailor is good with other dogs and enjoys canine company. He could happily share his life with a compatible dog, or finally have all the love of a family to himself.

Young enough to have years of adventures ahead of him.

Ready for long walks, new places, familiar voices and the comfort of knowing exactly where he belongs.

Sailor deserves to be more than a beautiful face people pause to admire.

He deserves to have someone learn every expression in those eyes.

To become the dog whose presence is deeply woven into a home that life without him becomes impossible to imagine.

There is an entire lifetime inside this boy.

Years of love waiting to become part of someone’s story.

Ready for someone to look at him and see their boy.

3 years oldHandsome Lagotto mixGood with other dogsLoving, beautiful and ready for family lifeStrong, striking and full of possibilityLooking for a cat-free home

Fully vaccinatedNeutered4D testedBrucellosis tested

name: Splash
description:
Splash came into our care as a stray and was never claimed by an owner. He has struggled with kennel life and just wants a human to love.

Possibly from a working background, Splash’s prey drive is very high, and he is kept on lead and muzzled when walked but loves sprinting around in a secure field.

Splash does find a lot of things overwhelming and is looking for a calm and relaxed approach to life but with lots of fun and delicious treats at home.

Splash is very smart and does get quite excited when meeting new people. He is best suited with living teenagers and as the only animal.

He has however been walked with other sighthounds but does get over the top.

name: Pirelli
description:
Pirelli is a 2 year old male medium Lurcher.

Pirelli came into our care as a stray and was never claimed by an owner. We believe he may have been used for working as he has a high prey drive and loves playing with squeaky toys.

He is one of our longest dogs on site and although he has walked with a couple of other sighthounds, he would love to be the only animal in his new home.

He does enjoy company of older children but can jump quite high and is very leggy so would best suit a home with teenagers.

A lover of all people and very inquisitive, Pirelli is fantastic at meeting and greeting and loves to run around off lead in a secure field. He is muzzled and kept on lead when out on walks due to his prey drive.

name: Jack
description:
Meet Jack, a 6 month old male Cross-Breed expected to grow into a medium-sized dog of about 30 kilograms. He is currently being fostered in Bulgaria and will be ready to travel once his forever family is found.

Jack’s beginning was far from easy. He and his four siblings were found on the streets alongside their young mother, Lisa — barely alive, exhausted, and trying to keep her newborn puppies safe.

It’s a miracle they survived at all. Thanks to love, care, and patience, this little family recovered, and Jack is now a healthy, happy, and curious young boy.

Still a little timid around new people and situations, Jack has shown what a smart and sensitive soul he truly is. Once he feels safe, his affectionate and playful nature shines through.

He enjoys the company of other dogs, is gentle with children, and is perfectly fine around cats.

Jack loves exploring, learning new things, and being part of family life. Good on a lead, still working on hygiene habits.

He will thrive in a calm, loving home — ideally with people who have some experience with young dogs and understand that rescue dogs need time to adjust.

With patience and care, Jack will become an incredibly loyal and devoted companion.

Fully vaccinatedMicrochippedNot neutered (too young)Vet checked and tested negative for BrucellosisGood with dogs, cats, and childrenReady to travel with full DEFRA-approved paperwork and EU pet passport

Jack may have had a difficult start, but he’s ready to build a new, brighter future — full of love, safety, and adventure. Could you be the one to give this sweet boy his forever home?

name: Chiara
description:
Chiara is a 2.5 year old female Cross-Breed currently under the care of Network for Animals – Azil Danica in Bosnia. She was heartbreakingly dumped as a puppy outside the shelter with her siblings back in November 2023.

Sadly, due to a lack of promotion, she never got the chance to be adopted — but now it’s her time to shine and finally find her forever home.

Chiara weighs around 15 kilograms, making her a perfectly medium-sized girl. She’s friendly, eager to please, and walks well on the lead.

She currently shares her kennel space with three other dogs and gets along wonderfully with them. She also ignores cats, making her a great fit for multi-pet homes.

Chiara is vaccinated, blood tested, flea and worm treated, microchipped, and spayed. She’s a happy, loving girl who’s ready to start her next chapter — one filled with warmth, care, and the family she’s always deserved.

Rescue support and backup by Meadow of Hope Dog Rescue.

name: Jasper
description:
Meet Jasper, a 5 year old male Pointer Cross currently in the UK, looking for a calm, loving forever home through no fault of his own.

This gorgeous, gentle boy is the definition of loyal — a true “Velcro dog” who forms incredibly strong bonds, especially with the women in his life.

Jasper has been a cherished companion for over four years, and now he’s ready to start a new, peaceful chapter where he can finally relax and feel safe.

Sensitive and affectionate, Jasper thrives in a stable, quiet environment.

He’s fully house-trained, wonderful with other dogs (he’s even a regular at doggy daycare), and walks nicely on the lead — though that Pointer nose sometimes leads him on a mission after squirrels!

He’s the perfect companion for someone who wants a devoted, loving dog always by their side.

Jasper does have some separation anxiety, so he’ll need someone patient who can work with him gently and help him feel secure when left alone.

He’s best suited to an adult-only household or one with older, considerate children who understand a dog’s need for space.

Jasper has a history of Leishmaniasis, but don’t let that put you off — he’s in remission, off medication, and in good health. His most recent blood test in August 2025 confirmed that he’s doing brilliantly.

Even better, Pointer Rescue will cover the cost of any future Leishmaniasis medication for his lifetime if ever needed.

If you’re looking for a devoted best friend who will reward your love a thousand times over, Jasper is your boy. Let’s find this gentle soul the peaceful life he’s dreaming of.

name: Valentin
description:
Meet Valentin, a 1.5 year old male Hound Cross weighing 25 kilograms. He’s a beautiful young hound who has already been through so much in his short life.

Valentin came from a pound in northern Spain, where he was sadly stuck for six months before being rescued. Like many hounds in the region, he was likely a discarded hunting dog, but despite his past, he has kept his gentle spirit.

This lovely boy is in excellent health – he has been fully blood tested (including brucellosis), neutered, microchipped, and has his passport ready for travel.

Valentin gets along wonderfully with other dogs and would thrive in a home with canine companions. He can be a little timid when first meeting new people, but he warms up with patience and kindness and is incredibly loyal once he trusts you.

Valentin is ready to start the next chapter of his life – and he can travel! He is ready to travel, making it easier than ever to welcome him into your family.

As with all of our dogs, he comes with full rescue back-up for life.

name: Paddy
description:
Paddy is an 8-month-old male Cross-Breed. He’s one of Bea’s five adorable puppies and has already shown himself to be a gentle and sweet-natured boy.

Despite being a little hand-shy, Paddy’s personality shines through—he just needs some time, patience, and love to help his confidence blossom.

Like many pups, Paddy is still learning about the world around him. His gentle temperament suggests he’ll grow into a loyal and affectionate companion once he settles into a secure and loving home.

He’s expected to be medium-sized when fully grown, making him the perfect balance between playful energy and easy manageability.

Currently, Paddy is in Romania, waiting eagerly for his chance to travel to the UK. With winter quickly approaching, rescuers are hoping to find him a home before the cold truly sets in.

Paddy has been fully vaccinated and blood tested, so he’s ready for his next big adventure—a forever home of his own.

Pennypaws Rescue will provide full rescue back-up and ongoing support to make sure Paddy and his future family have everything they need for a smooth transition.

A video homecheck will be required, ensuring that Paddy finds a safe, warm place where he can grow up feeling loved and secure.

name: Tosja
description:
Meet Tosja, a large gentle giant standing about 65 to 70 cm tall. She is a 4 to 5 year old female Shepherd Cross, underweight but still beautiful and strong—especially strong in her kindness, gentleness, and positivity.

She surely didn’t have an easy life. She’s so sunny, docile, confident, and affectionate—a true joy to be around. One of the most wonderful dogs in the public shelter in Romania, she is confined to a small space and only gets out for photos.

She’s amazing: balanced, loving, and playful without being pushy or annoying. Affectionate and loyal, she’s a treasure in an extra-large package with the sweetest gentle personality.

She loves every dog and person she meets. She is not cat tested, so that remains uncertain. Tosja is vaccinated and will be blood tested, including for Brucellosis, with the test sent to the UK prior to travelling.

She is neutered. From next year, dogs with cut tails and ears will not be able to travel to the UK because of new regulations coming into force. Please give her a chance—Tosja needs to travel this year.

Consider this beautiful girl; she will bring so much joy and be a wonderful companion. No small children because of her size—only someone with plenty of time and a loving home.

Adoption fee £450. Home check requested. Rescue back-up provided.

name: Bonny
description:
Welcome Bonny, one half of a brave sisterhood.

Bonny is a 10 month old female Cross-Breed, affectionate and friendly, who loves people just as much as she loves other dogs.

She and her sister Ivy were found abandoned in the middle of nowhere — two young souls lost in the fields, wandering under the burning sun with no food, no water, and no one to protect them.

They only had each other. Side by side, they faced the hardest days, finding strength in their bond and refusing to give up.

Now both girls are safe — and for the first time, they’re learning what love and care truly mean.

Bonny still looks for comfort in closeness — leaning into a kind hand or gently pressing against another dog for reassurance.

At around 10 months old, Bonny is still full of life and curiosity. She’s ready for long walks, playful moments, and quiet evenings beside someone who will finally call her their own.

Though she and Ivy shared their toughest chapter together, now it’s time for each of them to find their own forever home — a place where they’ll be loved, safe, and never alone again.

Bonny will come with a full adoption package including:

If you’ve ever wanted to open your heart to a dog who’s already proven how deeply she can love — Bonny is waiting. She survived because of love… and now she’s ready to live for it.

name: Ivy
description:
Meet Ivy, a 10 month old female Hunting Cross of medium size. She’s a playful, affectionate, and loving young girl who never lost her faith in people.

Ivy was found abandoned in a lonely field with her sister Bonny, wandering for days under the hot sun without food or water. Against all odds, she survived — and through it all, she kept her gentle, trusting nature.

Ivy is very people-oriented and adores human companionship. She’s wonderful with other dogs, greeting them with a wagging tail and plenty of puppy affection.

Despite her tough start, Ivy’s spirit shines with warmth and joy. She’s ready to leave her past behind and begin a new chapter filled with safety, comfort, and love.

Ivy will come with a full adoption package, including vaccinations, microchip, blood tests, neutering, and full rescue back-up. A home check applies.

If you’re looking for a kind-hearted, loyal companion who will brighten every single day, Ivy is waiting to meet you.

name: Conor
description:
Conor is a 3-year-old male Beagle cross Hound. This gorgeous boy weighs around 25kg and has a gentle, soulful expression that perfectly matches his kind nature.

Conor’s story started out rough — he was found wandering the streets before being taken to a pound in Galicia, Northern Spain. Sadly, he spent nearly 12 months in one of the toughest pounds in the country.

Despite that, his spirit remained unbroken, and now he’s safe in residence near Lugo, finally getting the care and kindness he deserves.

He’s a handsome hound mix who’s healthy, active, and ready for a new start. Conor is friendly with people, though a little shy when meeting new faces.

Once he feels safe, he quickly warms up and shows his affectionate, relaxed side. He’s wonderful with other dogs, enjoying playtime and socialising, and he’s been cat tested — with great results. This shows what a gentle and adaptable dog he truly is.

Conor loves being outdoors, whether he’s exploring on walks or simply enjoying fresh air in a secure garden. A secure space is essential for his safety and comfort as he continues adjusting to home life.

He’s fully neutered, vaccinated (including rabies), microchipped, and has had comprehensive blood tests for Mediterranean diseases and brucellosis.

Conor also comes with a passport and full rescue backup. Transport can be arranged anywhere in the UK, so this sweet boy can start his next chapter wherever his perfect family may be.

name: Abbie
description:
Abbie, a 3-year-old female cross-breed dog, hails from Romania, having been rescued from the Lancram shelter.

Despite her challenging beginnings, Abbie now resides in a private foster home, eagerly awaiting the opportunity to join a loving family. This small-sized cross breed, standing at 40cm in height, is adored for her sweet and kind nature.

Known for her infectious smile and enthusiastically wagging tail, Abbie thrives on human interaction and affection.

Abbie has been described as lead trained and exhibits no known allergies or intolerances. Despite her underbite, which does not cause her discomfort, she maintains a healthy appetite and enjoys normal eating and drinking habits.

Regular dental care is recommended to ensure her oral hygiene remains in good condition. Remarkably, Abbie shares her foster home with a cat and has shown no inclination towards chasing or bothering her feline companion, demonstrating her peaceful nature and adaptability.

For those interested in adopting Abbie, applications and checks are facilitated through Meadow Of Hope Dog Rescue UK.

With her endearing personality and gentle demeanour, Abbie promises to bring joy and companionship to her future forever family.

name: Monty
description:
Meet Monty, a 4 year old male Sighthound who is outstanding and extremely friendly!

Monty has experienced unimaginable suffering but still forgives so much. He is looking for a wonderful and loving home.

Monty was saved from a private shelter where he received no medical treatment and little food.

It was discovered that Monty had suffered blunt trauma to his eye. Now residing in a private shelter run by a local vet in Romania, Monty is ready to find his forever home.

Monty is human-orientated, loves people, and craves human touch and contact.

He is active, playful, and a pure delight to be around. Monty shows no fear of veterinary procedures and has displayed no aggression toward carers, vets, or visitors. He is absolutely desperate for love.

Monty can live with older dog-savvy children and needs an experienced dog owner.

He requires a secure garden with 6ft fencing for play and training. A home without cats or small furries is preferable, as Monty will chase them.

Monty has been thoroughly vet-checked, and while he has a non-functional left eye, it does not cause him pain. There is a potential risk of future complications, but surgery is not recommended at this time.

Anyone who opens up their home to Monty will be truly blessed. He is a beautiful and kind-natured dog who will settle easily into a home environment.

name: Virgie
description:
Meet Virgie, a 4.5 month old female Cross-Breed who is inquisitive and intelligent!

Virgie has lots to learn and is eager to explore the world. She is looking for a wonderful rescue-experienced home that will support her training in a positive manner.

Virgie will need help transitioning into a home environment and with lead work, as she currently lives in a shelter and doesn’t yet understand toilet training.

A committed home, focused on her ongoing training, is essential.

Virgie arrived at a rescue shelter in Romania after being abandoned in a plastic bag with her siblings.

She is very lovely, human-focused, and good with other dogs in the shelter. She loves to sniff and play in the shelter playground.

She is suited for a home with older dog-savvy children aged 12+ and needs a secure garden for play and continued training.

A home without cats or small animals is preferable, as she isn’t used to them. Positive reinforcement in her new home will be important for her development.

Virgie is healthy, with clear blood tests, and is vaccinated, flea and worm treated, and microchipped.

name: Chance
description:
Chance is an 8 year old male Cross-Breed, currently residing in Romania and looking for a home. He is 30kg in weight and 65cm in height.

Chance was rescued from the Breasta public shelter in Romania, where he was at risk of euthanasia.

He travelled to a safe shelter but, due to the ill health of the foster, he recently moved to another safe shelter. Despite this, Chance is a friendly and social dog.

Chance likes to go out into the shelter playground with his shelter buddies. He is affectionate with those caring for him and isn’t afraid of being handled or stroked.

Chance is looking for a dog-experienced home who are knowledgeable in caring for a dog with past trauma.

He would like a secure garden and would not be suited to a home with cats or small furries. A patient home to help him settle after a long journey would be ideal.

Health-wise, Chance is healthy with no allergies or intolerances and doesn’t take any regular medication. He is fully vaccinated and neutered.

RBU – Meadow Of Hope Dog Rescue UK application and checks apply.

name: Bonnie
description:
Bonnie is a lively 5-month-old female cross-breed, born in January 2024, who finds herself in need of a loving home after being abandoned in Romania alongside her two siblings.

Currently under the care of the NGO rescuer Andreea, Bonnie is fortunate to be in a private foster home.

She embodies the spirit of puppyhood, displaying a playful and cheerful demeanor, often seen frolicking outdoors with her siblings, her joy evident in her fondness for chasing tennis balls.

Bonnie has been meticulously cared for; she’s received vaccinations, undergone blood tests, and has been treated for fleas and worms.

Additionally, she’s been microchipped, though she has not yet been spayed due to her young age. With no known allergies or intolerances, Bonnie requires no regular medication.

However, she will thrive in a home that can provide dedicated support for her training, including house training and ongoing socialization.

Given her playful nature, a secure garden is a must for her safety and enjoyment.

Those interested in offering Bonnie a forever home can reach out to Rbu – Meadow Of Hope Dog Rescue UK.

name: Zeus
description:
Zeus is a 4-year-old male Cross-Breed. He stands 55 cm tall, weighs 27 kg, and has been neutered. Once a lost soul wandering along a busy road, Zeus was tired and alone but never fully gave up hope.

His journey was long and uncertain, but today, he is safe in a shelter, patiently waiting for someone to give him the love he truly deserves.

Zeus is cheerful and full of life. He loves going on long walks and sees the leash as a symbol of freedom. Playful and affectionate, he thrives on human companionship and enjoys spending time with people.

He is social with other dogs, especially females and some males, and balances his playful nature with quiet moments of calm.

With no signs of aggression in him, Zeus is a gentle dog with a huge, loving heart. He is the kind of companion who will sit quietly by your side, offering silent comfort and loyalty.

His only wish is to find a real home—a place where he is not just safe, but also truly loved and seen.

Zeus is more than just a shelter dog. He is a true friend, a loyal companion, and a joyful presence who has so much to give to the right person.

name: Spirit
description:
Hello there! My name is Spirit, a 3 year old male Cross-Breed from Romania.

I was rescued from a field where I was attached to a chain 24 hours a day. My fur was matted, my skin was sore and I was crawling with fleas; it was so uncomfortable for me.

Despite those awful days, weeks and years of my life, I remain forgiving and happy.

I’m super friendly with people, other dogs and children over 10.

I love to play, run around and roll in the long grass now that I am free from those horrible chains.

I currently reside in private foster in Romania under the care of NGO Andreea.

I am super excited for what the future holds for me and what adventures can be made now that I have a new lease of life.

Allergies or health conditions – None present

name: Amos
description:
Amos is a 7-year-old male Mioritic Shepherd. He has spent an incredibly long 4 years in a private shelter in Romania and is now ready to find a loving forever home. Amos is a large dog, standing at 62cm tall and weighing around 32kg, with a big, fluffy coat that reflects his gentle nature.

Amos is very friendly with other dogs and currently lives peacefully in a kennel alongside two female dogs and one male dog. His temperament is loving and affectionate once he feels comfortable, though he may be a little shy at first. Patience and understanding will help him build trust as he adjusts to a new environment.

Having spent most of his life in a shelter, Amos is unfamiliar with life in a home. As such, he will need time to adapt, along with guidance and encouragement to learn household routines and boundaries. He enjoys being outside and would thrive in a home with a garden, where he can safely explore and enjoy some freedom.

Amos is fully vaccinated, blood tested, microchipped, neutered, and tested negative for brucellosis. He has no known allergies or medical needs. He is looking for a home with someone who has experience with Mioritic Shepherds or similar guardian breeds, as they can have unique traits that benefit from knowledgeable handling.

While Amos is still getting used to walking on a lead and harness, he shows enthusiasm for exploring outside. He may have selective hearing at times, especially when excited to be out of his kennel, so consistency and calm training will be important in helping him settle into home life.

Amos has waited long enough and truly deserves a chance to experience love, comfort, and stability in a home of his own.

name: Sadie
description:
Sadie is a 6-7 year old female Boxer Cross. She is very loving, friendly, and playful. She loves running through fields and playing in streams. She also loves to play with other dogs.

Sadie can be strong on the lead, especially if she sees another dog so does need someone strong enough to hold her.

Sadie has lived both as an only dog and as part of a pack. She cannot be homed with cats and any resident children need to be dog respectful 12+.

name: Albie
description:
Albie is a 5 year old male Cross-Breed. He was adopted through us several years ago but his family have had a baby and Albie isn’t coping.

Albie has moved out to a relative’s home but this is only a temporary solution and he needs to find a new home as soon as possible.

Albie is a very sweet, loving boy who just needs an adult-only home where someone is around a lot of the day (although is fine to be left for a few hours).

Albie has a secure garden and places nearby where he can be walked without too many dogs in his face as he is a little lead reactive (this can improve with positive reinforcement and time).

Albie is a nice boy who is at that great age with lots of life left, energy enough for long walks but able to relax when at home.

name: Flora
description:
Flora is a mature mioritic, born approximately in 2016, and she is a female residing in Romania. She is associated with the Meadow Of Hope Dog Rescue UK and has received vaccinations such as Dhppirl and Nobivac KC.

Flora has undergone thorough blood tests, including screening for brucellosis, and has been diligently treated for fleas and worms. Additionally, she is microchipped and spayed under the care of veterinary professionals.

Beneath her outer layer, Flora possesses a charming spirit that longs to gain the trust of others. The belief is that she will flourish in a home with the correct and knowledgeable environment.

Much like a lovely flower, Flora requires time to blossom, and she is undeniably putting in the effort to do so.

Flora, along with her brother, was rescued from the Breasta public shelter in Romania. Their initial ordeal involved huddling together in a kennel corner for comfort, possibly reflecting the trauma of running for their lives.

Fortunately, they found refuge in a private shelter, though Flora’s brother sadly succumbed to natural causes shortly after their arrival.

Currently cohabiting with other dogs, Flora exhibits amicable relations with her fellow canines. While she remains a bit reserved with people, her progress in the private shelter has been notable.

The ideal home for Flora is one that patiently nurtures bonds with her, avoiding situations that may induce discomfort. Adaptation to leash walking is also a gradual process for Flora, as she hasn’t experienced it yet.

A breed-specific residence with ample free space is deemed suitable for her.

Despite her initial reservations, Flora’s true joy shines through when she feels at ease. Described as large, energetic, and fun, she awaits a compassionate individual who can offer her the home and understanding she requires.

If you believe you could be the person to provide Flora with the right environment, the adoption process involves an application and necessary checks. We look forward to hearing from potential adopters who can provide Flora with the loving home she deserves.

name: Marta
description:
Marta, a delightful 1-year-old female Cross-Breed, is eagerly awaiting her forever family through Meadow Of Hope Dog Rescue UK.

Despite her challenging beginnings—being discovered abandoned with her siblings, malnourished and frightened—Marta has blossomed into a confident and loving companion.

She’s an absolute snugglebug, finding comfort in being by your side or nestled on your lap. Marta’s affection knows no bounds; she showers love and warmth upon anyone willing to reciprocate.

Her resilient spirit and unwavering love for everyone and everything showcase her remarkable character. Marta dreams of a family with children to cuddle and play with, providing her with the love and security she craves.

This sweet girl embodies gentleness and playfulness, making her an ideal addition to any household. She’s good-natured, easygoing, and eager to please, displaying a genuine desire for affection and companionship.

Marta’s suitability with children, cats, and dogs further underscores her adaptable and sociable nature. Currently residing in Bosnia, Marta awaits her chance to find a loving home.

Prospective adopters will need to undergo an application process and checks through Meadow Of Hope Dog Rescue UK.

Additionally, it’s important to note that Bosnian dogs, like Marta, must undergo a 48-hour quarantine in UK kennels upon arrival before traveling home.

name: Bianka
description:
Bianka, a delightful female cross breed dog of approximately 1 year old, is eagerly seeking her forever home.

This medium-sized sweetheart, currently located in Bosnia, has a charming and playful nature that captures the hearts of everyone she meets.

Bianka’s playful spirit ensures she’s always in the midst of any fun happening at the shelter, enthusiastically engaging with her friends and toys alike.

Although initially shy around strangers, Bianka transforms into a confident and affectionate companion once she’s out of her kennel.

She thrives in the company of other dogs and children, showcasing her adaptability and gentle nature.

Bianka’s potential shines brightest in a loving home environment, where she can continue to blossom with the support of another dog and ongoing training to build her confidence.

Fully vaccinated, blood tested, flea and worm treated, spayed, and microchipped, Bianka is ready to embark on her new life journey.

If you’re ready to provide Bianka with the loving and nurturing home she deserves, please consider submitting an application through Rbu – Meadow Of Hope Dog Rescue UK.

Application and checks are part of the adoption process to ensure Bianka finds the perfect match.

name: Snoopy
description:
Snoopy, a charming male Hound Cross puppy of just 3 months old, is eagerly seeking a loving family to call his own.

This medium-sized Hound cross was found abandoned in the bushes and brought to the shelter, but despite his rocky start, Snoopy’s happy-go-lucky nature shines through.

Lonely in the shelter, Snoopy longs for companionship and a warm home environment where he can thrive.

Despite his young age, Snoopy exudes confidence and affection.

He adores playtime, with tug being his favorite game, and he eagerly interacts with other dogs and people alike.

Snoopy’s loving nature extends to children, and he is currently working on being calm around them. As he is still in the early stages of his life, Snoopy is open to being socialized with cats at the shelter.

Snoopy’s delightful personality makes him an ideal addition to any loving home. He is vaccinated, blood tested, flea and worm treated, and microchipped, with neutering pending due to his age.

Upon arrival in the UK, Snoopy, like other Bosnian dogs, will need to quarantine in UK kennels for 48 hours before joining his new family.

If you’re ready to open your heart and home to Snoopy, please consider submitting an application through Rbu – Meadow Of Hope Dog Rescue UK.

Application and checks are part of the adoption process to ensure Snoopy finds the perfect match.

name: Frodo
description:
Frodo, a male crossbreed dog of approximately 1-2 years old, is eagerly searching for his forever home.

This medium-sized cross breed pup, currently residing in Bosnia, is known for his gentle and placid nature. Despite not being cat-tested, Frodo loves the company of other dogs and is excellent with calm and sensible children.

At the shelter, Frodo is a beloved favorite, often found curled up under the desk in the office, seeking affection from shelter staff. He enjoys strokes, cuddles, and the companionship of both humans and fellow canines.

Although he may initially be nervous, especially since he has spent most of his life in the shelter, Frodo quickly gains confidence with love and attention. Once he forms a bond with you, he becomes your loyal and affectionate best friend.

Frodo is described as affectionate, loyal, and eager to please. He is making great progress with his training and is keen to learn and adapt to his new environment.

Fully vaccinated, blood tested, flea and worm treated, neutered, and microchipped, Frodo is ready to embark on his new life adventure.

Upon arrival in the UK, Frodo, like other Bosnian dogs, will need to quarantine in UK kennels for 48 hours before joining his new family.

If you’re interested in giving Frodo the loving home he deserves, please consider submitting an application through Rbu – Meadow Of Hope Dog Rescue UK.

Application and checks are part of the adoption process to ensure Frodo finds the perfect match.

name: Medena
description:
Medena, a stunning female dog, is looking for her forever home. Estimated to be around 1-2 years old, Medena is of medium size and boasts a cross breed heritage.

Her current residence is in Bosnia, but she dreams of finding a loving family to explore the world with. Despite her beauty, Medena’s exuberant personality makes her better suited to homes with children aged 13 and above, and she has not been tested with cats.

At the shelter, Medena stands out as one of the most beautiful dogs, and she certainly knows it! She thrives on attention and is at her happiest when she’s out of her kennel, whether it’s for a walk or playtime.

With her intelligence and quick learning ability, Medena is eager to please and would benefit from continued training in a loving home environment.

Medena’s ideal home would provide her with the guidance of a confident older dog and owners committed to continuing her training.

Managing her arousal levels and ensuring she receives plenty of exercise and mental stimulation are crucial for her well-being. Vaccinated, blood tested, flea and worm treated, microchipped, and spayed, Medena is ready to embark on her new life adventure.

Upon arrival in the UK, Medena, like other Bosnian dogs, will need to quarantine in UK kennels for 48 hours before joining her new family.

If you believe you can offer Medena the loving and supportive home she deserves, please consider submitting an application through Rbu – Meadow Of Hope Dog Rescue UK.

Application and checks are necessary steps in the adoption process to ensure Medena finds the perfect match.

name: Bleki
description:
Introducing Bleki, a delightful female dog awaiting her forever home.

At 2 years old, Bleki is a beautiful Lab/Hound cross currently residing in Bosnia. Despite her past, Bleki is in excellent health and has been fully vaccinated, blood tested, flea and worm treated, microchipped, and spayed.

Bleki’s loving personality has won over the hearts of everyone at the shelter where she resides. Known for her easygoing nature and calm demeanor, Bleki serves as a positive influence on her more energetic companions.

She exudes confidence and affection, readily seeking out cuddles and enjoying being groomed and stroked.

Bleki is well-behaved on the lead and thoroughly enjoys her walks, where she can indulge in the joy of exploration. She gets along well with other dogs and is good with children.

However, she has not been tested with cats. Bleki’s ideal home would provide her with plenty of love, attention, and opportunities for outdoor adventures.

Please note that upon arrival in the UK, Bosnian dogs such as Bleki are required to quarantine in UK kennels for 48 hours before being able to join their new families.

If you’re interested in providing Bleki with the loving home she deserves, please submit an application through Rbu- Meadow Of Hope Dog Rescue UK. Application and checks are part of the adoption process to ensure Bleki finds the perfect match.

name: Julie
description:
Julie is a 1 year old female Cross-Breed, medium/small in size, currently located in Romania.

She was abandoned in a cardboard box along with 4 newborns on the sidewalk of a road in the town of Tecuci in Romania on 25/05/2024.

A lady asked for help with them, and although we already have a lot of animals in care, we couldn’t bear to leave them there.

Julie is a perfect mother, caring and affectionate. She has a very gentle, kind, and submissive character; she likes to be cuddled and petted.

She can live, after a gradual introduction, with other dogs and children aged 10+. Unfortunately, there is not enough information about how she interacts with cats.

Adopting a dog is a very big decision, so please make sure you are ready for the challenge and commitment.

Are you ready to take care of her? Pay her vet bills? Feed her? Walk her? Consider her a family member for the rest of her life?

If so, we’d love to hear from you! RBU – Meadow Of Hope Dog Rescue UK.

name: Lola
description:
Meet Lola, a bundle of squishy love at approximately 7 months old, captured in all her playful glory in the picture below. Lola is a loving, active, and spirited pup who delights in running, jumping, and playing throughout the day.

Her exuberance is contagious, but it’s important to note that Lola can get quite excited and jump up, making her more suitable for a home without small children.

In search of an experienced and active home, Lola thrives on interaction and companionship, preferring not to be left alone for extended periods.

Having been abandoned by her sisters when she was tiny, Lola has yet to experience life in a house, making her journey to a forever home a special one that requires patience and positive guidance.
